### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2025.09.0+387
    OS Version      : macOS 26.0 (also one person reporting this on Ubuntu, no other details)
    R Version       : 4.5.1
    Quarto Version  : 1.8.24

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Not using the bundled copy of Quarto (1.7.32) but a separately installed copy (1.8.24).

- Open a Quarto project in RStudio.
- Open a .qmd file.
- Modify code inside a chunk.
- Observe syntax highlighting disappearing.
- Try running the chunk via the green arrow or Cmd+Shift+Enter. Some chunks do not execute.

### Describe the problem in detail

- **Syntax Highlighting Issue**: When editing .qmd files, syntax highlighting disappears in code chunks after modifying the code. The highlighting is restored only after saving the file.
- **Chunk Execution Issue**: In some .qmd files, the run chunk green arrow disappears. Even when the arrow is visible, clicking it does not execute the chunk. This happens inconsistently across chunks.

### Describe the behavior you expected

- Syntax highlighting should persist while editing code.
- Chunks should execute consistently when triggered.

issue_title: Issues with repository access using latest RStudio version and old(er) R versions
issue_body:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2025.09.0 Build 387
    OS Version      : Windows 10 Enterprise 22H2
    R Version       : 4.1.2 (x64)

----------

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Launch an RStudio (2025.09.0 Build 387) session running R 4.1.2 (x64)
2. Try to check for packages available in https://cran.rstudio.com
```R
PKGS <- available.packages(repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com")
nrow(PKGS)
```

----------

### Describe the problem in detail

The first statement returns the following warning:
```R
Warning: unable to access index for repository https://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib:
  cannot open URL 'https://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib/PACKAGES'
```
whereas the second returns `0`, indicating no available packages were found, likely because, as mentioned in the warning, the repository could not be accessed.

----------

### Describe the behavior you expected

I expected no warnings from the first statement, and for the second to return the actual number of packages currently available in https://cran.rstudio.com.

The same two statements work when running the same R 4.1.2 (x64) installation via the R GUI, which results in no warnings from the first one and `21971` returned by the second.

They also work when using the same RStudio installation (2025.09.0 Build 387) but in a session running R 4.4.3 (x64) instead of 4.1.2, again yielding no warnings from the first statement and with the second returning `22751`.

Finally, they also work when running R 4.1.2 (x64) using an older RStudio version (2024.04.2 Build 764), with results fully consistent with those from the R GUI, as one would expect.

<!--

IMPORTANT: Please provide a reproducible example! This can be a snippet of code, or set of actions, that we can use to reproduce the issue you are encountering. issue_title: RStudio 2025.09.0 crashes when running glm() / glm.nb() (R 4.5.1, Windows 10)
issue_body: _The latest patch release of RStudio, 2025.09.1, is now available and has a fix for this issue and is available at https://posit.co/downloads/. Thanks for your patience, and sorry for the trouble!_ -- @kevinushey --- _If you are experiencing crashes when fitting models in your R session, you can work around this crash by disabling automatic updates of the environment pane. Use the small dropdown arrow next to the Refresh button in the Environment pane toolbar, and switch to Manual Refresh Only._ _Alternatively, you can install the previous release of RStudio from https://dailies.rstudio.com/version/2025.05.1+513.pro3/._ _We have test builds available with a candidate fix at https://dailies.rstudio.com/rstudio/cucumberleaf-sunflower/, and will be preparing a patch release including this fix as soon as possible._ _Thanks, and sorry for the trouble._ -- @kevinushey @ Posit --- System Environment: RStudio: 2025.09.0 Build 387 R version: 4.5.1 (2025-06-13 ucrt) Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 OS: Windows 10 (also reproducible on other OS?) Description of the bug: When fitting a generalized linear model with glm() (family = poisson) or glm.nb() (from MASS), the RStudio IDE session crashes immediately. The crash occurs only in RStudio IDE. Running the exact same code in Rterm (console) or R GUI works without any problem. Rolling back to the previous RStudio release (2025.05.0) resolves the issue. This suggests an IDE-specific bug (possibly related to Environment pane preview of model objects). Minimal reproducible example: library(MASS) set.seed(123) testdata <- data.frame( y = rpois(100, lambda = 3), x = rnorm(100) ) # Poisson GLM m1 <- glm(y ~ x, family = poisson, data = testdata) # Negative Binomial GLM m2 <- glm.nb(y ~ x, data = testdata) Observed behavior: As soon as the model is fit (glm or glm.nb), RStudio crashes and the session terminates. Expected behavior: Model should fit normally, as it does in R console or previous RStudio versions. Additional info: Crash seems related to the Environment pane auto-preview of model objects. Disabling Environment auto-refresh may be a temporary workaround. All packages (including MASS) were reinstalled under R 4.5.1.

commit_message:
fix quarto syntax highlight issues (#16469)

* don't delete saved state when exiting quarto highlight

* add automation test

* update NEWS
patch:
--- a/src/cpp/tests/automation/testthat/test-automation-quarto.R
+++ b/src/cpp/tests/automation/testthat/test-automation-quarto.R
@@ -554,3 +554,35 @@ withr::defer(.rs.automation.deleteRemote())
       expect_equal(editor$session$getLine(4), "```{=latex}")
    })
 })
+
+# https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/16463
+.rs.test("empty quarto blocks don't break highlight in chunk", {
+   
+   contents <- .rs.heredoc('
+      ---
+      title: Chunk Syntax Highlighting
+      ---
+      
+      ```{r}
+      #| echo: true
+      2 * 2
+      ```
+   ')
+   
+   remote$editor.executeWithContents(".qmd", contents, function(editor) {
+      
+      editor$gotoLine(6, 13)
+      remote$keyboard.sendKeys("<Enter>")
+      remote$keyboard.sendKeys("<Enter>")
+      Sys.sleep(0.1)
+      tokens <- as.vector(editor$session$getTokens(8))
+
+      expect_equal(tokens[[1L]]$value, "2")
+      expect_equal(tokens[[2L]]$value, " ")
+      expect_equal(tokens[[3L]]$value, "*")
+      expect_equal(tokens[[4L]]$value, " ")
+      expect_equal(tokens[[5L]]$value, "2")
+
+   })
+   
+})

Create a new Quarto Document (html) 2. Press "create" 3. In the first code chunk, add a label (or any options) 4. Press enter twice (I have the "continue comment" option on) 5. The code below becomes unrunnable ### Describe the problem in detail When I open a quarto document (HTML), and if I put in a code chunk option (in this case, label). This issue appears to be specific to RStudio, as I was unable to recreate it in Positron. The problem goes away if I cut and paste the script. It happens when I am typing in the code originally. Not working: After copying and pasting it, the whole thing starts working again: Highlighting and all that go back to normal, and the code chunk can run. ### Describe the behavior you expected I would issue_title: RStudio install.packages() misinterprets binary ZIP file path as package name
issue_body:
Description:
After updating to the latest RStudio build installing a Windows binary package from a local .zip file fails with spurious errors inside RStudio, though the same installation works fine in plain R.

Rstudio build: (RStudio 2025.09.0+387 "Cucumberleaf Sunflower" Release (af5fc22a687c0f462ee27c6afeeee38ee46507b9, 2025-09-11) for windows Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) RStudio/2025.09.0+387 Chrome/138.0.7204.185 Electron/37.2.6 Safari/537.36, Quarto 1.7.32), 

The problem arises I believe because RStudio’s internal function .rs.recordPackageSource() calls utils::packageDescription() using the zip file name (e.g., mypackage_0.2.0.9027.zip) instead of the package name (mypackage). This results in RStudio attempting to open a non-existent DESCRIPTION file inside the zip path, producing misleading warnings and sometimes leaving the package in a broken state.

Steps to Reproduce:

In a fresh RStudio session (R 4.5.1 on Windows 11), run:

zipfile <- "C:/Users/me/Dropbox/CBP/binary/mypackage_0.2.0.9027.zip"
install.packages(zipfile, repos = NULL, type = "win.binary")


Observe that the package unpacks successfully, but then RStudio reports:

Warning: no package 'mypackage_0.2.0.9027.zip' was found
Error in file(con, "r"): cannot open file
  '.../mypackage_0.2.0.9027.zip/DESCRIPTION': No such file or directory


Tracing utils::packageDescription() shows the call stack originates from:

.rs.recordPackageSource(pkgs, local = TRUE)
.rs.recordPackageSourceImpl(pkgPath, db, local)
packageDescription(pkgName, lib.loc = dirname(pkgPath))


where pkgName is incorrectly set to the full zip filename.

Expected Behavior:
RStudio should record the package source using the actual package name (mypackage), not the .zip filename, so that packageDescription() works correctly and no spurious errors are raised.

Actual Behavior:

RStudio misinterprets the .zip path as the package name.

packageDescription() fails, producing confusing warnings.

This behavior does not occur when installing the same package from a local .zip using plain R outside RStudio.

Environment:

R 4.5.1 (Windows 11 x64, UCRT build)

RStudio 2025.01 (current preview/release as of Sept 2025)

Windows 11 Pro (build 26100)

Workarounds Tried:

Installing outside RStudio works.

Installing into a clean library works.

Overriding .rs.recordPackageSource to a no-op also works, confirming the bug source.

Request:
Please adjust .rs.recordPackageSource() so it parses the actual package name from the zip rather than passing the full filename to packageDescription(). This would restore the long-standing behavior where install.packages(<zip>, repos=NULL, type="win.binary") works inside RStudio the same as it does in plain R.

issue_title: R session crashes when assigning the return value of HiResTEC::getMultipleBPC() to a variable
issue_body:
Below issue occurred after upgrading RStudio to the latest version (2025.09). It did not occur in 2025.05 nor does it occur in RGui or Emacs. The issue makes the R session crash/restart. RStudio does not crash.

### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2025.09.0 Build 387
    OS Version      :  Windows 11 x64 (build 26100)
    R Version       : 4.5.1 (2025-06-13 ucrt)

### Steps to reproduce the problem

```R
install.packages("HiResTEC")
library(HiResTEC)
raw <- HiResTEC::raw
mz <- 556.263 + c(0:3) * 1.0034 # precise values do not matter here, they are just the same as in example(getMultipleBPC) 
getMultipleBPC(x = raw[[1]], mz = mz, mz_dev = 0.04, rt = 1026) # works as expected
x <- getMultipleBPC(x = raw[[1]], mz = mz, mz_dev = 0.04, rt = 1026) # R crashes
```

### Describe the problem in detail
Running above example works fine as long as the return value of getMultipleBPC(), a numeric matrix, is written to stdout (lines 1-5). When it is assigned to a variable (line 6) the R session crashes. Using other variable names (e.g., 'y') produces the same result.

### Describe the behavior you expected
A numeric matrix should be assigned to 'x'. The R session should not crash.

issue_body: _The latest patch release of RStudio, 2025.09.1, is now available and has a fix for this issue and is available at https://posit.co/downloads/. Thanks for your patience, and sorry for the trouble!_ -- @kevinushey --- _If you are experiencing crashes when fitting models in your R session, you can work around this crash by disabling automatic updates of the environment pane. issue_title: Bug Report: RStudio Freeze/Crash Caused by Unstable GitHub Copilot Extension
issue_body:
Subject: Bug Report: RStudio Freeze/Crash Caused by Unstable GitHub Copilot Extension

Hello RStudio / GitHub Team,

Hope you're doing well.

I'm experiencing frequent, intermittent freezes and crashes in RStudio Desktop. After a detailed forensic diagnosis, all the evidence points to an instability in the integrated GitHub Copilot extension.

Key Symptoms:
The RStudio rsession.log file consistently shows the following errors in the minutes leading up to a session crash:

ERROR json-parse error

ERROR [onStdout]: Internal error: response contains no Content-Length header.

System Details:

RStudio Version: 2025.05.1+513

Copilot Version: 1.300.0

Operating System: Windows 11 x64 (build 26100)

Diagnostic Steps Taken:
I've been able to confirm the following:

The rsession.log consistently shows the Copilot-specific errors above right before a crash.

The Copilot diagnostic report shows full network reachability (HTTP 200 to all endpoints), which rules out any local firewall, proxy, or connectivity problems.

Based on this evidence, the strong working diagnosis is that the Copilot extension is the cause of the instability. The next confirmatory step is to disable the extension and monitor for long-term stability.

This issue currently impacts the ability to use Copilot while maintaining a reliable IDE, which significantly disrupts workflow.

Thanks for your help in looking into this.

issue_title: Caught errors do not display when using globalCallingHandlers
issue_body:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop
    RStudio Version : 2025.05.0 Build 496
    OS Version      : Windows 11
    R Version       :  4.4.2 and 4.5.0

### Steps to reproduce the problem

The following code comes from testing `globalCallingHandlers` to print caught errors so they can be captured by `sink` for logging. The display that appears in the RStudio console is significantly different from the output that is sunk to file.

```r
## create global calling handlers ----------------------------------------- ----

globalCallingHandlers(
  error = function(e) {
    cat("Global error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  }
)

## Function for testing --------------------------------------------------- ----

test_function = function(x){
  print("=================")
  print(x)
  if(x == "print") print("print output")
  if(x == "error") stop("test error")
  
  if(x == "simple try error silent"){
    status = try(stop("loud caught error"), silent = TRUE)
    print(as.character(status))
  }
  
  if(x == "simple try error loud"){
    status = try(stop("silent caught error"), silent = FALSE)
    print(as.character(status))
  }
  
  if(x == "try error"){
    status = tryCatch(
      {stop("caught error")},
      error = function(e){
        msg = paste(e$message, collapse = "\n")
        msg = paste("Stopped with error: ", msg)
        return(msg)
      }
    )
    print(status)
  }
  
}

## function for execution ------------------------------------------------- ----

run_function = function(){
  
  sink("./test_sink.txt", split = TRUE)
  on.exit(sink(), add = TRUE)
  
  test_function("print")
  test_function("simple try error silent")
  test_function("simple try error loud")
  test_function("try error")
  test_function("error")
  test_function("print")
  
}

run_function()

# unlink("./test_sink.txt")
```

### Describe the problem in detail

The `try` unsilent error seems to interact with the error, and the output between these does not print to console. As a result the sink file contains the full output:
```
[1] "================="
[1] "print"
[1] "print output"
[1] "================="
[1] "simple try error silent"
[1] "Error in try(stop(\"loud caught error\"), silent = TRUE) : \n  loud caught error\n"
[1] "================="
[1] "simple try error loud"
[1] "Error in try(stop(\"silent caught error\"), silent = FALSE) : \n  silent caught error\n"
[1] "================="
[1] "try error"
[1] "Stopped with error:  caught error"
[1] "================="
[1] "error"
Global error: test error 
```
But what appears in the console is:
```
[1] "================="
[1] "print"
[1] "print output"
[1] "================="
[1] "simple try error silent"
[1] "Error in try(stop(\"loud caught error\"), silent = TRUE) : \n  loud caught error\n"
[1] "================="
[1] "simple try error loud"
Error in test_function("error") : test error
```

### Describe the behavior you expected

I expected that the two would be identical. Commenting out `test_function("simple try error loud")` or `test_function("error")` means that the console display and the sink file are identical.

Problem appears to be how RStudio console displays errors. When running code in the base R gui, the output in the sink file and the output displayed in the console match.

issue_title: renv::install("commonmark@1.7") fails in a project using renv in rhel10
issue_body: ### System details RStudio Edition : Server/workbench RStudio Version : 2025.08.0+349.pro6 OS Version : R Version : ### Steps to reproduce the problem 1. Login into a rhel10 instance. 2. Start an RStudio session. 3. Create a project that uses renv. 4. Run `renv::install("commonmark@1.7")` ### Describe the problem in detail The user sees the errors below: ``` # Downloading packages ------------------------------------------------------- - Querying repositories for available source packages ... Done! renv was unable to query available packages from the following repositories: - # https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/rhel1/latest/src/contrib -------- error downloading 'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/rhel1/latest/src/contrib/PACKAGES.rds' [error code 22] error downloading 'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/rhel1/latest/src/contrib/PACKAGES.gz' [error code 22] error downloading 'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/rhel1/latest/src/contrib/PACKAGES' [error code 22] - Downloading commonmark from Repository ... ERROR [error code 22] Show Traceback Rerun with Debug Error: failed to retrieve package 'commonmark@1.7' 7.stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.) 6.stopf("failed to retrieve package '%s'", remote) 5.renv_retrieve_repos(record) 4.renv_retrieve_impl_one(package) 3.handler(package, renv_retrieve_impl_one(package)) 2.renv_retrieve_impl(packages) 1.renv::install("commonmark@1.7") > ``` ### Describe the behavior you expected No issues or errors installing that package. - [ ] I have read the guide for [submitting good bug reports](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Writing-Good-Bug-Reports). - [ ] I have installed the latest version of RStudio, and confirmed that the issue still persists. - [ ] If I am reporting an RStudio crash, I have included a [diagnostics report](https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/articles/200321257-Running-a-Diagnostics-Report). - [ ] I have done my best to include a minimal, self-contained set of instructions for consistently reproducing the issue.

issue_title: bookdown::render_book() fails with “path for html_dependency not found” only when building all chapters
issue_body:
I'm having a persistent issue with rendering a bookdown project in RStudio. Building individual chapters (or two at a time) works fine, but when I render the entire book (9 chapters) it fails with this error:
Error: path for html_dependency not found: 
```
C:/Users/user/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpUBxRLF/fileb4ec3c0a381  
Execution halted  
Error: bookdown::render_book() failed to render the output format 'bookdown::gitbook'.: Error: path for html_dependency not found: C:/Users/user/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpUBxRLF/fileb4ec3c0a381  
Execution halted
```
Environment:

 - R: 4.5.1   
- RStudio: 2025.05.1 (Windows 11)  
- bookdown: 0.43  
- rmarkdown:2.29   
- Pandoc: 3.4  
- Rendering to: bookdown::gitbook (HTML)

I have tried toggling chunk cache on/off (knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = TRUE) and cache = FALSE) and updating relevant packages (bookdown, rmarkdown, htmltools).Howver, Single or pairs of chapters build without error, but when the full set (9 .Rmd chapters plus index) is built the failure occurs.

issue_title: package installation doesn't work in background jobs when using authenticated repos
issue_body:
```
Installing 'rsconnect' for Publishing...
[1/3] Installing PKI...
Installing package into ‘/Users/kevin/Library/R/arm64/4.5/library’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
Warning: unable to access index for repository https://solo.packagemanager.posit.co/cran-auth/latest/src/contrib:
  cannot open URL 'https://solo.packagemanager.posit.co/cran-auth/latest/src/contrib/PACKAGES'
Warning: unable to access index for repository https://solo.packagemanager.posit.co/cran-auth/latest/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.5:
  cannot open URL 'https://solo.packagemanager.posit.co/cran-auth/latest/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.5/PACKAGES'
```

This occurs because the hooks that RStudio installs for `download.file()` only work in the main RStudio R session. We should make sure the same download hook is installed within R sub-processes launched by RStudio as well.

+         retvals[idx] <- eval(call, envir = parent.frame())
+      }

+      # Note that even if multiple files are downloaded, R only reports
+      # a single status code, with 0 implying that all downloads succeeded.

+      invisible(status)
+

+.rs.defineHook(
+   package = "utils",
+   binding = "install.packages",
+   function(pkgs, lib, repos)
+   {
+      ""
+      "This is an RStudio hook."
+      "Use `utils::install.packages()` to bypass this hook if necessary."
+      ""
+      
+      if (interactive())
+      {
+         # Check if package installation was disabled in this version of RStudio.
+         canInstallPackages <- .Call("rs_canInstallPackages", PACKAGE = "(embedding)")
+         if (!canInstallPackages)
+         {
+            msg <- "Package installation is disabled in this version of RStudio."
+            stop(msg, call. = FALSE)
+         }
+         
+         # Notify if we're about to update an already-loaded package.
+         # Skip this within renv and packrat projects.
+         if (.rs.installPackagesRequiresRestart(pkgs))
+         {
+            call <- sys.call()
+            call[[1L]] <- quote(install.packages)
+            command <- .rs.deparseCall(call)
+            
+            .rs.enqueLoadedPackageUpdates(command)
+            invokeRestart("abort")
+         }
+         
+         # Make sure Rtools is on the PATH for Windows.
+         .rs.addRToolsToPath()
+         on.exit(.rs.restorePreviousPath(), add = TRUE)
+      }
+      
+      # Resolve library path.
+      if (missing(lib) || is.null(lib))
+         lib <- .libPaths()[1L]
+      
+      # Check if we're installing a package from the filesystem,
+      # versus installing a package from CRAN.
+      isLocal <- is.null(repos) || any(grepl("/", pkgs, fixed = TRUE))
+      
+      if (isLocal)
+      {
+         # Invoke the original function.
+         call <- sys.call()
+         call[[1L]] <- quote(utils::install.packages)
+         result <- eval(call, envir = parent.frame())
+         
+         # Record the package source.
+         shouldRecord <- is.character(pkgs) && length(pkgs) == 1L
+         if (shouldRecord)
+            .rs.recordPackageSource(pkgs, local = TRUE)
+      }
+      else
+      {
+         # Get paths to DESCRIPTION files, so we can see what packages
+         # were updated before and after installation.
+         before <- .rs.installedPackagesFileInfo(lib)
+         
+         # Invoke the original function.
+         call <- sys.call()
+         call[[1L]] <- quote(utils::install.packages)
+         result <- eval(call, envir = parent.frame())
+         
+         # Check and see what packages were updated.
+         after <- .rs.installedPackagesFileInfo(lib)
+         
+         # Figure out which packages were changed.
+         rows <- .rs.installedPackagesFileInfoDiff(before, after)
+         
+         # For any packages which appear to have been updated,
+         # tag their DESCRIPTION file with their installation source.
+         .rs.recordPackageSource(rows$path, local = FALSE)
+      }
+      
+      # Notify the front-end that we've made some updates.
+      if (interactive())
+      {
+         .rs.updatePackageEvents()
+         .Call("rs_packageLibraryMutated", PACKAGE = "(embedding)")
+      }
+      
+      # Return installation result, invisibly.
+      invisible(result)
+   })
+
+.rs.defineHook(
+   package = "utils",
+   binding = "remove.packages",
+   function(pkgs, lib)
+   {
+      ""
+      "This is an RStudio hook."
+      "Use `utils::remove.packages()` to bypass this hook if necessary."
+      ""
+      
+      # Invoke original.
+      result <- utils::remove.packages(pkgs, lib)
+      
+      # Notify front-end that the package library was mutated.
+      if (interactive())
+      {
+         .Call("rs_packageLibraryMutated", PACKAGE = "(embedding)")
+      }
+      
+      # Return original result.
+      invisible(result)
+   })
+

issue_title: json::readObject with boost::optional does not behave the way it is documented
issue_body:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : workbench
    RStudio Version : Cucumberleaf Sunflower
    OS Version      : linux
    R Version       : NA

### Steps to reproduce the problem

make a call to the following function with a param that already holds a value:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/c24efd18fd79551cdddab079dc24ba25eca2b72c/src/cpp/shared_core/include/shared_core/json/Json.hpp#L1987

observe the param still holds that value and there is no indication that the key value pair did not exist in the json.

observe that the function does not return error despite the documentation saying it should.


### Describe the problem in detail

If calling this function and passing in a param that belongs to a POD struct, or anything that is initialized, and we were seeking to change the value, if the key was present in the json, we'd assume the key appeared and was the same, rather than handling the case where the key did not appear.

```
std::string json = "{}";
core::json::Value value;
value.parse(json));
core::json::Object obj = value.getObject();

boost::optional<std::string> testme = std::string("I will still be here");
core::Error error = core::json::readObject(obj, "snuffleupogus", &testme);

if(error)
   abort();
if(testme.hasValue())
{
   // this should not occur, but it does
}

```
### Describe the behavior you expected
This function should set the out param to boost::none when the key is not found
The code documentation should read something akin to:
```
out_value - will be boost::none if the member does not exist, otherwise contains the member's value.
return - Success if the value did not exist or the value was read. Error if the type was not T.
```

AFAICT, all the existing calls use an freshly constructed boost::optional, and would not be effected by the requested change, but all call sites should be checked to handle the change correctly.

-->

### System details

    RStudio Edition :  RStudio-Server
    RStudio Version :  2025.05.1 Build 513
    OS Version      :  Debian 12 (bookworm)
    R Version       :  4.5.1

### Steps to reproduce the problem

This issue consistently occurs on the server whenever I open the RStudio Server GUI using any browser

### Describe the problem in detail

I'm encountering an issue while using RStudio Server on a Debian 12 (bookworm) system with multiple users.

After the admin upgraded RStudio Server to version 2025.05.1 Build 513, we noticed that the memory usage displayed in the RStudio memory panel is unrealistically high , typically in the range of 400–500 GB, even when individual sessions are using less than 200 MB (confirmed via /proc/<pid>/status and pryr::mem_used()).

Upon investigation, we found that the high memory usage shown in the panel is attributed to the cgroup memory usage, and it appears that RStudio Server is reusing a shared memory cgroup (/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/USER-abc, the user id is the rstudio-server user id) across multiple users or sessions.

This leads to misleading memory reports in the UI for each user.

My questions:
Is this likely a bug or a known limitation of the current RStudio Server build?
Are there any recommended ways to diagnose or isolate per-user memory usage more accurately?
Any guidance or suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance!

![img](https://forum.posit.co/uploads/default/original/3X/e/a/eae2e21bd211f0b292b161faa49c14f686934d63.png)

### Describe the behavior you expected

I hope rstudio memory panel shows  the correct rsession memory usage for each user on the server.

issue_title: Message or warning output from R Markdown chunks is sometimes truncated
issue_body:
### System details
    RStudio Edition :  Server
    RStudio Version :  2025.05.1+513
    OS Version      :  Ubuntu 24.1
    R Version       :  4.5.1

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Create a new R Markdown file and execute code that generates errors or warnings.

### Describe the problem in detail

In some cases, the output of message or warning from code chunks in R Markdown documents appears to be cut off or not fully displayed as bellow. This makes it difficult to debug or understand the results properly.

It seems that if you rerun the same code or click the "Show Traceback" button to expand the message, the output is often displayed fully without being cut off on subsequent attempts.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fa8ee44-04c7-4f9a-9273-3f5eb752bf66)

If I rerun the code that triggers the above error, all messages are displayed completely as shown below.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/485949e7-1e35-4057-9c68-60dee9b22d28)

### Describe the behavior you expected

Error, warning, and other messages or outputs should be displayed fully without being truncated.

-->

### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop, probably Server
    RStudio Version : 2025.08.0-daily+214
    OS Version      : Windows 11
    R Version       : 4.5.0

### Steps to reproduce the problem

If Copilot is already on:
0. <kbd>Tools -> Global Options -> Copilot</kbd>, uncheck <kbd>Enable</kbd>, and click <kbd>OK</kbd>.

Steps
1. <kbd>Tools -> Global Options -> Copilot</kbd>, check <kbd>Enable</kbd>, and click <kbd>OK</kbd>.
    - "Restart Required" pops up.
2. <kbd>No</kbd>
    - "Global Options" closes.
3. <kbd>Tools -> Global Options -> Copilot</kbd>, uncheck <kbd>Enable</kbd>, and click <kbd>OK</kbd>.
    - "Global Options" closes.
4. <kbd>Tools -> Global Options -> Copilot</kbd>, check <kbd>Enable</kbd>, and click <kbd>OK</kbd>.
    - "Restart Required" pops up.
 
### Describe the problem in detail

"Restart Required" pops up.

### Describe the behavior you expected

"Restart Required" should not pop. This was the case in 2025.05.1.

issue_title: Can't show the Update Packages dialog
issue_body: ### System details RStudio Edition : Desktop or Server RStudio Version : 2025.08.0-daily+209 OS Version : macOS / Ubuntu 24 R Version : 4.5.0 ### Steps to reproduce the problem - start RStudio - show Packages pane - click Update ### Describe the problem in detail - "subscript out of bounds" error shown ### Describe the behavior you expected - dialog box for updating packages ### QA Notes > Once you have opened a PR, add additional information for QA on how to validate the change, paying special attention to the level of risk, adjacent areas that could be affected by the change, and any important contextual information not present in the original description. - [x] I have read the guide for [submitting good bug reports](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Writing-Good-Bug-Reports). - [x] I have installed the latest version of RStudio, and confirmed that the issue still persists. - [x] If I am reporting an RStudio crash, I have included a [diagnostics report](https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/articles/200321257-Running-a-Diagnostics-Report). - [x] I have done my best to include a minimal, self-contained set of instructions for consistently reproducing the issue.
commit_message: guard against empty libraries (#16146)
patch:
--- a/src/cpp/r/R/Tools.R
+++ b/src/cpp/r/R/Tools.R
@@ -1206,6 +1206,7 @@ environment(.rs.Env[[".rs.addFunction"]]) <- .rs.Env
 
 .rs.addFunction("rbindList", function(data)
 {
+   data <- Filter(length, data)
    result <- do.call(mapply, c(c, data, USE.NAMES = FALSE, SIMPLIFY = FALSE))
    names(result) <- names(data[[1]])
    as.data.frame(result, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

--- a/src/cpp/session/modules/SessionPackages.R
+++ b/src/cpp/session/modules/SessionPackages.R
@@ -187,7 +187,11 @@
          pkgDesc[c("Package", "Version")]
       })
       
-      pkgResult <- .rs.rbindList(Filter(length, pkgDescs))
+      pkgDescs <- Filter(length, pkgDescs)
+      if (length(pkgDescs) == 0L)
+         return(NULL)
+      
+      pkgResult <- .rs.rbindList(pkgDescs)
       pkgResult[["LibPath"]] <- libPath
       pkgResult
    })

                       character.only = TRUE)

                    call. = FALSE, domain = NA)
    }
}

    while(length(dupes <- names(Sys.getenv())[table(names(Sys.getenv())) > 1])) {

      warning("Dropping ", missing, " rows with missing values", call. = FALSE)
    }

  }

issue_title: Sending textDocument/didOpen more than once for a given document (Copilot)
issue_body:
### System details

    RStudio Edition : Desktop or Server
    RStudio Version : 2025.08.0-daily+194
    OS Version      : any
    R Version       : any

### Steps to reproduce the problem

- add `COPILOT_LOG_LEVEL=3` to ~/.Renviron
- start RStudio, no project, no source files open
- open a source file (e.g. foo.R)
- look at Copilot messages in Console
- make a change to the document
- look at Copilot messages in Console

### Describe the problem in detail

Per the [LSP spec](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textDocument_didOpen):

> An open notification must not be sent more than once without a corresponding close notification send before. This means open and close notification must be balanced and the max open count for a particular textDocument is one.

We are sending `textDocument/didOpen` more than once for a document opened in RStudio, both when it is initially opened or when it is edited. For editing we should be using `textDocument/didChange` (ultimately this should send incremental updates vs. re-sending the entire document, but that work is covered by #15901).

This can also be seen if a project (Rproj) is open, project indexing is enabled (under Copilot options), and one or more files that belong to the project are opened in the editor when RStudio launches (i.e. those files were open when the previous session was exited). The files that were already loaded will trigger `textDocument/didChange` both when they are reopened at launch, and via project indexing.

### Describe the behavior you expected

Only a single `textDocument/didOpen` is sent for a give document. Subsequent updates to the document (i.e. edits) should be communicated with `textDocument/didChange`.

commit_message:
Fix issue with crate.bat and PowerShell

PowerShell splits arguments (when using `%*`) also on the 1st dot of
a setting `key`. e.g.:
```
-Cdiscovery.type=single-node
```
would become:
```
-Cdiscovery .type=single-node
```

Add a replacement of ` .` to `.` to rejoin them. The replacement
doesn't affect normal runs with standard `cmd`.

Fixes: #18378
patch:
--- a/app/src/main/dist/bin/crate.bat
+++ b/app/src/main/dist/bin/crate.bat
@@ -116,6 +116,8 @@ if "%CRATE_CLASSPATH%" == "" (
 set CRATE_PARAMS=-Cpath.home="%CRATE_HOME%"
 
 set params='%*'
+REM PowerShell splits setting keys/values on `.`, so this joins again the splitted keys/values
+set params=%params: .=.%
 
 for /F "usebackq tokens=* delims= " %%A in (!params!) do (
     set param=%%A

--- a/docs/appendices/release-notes/6.0.4.rst
+++ b/docs/appendices/release-notes/6.0.4.rst
@@ -59,3 +59,8 @@ Fixes
 
 - Fixed a replication issue happening when an integral value, not fitting to
   ``INT`` or ``LONG`` types, was stored in an OBJECT with policy ``IGNORED``.
+
+- Fixed an issue with ``crate.bat`` Windows startup script throwing error and
+  preventing bootstrap of CrateDB, if ``PowerShell`` was used instead of plain
+  ``CMD`` and parameters were passed with ``-C<key>=value`` command line
+  arguments.

issue_title: Improve error message when column is not in the group by in window functions
issue_body:
### Problem Statement

On queries like: 

```sql
SELECT row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY t) FROM t2 GROUP BY t3;
```

where `t` is not in the group by, an exception is raised:

```sql
UnsupportedFeatureException[Can't handle Symbol [SimpleReference: t]]
```

This error is very confusing for the user:

In postgres is:

```
matriv=# CREATE TABLE "t2" (
  "t" TEXT,
  "t3" TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE
matriv=# SELECT row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY t) FROM t2 GROUP BY t3;
ERROR:  column "t2.t" must appear in the GROUP BY clause or be used in an aggregate function
LINE 1: SELECT row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY t) FROM t2 GROUP BY t...
                                               ^
```

### Possible Solutions

Improve the error message 

### Considered Alternatives

_No response_
commit_message:
Fix partition by cols not in group by

The symbols in `partition by` clause of a window function must also
appear in the `group by` clause of the query, (matching psql behavior).
Previously, this validation was not applied, therefore a confusing
message was thrown later on from the planner, e.g.:
```
SELECT sum(x) over(partition by x, y)
FROM unnest([1], [6]) as t (x, y)
GROUP BY x
```
thew:
```
UnsupportedFeatureException[Can't handle Symbol [SimpleReference: y]]
```

Fixes: #18283

seqNo, primaryTerm and version wasn't sent, causing the replica
operation to fail.

seqNo, primaryTerm and version wasn't sent, causing the replica

issue_title: Generated timestamp column becomes NULL when updating records
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.11

### CrateDB setup information


Single node, default settings

### Problem description

Given a column `last_modified TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE GENERATED ALWAYS AS CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, when a record is updated, the expected behavior is to have the `last_modified` value updated to the `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` however, the value becomes `NULL` instead. It doesn't apply to other data types, for instance a generated column defined as `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (number*10)`.
The behavior was observed in 5.10.11 first (not in previous versions)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create table 
``` sql
create table bug_example(
    "value" int,
    "last_updated" TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE GENERATED ALWAYS AS CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);
```
2. Insert into the table:
```sql
insert into bug_example (value) VALUES (1);
---  1 	 1753697754671 (2025-07-28T10:15:54.671Z) 
```
3. Now update the record and check the table:
```sql
update bug_example set value = 2;
---  2 	 NULL 
```


### Actual Result

After updating the table:
` 2 	 NULL `

### Expected Result

After updating:
`2 	 1753697754671 (2025-07-28T10:15:54.671Z)`

issue_title: `mapping.total_fields.limit` not enforced in `CREATE TABLE`
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.10

### CrateDB setup information

Standard single node

### Problem description

When creating a new table with more columns than configured in `mapping.total_fields.limit`, the limit is not enforced.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE t1 (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c INTEGER, d INTEGER) WITH ("mapping.total_fields.limit" = 3);
-- CREATE TABLE OK, 1 record affected (0.352 seconds)

CREATE TABLE t2 (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c OBJECT AS (c1 INTEGER, c2 INTEGER)) WITH ("mapping.total_fields.limit" = 3);
-- CREATE TABLE OK, 1 record affected (0.382 seconds)
```

### Actual Result

Tables are created successfully.

### Expected Result

Table creation is rejected due to exceeding the limit.

issue_title: Same role can be granted twice on a user
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.9

### CrateDB setup information

_No response_

### Problem description

A user can have the same role repeated, if granted by a different grantor.

For example a user `user_a` can have the role `role_a` granted by `crate` and by `user_admin`.

This opens the windows for many sketchy situations, like roles that cannot be revoked if the original user grantor was dropped.

### Steps to Reproduce

Create two users.
```sql
create user user_admin
```
```sql
create user user_a
```
Create a role and give it permissions.

```sql
create role admin
```
```sql
create role role_a
```

```sql
grant al to admin
```

Give roles

```sql
-- as superuser crate
grant admin to user_admin
```

```sql
-- as superuser crate
grant role_a to user_a
```
```sql
-- as user_admin
grant role_a to user_a
```
now `user_a` has `role_a` twice:

##### Query ran at 2025-07-03T12:39:08.469Z on CrateDB 5.10.9
```
SELECT
  name,
  granted_roles
FROM
  sys.users
order by
  name;
```
|name|granted_roles|
 |-|-| 
|"crate"|[]|
|"user_a"|[{"role":"role_a","grantor":"crate"},{"role":"role_a","grantor":"user_admin"}]|
|"user_admin"|[{"role":"admin","grantor":"crate"}]|

 Additionally, if I drop the user `user_admin`, I cannot remove the role `role_a` granted by `user_admin`, I would need to drop the user.


### Actual Result

same role is twice on the same user

### Expected Result

one user can only have the same role once
commit_message:
Fix for duplicate roles granted to a user by different grantors

Also, allowed 'crate' to be able to revoke any granted roles.

Fixes #18099

issue_title: Flaky bulk `INSERT` behaviour with complex `OBJECT`
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.9

### CrateDB setup information

`docker run --publish=4200:4200 crate/crate:5.10.9`

### Problem description

When running a bulk `INSERT` statement over HTTP, only a subset of the values gets inserted. The count of the number of values inserted is inconsistent and varies when the experiment is repeated.

I tried both multi-value and batch approaches over HTTP, and the behaviour is the same. It was not reproducible anymore after drastically simplifying the JSON document.

The issue is also not reproducible on a nightly build.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
from crate import client

connection = client.connect(servers="http://localhost:4200")
cursor = connection.cursor()

JSON = {"resourceType":"Observation","id":"cf.cgmdata.BBBB","meta":{"profile":["http://bla.com/vitalsigns-observation"]},"extension":[{"url":"http://bla.com/time-offset","valueQuantity":{"value":200,"unit":"min","system":"http://bla.org","code":"min"}},{"url":"http://bla.com/patient-timezone","valueString":"+02:00"},{"url":"http://bla.com/provenance-channel","valueString":"string"},{"url":"http://bla.com/provenance-source","valueString":"string"}],"identifier":[{"system":"http://bla.com","value":"BBBB"}],"status":"final","category":[{"coding":[{"system":"http://url.com","code":"vital-signs","display":"Vital Signs"}]}],"code":{"coding":[{"system":"http://url.com","code":"434910001","display":"Interstitial fluid glucose concentration (observable entity)"}],"text":"CGMGlucoseConcentration"},"subject":{"reference":"Patient/string"},"effectiveDateTime":"2020-08-04T15:00:16Z","performer":[{"reference":"Patient/string"}],"valueQuantity":{"value":118,"unit":"mg/dL","system":"http://bla.com","code":"mg/dL"},"device":{"reference":"DeviceMetric/string"},"related":[{"type":"derived-from","target":{"reference":"Observation/cf.sess.202106151104","display":"202106151104"}}],"component":[{"code":{"coding":[{"system":"http://bla.com","code":"CGM-rate-of-change","display":"CGM rate of change"}],"text":"CGMTrendInformation"},"valueQuantity":{"value":-0.5,"unit":"mg/dL/min","system":"http://bla.com","code":"mg/dL/min"}},{"code":{"coding":[{"system":"http://bla.com","code":"CGM-quality","display":"CGM quality"}],"text":"CGMQuality"},"valueQuantity":{"value":90,"unit":"%","system":"http://bla.com","code":"%"}}]}

# Generate a batch with 500 times the same JSON document
docs = []
for i in range(0, 500):
    docs.append((JSON,))

print(f"Validation: {len(docs)} docs generated")

# Repeat the experiment 10 times
for i in range(0, 10):
    print(f"Run {i}")

    cursor.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS observations")
    cursor.execute("CREATE TABLE observations (raw_resource OBJECT(DYNAMIC))")

    cursor.executemany("INSERT INTO observations VALUES (?)", docs)

    cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM observations")
    result = cursor.fetchone()
    print(f"Row count before refresh: {result[0]}")

    cursor.execute("REFRESH TABLE observations")

    cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM observations")
    result = cursor.fetchone()
    print(f"Row count after refresh: {result[0]}")
    print("-----")

```

### Actual Result

```
Validation: 500 docs generated
Run 0
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 111
-----
Run 1
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 144
-----
Run 2
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 140
-----
Run 3
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 114
-----
Run 4
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 121
-----
Run 5
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 125
-----
Run 6
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 140
-----
Run 7
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 119
-----
Run 8
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 117
-----
Run 9
Row count before refresh: 0
Row count after refresh: 134
-----
```

### Expected Result

Consistent insertion of 500 records for each run of the experiment.

issue_title: SHOW CREATE TABLE returning statement with invalid property name
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.9

### CrateDB setup information

Single node / multi-node

### Problem description

Looking at recreating a table using the output from `SHOW CREATE TABLE` it emerged that `"routing.allocation.exclude._name"` its returned by `SHOW CREATE TABLE` as the invalid `"index.routing.allocation.exclude._name"`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE mytable (a integer);
ALTER TABLE mytable SET ("routing.allocation.exclude._name" = 'data-hot-1');
SHOW CREATE TABLE mytable;
```

### Actual Result

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| SHOW CREATE TABLE doc.mytable                               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."mytable" (                |
|    "a" INTEGER                                              |
| )                                                           |
| CLUSTERED INTO 4 SHARDS                                     |
| WITH (                                                      |
|    column_policy = 'strict',                                |
|    "index.routing.allocation.exclude._name" = 'data-hot-1', |
|    number_of_replicas = '0-1'                               |
| )                                                           |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Expected Result

```
...
|    "routing.allocation.exclude._name" = 'data-hot-1', |
...
```

issue_title: SQLParseException analysis error in bulk_args request reported in manner inconsistent with documented behavior
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.9

### CrateDB setup information

Single node

### Problem description

When performing data ingestion with `bulk_args`, looking at error handling, according to [the documentation](https://cratedb.com/docs/crate/reference/en/latest/interfaces/http.html#error-handling) , we expect analysis phase errors affecting the entire batch to be reported without a `results` array, however a `SQLParseException` seems to be returned in the `results` array, repeated for all records which can be misleading as error logging at record level will suggest there was something wrong with values which were actually good to be inserted.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
create table test2 (x int primary key);
```

```bash
curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-X POST '127.0.0.1:4200/_sql' -d@- <<- EOF
{
"stmt": "insert into test2 (x) values (?)",
"bulk_args": [["abc"], [6]]
}
EOF
```

### Actual Result

```json
{"cols":[],"duration":1.772286,"results":[{"rowcount":-2,"error":{"code":4000,"message":"SQLParseException[Cannot cast value `abc` to type `integer`]"}},{"rowcount":-2,"error":{"code":4000,"message":"SQLParseException[Cannot cast value `abc` to type `integer`]"}}]}
```

### Expected Result

According to the documentation we would expect this to either be an analysis error (no `results` array) which would make it clear to the client nothing was executed, or the record with value `6` inserted successfully.
commit_message:
Fix batch/bulk write analysis error response format

An analysis error while writing HTTP bulk items should result
in a complete error response instead of a per-item error payload.
Additionally, an PG `executeBatch` must fail completely in this
case.

Fixes #18067.

issue_title: Inconsistent format in response to bulk_args operation when a single record is passed and a runtime error occurs
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.9

### CrateDB setup information

Single node

### Problem description

Building an ingestion process using `bulk_args`, and looking at error handling, it is expected that errors will be returned in a `results` array, however this only seems to be the case if the `bulk_args` concerns more than one record.
The inconsistency makes it "more difficult to handle errors during bulk insertion" as the special case of a batch of 1 record, which can occur for the last batch in a task, needs to be handled separately.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
create table test (x int primary key);
```

```bash
curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-X POST '127.0.0.1:4200/_sql' -d@- <<- EOF
{
"stmt": "insert into test (x) values (?)",
"bulk_args": [[1]]
}
EOF

curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-X POST '127.0.0.1:4200/_sql' -d@- <<- EOF
{
"stmt": "insert into test (x) values (?)",
"bulk_args": [[1]]
}
EOF
```

### Actual Result

```json
{"error":{"message":"DuplicateKeyException[A document with the same primary key exists already]","code":4091}}
```


### Expected Result

With `bulk_args` being used, and `DuplicateKeyException` being a runtime error and not an analysis error, according to [the documentation](https://cratedb.com/docs/crate/reference/en/latest/interfaces/http.html#error-handling) a `results` array would be expected in the response.

issue_title: Allocation awareness settings not shown in `sys.cluster`
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.8

### CrateDB setup information

```bash
docker run --publish=4200:4200 crate/crate:5.10.8 \
  -Cnode.attr.zone=a \
  -Ccluster.routing.allocation.awareness.attributes=zone \
  -Ccluster.routing.allocation.awareness.force.zone.values=a,b,c \
  -Ccluster.routing.allocation.cluster_concurrent_rebalance=99 
```

### Problem description

Certain cluster-wide attributes aren't shown in `sys.cluster`. I was trying to reproduce an issue with a multi-zone setup reported in the [community](https://community.cratedb.com/t/increased-cost-in-aws-inter-zone-transfers/2039/7) and started a Docker container as described above.

To validate if my settings got applied correctly, I want to query `sys.cluster` and check if they appear.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a Docker container as described above
2. `SELECT settings['cluster']['routing']['allocation'] FROM sys.cluster`

### Actual Result

```json
{
    "allow_rebalance": "indices_all_active",
    "balance": {
        "index": 0.55,
        "shard": 0.45,
        "threshold": 1.0
    },
    "cluster_concurrent_rebalance": 99,
    "disk": {
        "threshold_enabled": true,
        "watermark": {
            "flood_stage": "95%",
            "high": "90%",
            "low": "85%"
        }
    },
    "enable": "all",
    "exclude": {
        "_host": "",
        "_id": "",
        "_ip": "",
        "_name": ""
    },
    "include": {
        "_host": "",
        "_id": "",
        "_ip": "",
        "_name": ""
    },
    "node_concurrent_recoveries": 2,
    "node_initial_primaries_recoveries": 4,
    "require": {
        "_host": "",
        "_id": "",
        "_ip": "",
        "_name": ""
    },
    "total_shards_per_node": -1
}
```

**Observations**:
1. `"cluster_concurrent_rebalance": 99` has been applied successfully from the Docker startup parameters
2. There is no sign of `cluster.routing.allocation.awareness.attributes` or `cluster.routing.allocation.awareness.force.zone.values`.

### Expected Result

`cluster.routing.allocation.awareness.attributes` and `cluster.routing.allocation.awareness.force.zone.values` are shown in `sys.cluster`, so one can check if they got applied correctly or not.
commit_message:
Fix `c.r.allocation.awareness.*` settings to be visible in `sys.cluster`

Mark the 2 settings were as exposed, and implement allow the implicit
cast of `Settings` (because the `force` one is a group setting), to an
Object, so that it can be transparently used in `SysClusterTableInfo`.

Fixes: #18047

issue_title: `OutOfMemoryError` when querying table with large vector field
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.7

### CrateDB setup information

CrateDB Cloud single-node S4

### Problem description

When querying a large result set with vectors of length 1152, there is an `OutOfMemoryError` instead of a `CircuitBreakingException`.

The issue does not occur when the vector column is defined as a plain `ARRAY(DOUBLE)`.


### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."WayveScenes" (
   "Vector_ID" TEXT,
   "File_Path" TEXT,
   "Coordinate" ARRAY(DOUBLE PRECISION),
   "Vector" ARRAY(DOUBLE PRECISION)
)
CLUSTERED INTO 4 SHARDS;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."WayveScenesVectors" (
   "Vector_ID" TEXT,
   "File_Path" TEXT,
   "Coordinate" GEO_POINT,
   "Vector" FLOAT_VECTOR(1152)
)
CLUSTERED INTO 4 SHARDS;
```
I imported the file https://huggingface.co/datasets/quasara-io/WayveScenes/resolve/main/data/Main_1-00000-of-00001.parquet using the Cloud import functionality into both tables.

### Actual Result

Querying the table with `ARRAY(DOUBLE)` fails with a `CircuitBreakingException`, which is expected given that the node is fairly small and there is no `LIMIT` clause:
```sql
SELECT * FROM "WayveScenes";

org.elasticsearch.common.breaker.CircuitBreakingException: Allocating 2mb for 'parent: http-result' failed, breaker would use 983.9mb in total. Limit is 972.7mb. Either increase memory and limit, change the query or reduce concurrent query load
	at org.elasticsearch.indices.breaker.HierarchyCircuitBreakerService.checkParentLimit(HierarchyCircuitBreakerService.java:275)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.breaker.ChildMemoryCircuitBreaker.addEstimateBytesAndMaybeBreak(ChildMemoryCircuitBreaker.java:129)
	at io.crate.rest.action.SqlHttpHandler.lambda$executeSimpleRequest$1(SqlHttpHandler.java:259)
	at io.crate.data.breaker.BlockBasedRamAccounting.addBytes(BlockBasedRamAccounting.java:74)
	at io.crate.breaker.TypedRowAccounting.accountForAndMaybeBreak(TypedRowAccounting.java:75)
	at io.crate.breaker.TypedRowAccounting.accountForAndMaybeBreak(TypedRowAccounting.java:36)
	at io.crate.rest.action.RestResultSetReceiver.setNextRow(RestResultSetReceiver.java:66)
	at io.crate.session.RetryOnFailureResultReceiver.setNextRow(RetryOnFailureResultReceiver.java:70)
	at io.crate.session.RowConsumerToResultReceiver.consumeIt(RowConsumerToResultReceiver.java:81)
	at io.crate.session.RowConsumerToResultReceiver.accept(RowConsumerToResultReceiver.java:61)
	at io.crate.execution.engine.InterceptingRowConsumer.lambda$tryForwardResult$1(InterceptingRowConsumer.java:93)
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1144)
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:642)
	at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1575)
```

However, the same query against the `FLOAT_VECTOR` table leads to an `OutOfMemory` error:

```sql
SELECT * FROM "WayveScenesVectors";

java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
-- no stack trace available
```

### Expected Result

`CircuitBreakingException` in both cases.
commit_message:
Fix OOM caused by under-accounted memory usage in JSON result sets

The result set for HTTP requests is returned in JSON format, but
the memory accounting logic was type dependant. For example, a
double was counted as 8 bytes, even though in JSON it's actually
a string like "0.123456789" which should be counted as 11 bytes(
sizeof utf-8 * length). This led to under-accounting and
potential OOM.

(cherry picked from commit 006187ad50f256dfb4f1018c01fd54bc2456fd66)

issue_title: Aggregations on generated columns return null when the table is partitioned by it
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.1, 5.10.7, nightly (6.0.0-SNAPSHOT-cd92316)

### CrateDB setup information

docker run -p 4200:4200 crate:5.10.7

### Problem description

If a table is partitioned by a generated column, aggregations on that column will result in `NULL`.



### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
create table t (a integer, b integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS a + 1 NOT NULL) partitioned by ("b");
```

```sql
INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (1), (2)
```

```sql
select min(a), max(b), sum(b) from t
-- 1, NULL, NULL
```

```sql
select * from t
-- 1,	2
-- 2,	3
```

if you add `count`, it works:
```sql
select min(a), max(b), sum(d), count(*) from t
-- 1, 3, 5, 2
```

If the table is not partitioned by the generated column, it works as expected.

### Actual Result

Null values

### Expected Result

Not nulls.
commit_message:
Fix aggregation on PARTITION BY cols

When a column is the PARTITION BY clause of a table we cannot use
doc values aggregators, otherwise the agg function will always return
`NULL` since no values are collected for those columns. Add checks to
`getDocValueAggregator()` to return `null` if the column has `PARTITION`
granularity.

Fixes: #17980

issue_title: ADD COLUMN making wrong schema changes when a hierarchy of fields is passed in a single ALTER TABLE statement
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.5 / 5.10.6

### CrateDB setup information

Single node / multi-node

### Problem description

Reported by: @zolbatar 

Consider a table where we need to define a new array of OBJECTs and a specific field within the objects.
This can be done in different ways.
One way is to do an `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` to add the array, followed by a separate `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` to add the field within, this works.
`ALTER TABLE` also accepts multiple `ADD COLUMN` operations separated by comma. It is understandable that the order of these `ADD COLUMN` operations may not be respected, or that they may run in parallel, but the actual result below is neither what we get adding the array first and the field afterwards not the error message we get adding the field first and the array afterwards, see below.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
create table test (obj object(dynamic));
alter table test add column obj['arr'] array(object(dynamic));
alter table test add column obj['arr']['id'] integer;
show create table test;
/*
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."test" ( |
|    "obj" OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (             |
|       "arr" ARRAY(OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (    |
|          "id" INTEGER                     |

--> GOOD
*/

drop table test;
create table test (obj object(dynamic));
alter table test add column obj['arr']['id'] integer;
alter table test add column obj['arr'] array(object(dynamic));
--> SQLParseException[The table doc.test already has a column named obj['arr']]

drop table test;
create table test (obj object(dynamic));
alter table test add column obj['arr'] array(object(dynamic)),add column obj['arr']['id'] integer;
--> ALTER OK, -1 rows affected
show create table test;
```

### Actual Result

```
| CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."test" ( |
|    "obj" OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (             |
|       "arr" OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (          |
|          "id" INTEGER                     |
|       )                                   |
|    )                                      |
| )                                         |
```
NB: `arr` got created as a plain `object`, not an `array`

### Expected Result

Ideally (sorting the fields to add by name should get them in the right order)
```
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."test" ( |
|    "obj" OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (             |
|       "arr" ARRAY(OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (    |
|          "id" INTEGER                     |
```
in alternative:
```
SQLParseException[The table doc.test already has a column named obj['arr']]
```
commit_message:
Fix adding parent & child object sub-cols in one ALTER stmt

When adding multiple object sub columns where, one is a parent of
another, the child one, would only try to find a parent in the original
table schema, without checking if that parent is also defined in another
`ADD COLUMNN` clause, thus ending up with the DEFAULT `object(dynamic)`
type being set for the parent sub column.

Fixes: #17875

```sql
alter table test add column obj['arr'] array(object(dynamic));
--> SQLParseException[The table doc.test already has a column named obj['arr']]

drop table test;
create table test (obj object(dynamic));
alter table test add column obj['arr'] array(object(dynamic)),add column obj['arr']['id'] integer;
--> ALTER OK, -1 rows affected
show create table test;
```

### Actual Result

```
| CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."test" ( |
|    "obj" OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (             |
|       "arr" OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (          |
|          "id" INTEGER                     |
|       )                                   |
|    )                                      |
| )                                         |
```
NB: `arr` got created as a plain `object`, not an `array`

### Expected Result

Ideally (sorting the fields to add by name should get them in the right order)
```
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."test" ( |
|    "obj" OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (             |
|       "arr" ARRAY(OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS (    |
|          "id" INTEGER                     |
```
in alternative:
```
SQLParseException[The table doc.test already has a column named obj['arr']]
```
commit_message:
Fix adding parent & child object sub-cols in one ALTER stmt

When adding multiple object sub columns where, one is a parent of
another, the child one, would only try to find a parent in the original
table schema, without checking if that parent is also defined in another
`ADD COLUMNN` clause, thus ending up with the DEFAULT `object(dynamic)`
type being set for the parent sub column.

Fixes: #17875
(cherry picked from commit c209664b06f0668788ad161f895aea23e94bddc1)

issue_title: view gets corrupted if its query depends on `error_on_unknown_object_key` = false
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.5 and 5.9.13

### CrateDB setup information

Both single node and multi-node.

### Problem description

VIEWs that depend on `"error_on_unknown_object_key"=false` are shown as corrupted in `information_schema.views` , which in turn is displayed prominently in the Cloud console.
`search_path` is being stored with the view, maybe the same would be needed for `error_on_unknown_object_key` or the setting of the user that is querying `information_schema.views` should be used?

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE tbl1 (obj OBJECT(DYNAMIC));
--> NB works with OBJECT(IGNORED)
CREATE USER user1;
ALTER USER user1 SET ("error_on_unknown_object_key"=false);
GRANT ALL TO user1;
```

```bash
crash -U user1
```

```sql
SELECT obj['not_existing'] as a FROM tbl1;
--> SELECT ok

CREATE VIEW vw1 AS 
	SELECT obj['not_existing'] as a FROM tbl1;
  
 SELECT * FROM vw1;
 --> SELECT ok
 
 select view_definition 
 from information_schema.views 
 where table_name='vw1';
```

### Actual Result

```sql
/* Corrupted view, needs fix */
```

### Expected Result

```
+----------------------------------+
| view_definition                  |
+----------------------------------+
| SELECT "obj"['not_existing'] "a" |
| FROM "tbl1"                      |
+----------------------------------+
```

issue_title: `INSERT` hangs when inserting to a table created on `5.10` upgraded to latest master
issue_body:
Start `5.10.x` 2 node cluster
```
cr8 run-crate 5.10.x -s cluster.name=dev -s path.data='/tmp/data' --keep-data &
cr8 run-crate 5.10.x -s cluster.name=dev -s path.data='/tmp/data2' --keep-data &
```
Create table:
```
cr> CREATE TABLE parted (cols object (dynamic)) CLUSTERED INTO 1 SHARDS;
CREATE OK, 1 row affected (0.925 sec)
```
Do a full restart upgrade to the latest master:
```
cr8 run-crate branch:master -s cluster.name=dev -s path.data='/tmp/data' --keep-data &
cr8 run-crate branch:master -s cluster.name=dev -s path.data='/tmp/data2' --keep-data &
```
Inserting a single row does not go through:
```
cr> INSERT INTO doc.parted (cols) VALUES ({"t_branch:master"= true});
```
Follow up select query results are inconsistent:
```
cr> select * from doc.parted;
+---------------------------+
| cols                      |
+---------------------------+
| {"t_branch:master": true} |
+---------------------------+
SELECT 1 row in set (0.002 sec)
cr> select * from doc.parted;
+------+
| cols |
+------+
+------+
SELECT 0 rows in set (0.004 sec)
```

Could not reproduce in older versions.
commit_message:
Fix issue with adding object sub-cols on insert on old table

Since tables crated on < 6.0.0 are migrated to RelationMetada with: #17670,
when writing the RelationMetada we need to do it regardless of the
`versionCreated` of the table, since the `RelationMetadata` is now the
source of true for the cluster.

Previously, because of the conditional `if` check on the
`versionCreated`, on a >= 2 nodes cluster, when inserting values into a
table which will dynamically create new cols, those new cols where only
visible in `IndexMetadata`, so the node holding a replica shard of the
table and only reading `RelationMetadata` to see the cols of the table,
would never see the new col added and therefore always fail with:
https://github.com/crate/crate/blob/master/server/src/main/java/io/crate/execution/dml/upsert/TransportShardUpsertAction.java#L367

Fixes: #17791

issue_title: Unexpected result when querying a partitioned table by a `BOOLEAN` column
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

CrateDB 6.0.0-SNAPSHOT built f94b10e

### CrateDB setup information

Manual build following the instructions here: https://github.com/crate/crate/blob/master/devs/docs/basics.rst

### Problem description

Consider the test case below. It is unexpected that the last query returns 0 rows because the result of the second query is TRUE, which means that the `WHERE` clause in the last query should be evaluated to TRUE and thus return the row in the table. PostgreSQL returns one row for the third query.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t1;

CREATE  TABLE  t1(c0 BOOLEAN ,PRIMARY KEY(c0))PARTITIONED BY (c0);
INSERT INTO t1(c0) VALUES (FALSE);
REFRESH TABLE t1;

SELECT * FROM t1; -- FALSE
SELECT ((t1.c0)=(FALSE)) FROM t1; -- TRUE
SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE ((t1.c0)=(FALSE));
-- Expected: FALSE
-- Actual: empty table
```

### Actual Result

empty table

### Expected Result

FALSE
commit_message:
Fix issue with BOOLEAN in PARTITION BY

When a table was partitioned by and a `BOOLEAN` column was included in
the `PARTITIONED BY` clause, then the encoding to create the partition
ident, was different when creating the partition (used `"false"` and
`"true"`) than when trying to retrieve the partition when querying the
table (use `"t"` and `"f"`).

Fix the issue, by unifying the encoding, by always using the
`StringType#implicitCast` in all cases where such encoding takes place.

Fixes: #17766

issue_title: Unexpected result when using `IP` addresses
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

CrateDB 6.0.0-SNAPSHOT built f94b10e

### CrateDB setup information

Manual build following the instructions here: https://github.com/crate/crate/blob/master/devs/docs/basics.rst

### Problem description

Consider the test case below. The third query could be unexpected since if the second query is evaluated to TRUE, thus the third query should return the row in the table. Otherwise the result of second query should be unexpected

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t0;

CREATE  TABLE  t0(c0 IP , PRIMARY KEY(c0));
INSERT INTO t0(c0) VALUES ('::ffff:192.168.1.1');
REFRESH TABLE t0;

SELECT * FROM t0; -- 192.168.1.1
SELECT (('192.168.1.1')=(t0.c0)) FROM t0; -- TRUE
SELECT * FROM t0 WHERE (('192.168.1.1')=(t0.c0)); 
-- Expected: 192.168.1.1
-- Actual: empty table
```

### Actual Result

empty table

### Expected Result

`192.168.1.1`
commit_message:
Fix issue with IP values normalization

When a `String` value is stored on a table `IP` column is
normalized in the `IpIndexer`, but this normalization was not
applied to the value when the `IP` column is part of the `PRIMARY KEY`
of the table and is encoded in the value stored as the `_id`.
As a result, a value `::ffff:192.168.0.1` would be stored as is in
the `_id` but would be stored as `192.168.0.1` (normalized) in the
actual column of the table, and therefore `Collect` queries would
yield different matching rows than `Get` queries since in one case
the normalized value would be used, and in the latter the un-normalized
value stored in `_id` would be used instead.

Always normalize the values in the `IpType#implicitCast()` method to
resolve this issue.

Fixes: #17764

issue_title: logical-replicated shards UNASSIGNED after a node restart
Restarting nodes breaks logical replications
issue_body:
1. start 1 node publisher cluster, create table and publication:

```
cr8 run-crate 5.6.x -s cluster.name=my_test -s path.data='/tmp/data' --keep-data &

cr> create table doc.x (a int) clustered into 1 shards with (number_of_replicas=0);
CREATE OK, 1 row affected (0.795 sec)
cr> create publication p for table doc.x;
CREATE OK, 1 row affected (0.082 sec)
```

2. start 1 node subscriber cluster, create subscription:
```
cr8 run-crate 5.6.x &

cr> create subscription rs connection 'crate://localhost:4300?user=crate&sslmode=sniff' publication p;
CREATE OK, 1 row affected (0.142 sec)
```

3. restart the publisher cluster(kill the process created from 1. and start again).

4. try dropping `doc.x` from subscriber side:
```
cr> drop table doc.x;
DROP OK, 1 row affected (0.084 sec)
```
not just `drop`, replication won't happen anymore.

Expected behaviour is actually an exception:
```
cr> drop table doc.x;
OperationOnInaccessibleRelationException[The relation "doc.x" doesn't allow DROP operations, because it is included in a logical replication subscription.]
```

This is regression in `5.6`, `5.5` works as expected.
commit_message:
Expose indices with non-active primary shards in publications

Once an index is restored on the subscriber side, it must always
be included in the publication state response, otherwise it
will be treat as dropped, which in turn causes the tracking to
stop and turn the table into a normal writable one.
Such, the index must even be exposed when it has some non-active
primary shards.
But indices with non-active primary shards will fail on restoring,
so each index will contain a marker setting to express this.
This way, such an index will not be tried to restore, and
already subscriped tables will continue to be tracked (retry).

Fixes #17734.
Supersedes #17830.
Follow up of #15108.

issue_title: Throttling is not working on a Batch INSERT ... SELECT.. ON CONFLICT
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.3

### CrateDB setup information

Number of nodes: 1
CRATE_HEAP_SIZE: 512m


### Problem description

This is similar to https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/17643 but covers an edge case of INSERT ON CONFLICT where update phase will add heavy unaccounted values to the `ShardUpsertRequest` items
(and hence behave similar to UPDATE in that regard).

Details:

If a column of the target table is not used in the INSERT clause it will be either
- fetched from the existing doc and taken as is if not mentioned in DO UPDATE SET
- overwritten in `DO UPDATE SET` by some hardcoded value or combination of other columns

In both cases we don't account for that value on a sender side when batching requests.
This leads to having heavier than expected requests on a recipient side.


Caveat:

There are 2 sub-cases:
1. Column is not used at all in the INSERT targets, then we can use statistics for the top-level column
2. An object column is used in targets but source table has more sub-columns. We have a logic to combine objects (see `Maps.mergeInto `in the `UpdateToInsert`) - we need to compute only "delta" and use stats only for non-overlapping sub-columns

### Steps to Reproduce

```
CREATE TABLE source (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        a INT,
        doc OBJECT(DYNAMIC)
    );

CREATE TABLE target (
        id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        a INT,
        doc OBJECT(DYNAMIC)
    );
```

commit_message:
Improve ram estimation for inserts-on-conflict-update

This adds table stats estimation for insert-on-conflict-update statements
to improve ram-estimation. It also moves the batch-update ram estimation
into the planner.

issue_title: `ALTER TABLE RESET` is not applied on partitions
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.3

### CrateDB setup information

Standard single-node Docker container

### Problem description

When running `ALTER TABLE SET`, the changed attribute is applied both to the table and all partitions of that table. A subsequent `ALTER TABLE RESET` however does not reset the value on partitions.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
cr> CREATE TABLE t1 (a INTEGER, b INTEGER) PARTITIONED BY (a);
CREATE OK, 1 row affected (0.096 sec)
cr> INSERT INTO t1 VALUES (1, 2), (2, 3);
INSERT OK, 2 rows affected (0.733 sec)
cr> SELECT partition_ident, settings['blocks']['write'] FROM information_schema.table_partitions;
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
| partition_ident | settings['blocks']['write'] |
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
|           04132 | FALSE                       |
|           04134 | FALSE                       |
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
SELECT 2 rows in set (0.019 sec)
cr> SELECT settings['blocks']['write'] FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name = 't1';
+-----------------------------+
| settings['blocks']['write'] |
+-----------------------------+
| FALSE                       |
+-----------------------------+
SELECT 1 row in set (0.019 sec)
cr> ALTER TABLE t1 SET ("blocks.write" = TRUE);
ALTER OK, -1 rows affected (0.055 sec)
cr> SELECT partition_ident, settings['blocks']['write'] FROM information_schema.table_partitions;
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
| partition_ident | settings['blocks']['write'] |
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
|           04132 | TRUE                        |
|           04134 | TRUE                        |
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
SELECT 2 rows in set (0.009 sec)
cr> SELECT settings['blocks']['write'] FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name = 't1';
+-----------------------------+
| settings['blocks']['write'] |
+-----------------------------+
| TRUE                        |
+-----------------------------+
SELECT 1 row in set (0.005 sec)
cr> ALTER TABLE t1 RESET ("blocks.write");
ALTER OK, -1 rows affected (0.042 sec)
cr> SELECT partition_ident, settings['blocks']['write'] FROM information_schema.table_partitions;
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
| partition_ident | settings['blocks']['write'] |
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
|           04132 | TRUE                        |
|           04134 | TRUE                        |
+-----------------+-----------------------------+
SELECT 2 rows in set (0.004 sec)
cr> SELECT settings['blocks']['write'] FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name = 't1';
+-----------------------------+
| settings['blocks']['write'] |
+-----------------------------+
| FALSE                       |
+-----------------------------+
SELECT 1 row in set (0.009 sec)
```

### Actual Result

See above.

### Expected Result

`settings['blocks']['write']` is `FALSE` on all partitions after the `ALTER TABLE t1 RESET ("blocks.write");`.

issue_title: SQLParseException only logged in jobs_log when statement came via http interface
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.2 and 5.10.3

### CrateDB setup information

```shell
podman run -d --name cratedb --publish=4200:4200 --publish=5432:5432 --env CRATE_HEAP_SIZE=1g docker.io/crate/crate:5.10.3 -Cdiscovery.type=single-node
```

### Problem description

`SQLParseException`s only seem to appear in `sys.jobs_log` when the statements come via the http interface

### Steps to Reproduce

```shell
psql -h localhost -U crate -d doc
```

```sql
ROLLBACK;

SELECT stmt FROM sys.jobs_log WHERE error IS NOT NULL ORDER BY started DESC LIMIT 1;
--> 0 rows
```

Ctrl+D

```shell
crash
```

```sql
SELECT stmt FROM sys.jobs_log WHERE error IS NOT NULL ORDER BY started DESC LIMIT 1;
--> 0 rows

ROLLBACK;

SELECT stmt FROM sys.jobs_log WHERE error IS NOT NULL ORDER BY started DESC LIMIT 1;
/*
+-----------+
| stmt      |
+-----------+
| ROLLBACK; |
+-----------+
*/
```

### Actual Result

See repro steps above

### Expected Result

`sys.jobs_log` reflecting all run statements with the errors returned regardless of the interface used to send the requests

```bash
mkjson --num 100000 \
```

Use table statistics to improve ram estimation for updates

use case where the updated values are not part of the request.
