commit_message:
Use table statistics to improve ram estimation for updates

This improves the ram estimation for ShardUpsertRequest for the update
use case where the updated values are not part of the request.
This avoids update workloads that can exceed the node's memory.

issue_title: mapping.total_fields.limit not enforced in CREATE TABLE statement
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10.2 and nightly-6.0.0-2025-03-18-00-02

### CrateDB setup information

Single node

### Problem description

`mapping.total_fields.limit` does not seem to be enforced when the initial table definition is already in conflict with the `total_fields.limit` setting.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE t1 (a int);
ALTER TABLE t1 SET ("mapping.total_fields.limit"=3);
ALTER TABLE t1 ADD column b int;
ALTER TABLE t1 ADD column c int;
ALTER TABLE t1 ADD column d int;
--> SQLParseException[Limit of total columns [3] in table [doc.t1] exceeded]
DROP TABLE t1;
CREATE TABLE t1 (a int,b int, c int, d int) WITH ("mapping.total_fields.limit"=3);
```

### Actual Result

```
CREATE OK, 1 row affected (0.326 sec)
cr> insert into t1 values (1,2,3,4);
INSERT OK, 1 row affected (0.015 sec)
cr> select * from t1;
+---+---+---+---+
| a | b | c | d |
+---+---+---+---+
| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
+---+---+---+---+
SELECT 1 row in set (0.005 sec)
```

### Expected Result

```
SQLParseException[Limit of total columns [3] in table [doc.t1] exceeded]
```

issue_title: New column in partitioned table wrongfully shows `NULL` in CrateDB console for not null values
issue_body: ### CrateDB version > 5.9.11 ### CrateDB setup information Tested with single node ### Problem description Given a table created prior to 5.5.0 before the column ID was implemented, if a new column is added to that table after upgrading to > 5.5.0 and its version was wrongfully updated by changing the `number_of_replicas`, for instance, the result set shows the Column with `NULL` values even though it is not `NULL`. However, with `crash` I get the correct result: ``` +---------+---------+ | version | new_col | +---------+---------+ | 1 | a | +---------+---------+ ``` ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create table in version 5.4.x: ```sql CREATE TABLE test_versions_col (version INT) partitioned by (version); ``` 2. Upgrade cluster to 5.7.5, alter table settings and add the new sub-column: ```sql ALTER TABLE test_versions_col SET (number_of_replicas = '0'); ALTER TABLE test_versions_col ADD COLUMN new_col TEXT; ``` 4. Upgrade cluster to 5.9.11, insert new record and select columns: ```sql INSERT INTO test_versions_col VALUES (5911, 'a'); SELECT version, new_col FROM test_versions_col; ``` ### Actual Result ### Expected Result ``` +---------+---------+ | version | new_col | +---------+---------+ | 5911 | a | +---------+---------+ ```
commit_message:
Fix misbehaving columns with oids in partitioned tables < COLUMN_OID_VERSION

Previously there was an issue with partitioned tables' created version
being falsely updated(#17178). The initial mitigation(#17228) was only
about the created version settings not oids. Now there are partitioned
tables < COLUMN_OID_VERSION but with columns with oids assigned resulting
in #17574.

Fixes #17574, #17575

issue_title: Column ID is displayed instead of name in new sub-column in partitioned table
issue_body: ### CrateDB version > 5.9.11 ### CrateDB setup information It was replicated in a local single node but it was observed in multi-node clusters. ### Problem description Given a table created prior to 5.5.0 before the column ID was implemented, if a new sub-column is added to that table after upgrading to > 5.5.0 and its version was wrongfully updated by changing the `number_of_replicas` for instance, the result set shows the columnID instead of the sub-column name, as seen below: ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create table in version 5.4.x: ```sql CREATE TABLE test_versions_col (version INT, obj_strict OBJECT(STRICT) AS (sub_col1 TEXT, sub_col2 INT)) partitioned by (version); ``` 2. Upgrade cluster to 5.7.5, alter table settings and add the new sub-column: ```sql ALTER TABLE test_versions_col SET (number_of_replicas = '0'); ALTER TABLE test_versions_col ADD COLUMN obj_strict['sub_col3'] TEXT; ``` 4. Upgrade cluster to 5.9.11, insert new record and select columns: ```sql INSERT INTO test_versions_col VALUES (5911, {"sub_col1"='b',"sub_col2"=2, "sub_col3"='bb'}); SELECT obj_strict FROM test_versions_col; ``` ### Actual Result ``` +---------------------------------------------+ | obj_strict | +---------------------------------------------+ | {"1": "bb", "sub_col1": "b", "sub_col2": 2} | +---------------------------------------------+ ``` ### Expected Result ``` +---------------------------------------------------+ | obj_strict | +---------------------------------------------------+ | {"sub_col1": "b", "sub_col2": 2,"sub_col3": "bb"} | +---------------------------------------------------+ ```

issue_title: Table with FLOAT_VECTOR bigger than 2048 can be created
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

CrateDB 5.10.1 (built b898c2f/NA, Linux 5.15.0-134-generic amd64, OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM 23.0.2+7)

### CrateDB setup information

_No response_

### Problem description

[Doc](https://cratedb.com/docs/crate/reference/en/latest/general/ddl/data-types.html#ranges-and-widths) says that max FLOAT_VECTOR is 2048, but bigger ones can be created.

```sql
CREATE TABLE my_vectors (
    xs FLOAT_VECTOR(2147483647)
);
-- ok
```

Creating a vector bigger than the max integer value results in an error.

```sql
CREATE TABLE my_vectors (
    xs FLOAT_VECTOR(2147483648)
);
-- ArithmeticException[integer overflow]
```

I think we should check the input size and act accordingly.

### Steps to Reproduce

create table with float_vector bigger than 2048

### Actual Result

No error

### Expected Result

Error happens

According to the [docs](https://cratedb.com/docs/crate/reference/en/latest/general/ddl/analyzers.html#shingle), `max_shingle_size=2` and `output_unigrams=true` are the defaults, but when you create an analyser using shingle with the defaults, you end up getting error messages when you insert data.

commit_message:
Add missing DisableGraphAttribute implementation

ShingleTokenFilter can produce multiple tokens at each position of
differing lengths, which means downstream consumers that expect a
well-formed token graph, such as FixedShingleFilter or query parsers,
may produce nonsensical output. To prevent this, ShingleTokenFilter
will mark its TokenStream with a DisableGraphAttribute if it produces
output that cannot be coerced into a graph.

The concrete implementation class for this attribute was missing,
meaning that attempts to use a shingle filter with output_unigrams=true
or with differing min and max shingle sizes would cause errors on
ingest.


Fix privileges check for DROP ANALYZER

`visitDropAnalyzerStatement()` was not correctly overriden in
`AccessControlImpl`, so previsouly, only the `crate` superuser was able
to drop an analyzer.

planner because:

   issues (attempting to drop an already dropped analyzer)

issue_title: Nested join query returns empty result
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

master

### Problem description

Query result of a nested join query contains an empty result.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "core"."consumption_report" (
   "to_ts" TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
   "subscription_id" TEXT NOT NULL,
   "reporting_id" TEXT
)
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "core"."subscriptions" (
   "id" TEXT NOT NULL,
   "reference" TEXT,
   "provider" TEXT NOT NULL,
   PRIMARY KEY ("id")
)
```

```sql
insert into "core"."consumption_report" values ('1970-01-01T00:00:00', 1, null);
```

```sql
insert into "core"."subscriptions" values ('id', 1, 'AWS');
```

```sql
refresh table "core"."subscriptions";
refresh table "core"."consumption_report";
```

```sql
SELECT p.provider::TEXT, min(r.to_ts)::timestamptz
FROM core.consumption_report r
INNER JOIN core.subscriptions s
    ON r.subscription_id = s.reference
RIGHT JOIN UNNEST(['AWS', 'AZURE', 'STRIPE', 'STRIPE_BT', 'GCP']) AS p(provider)
    ON p.provider::TEXT = s.provider
WHERE
    r.reporting_id IS NULL
    AND s.provider IN ('AWS', 'AZURE', 'STRIPE', 'STRIPE_BT', 'GCP')
GROUP BY p.provider::TEXT
ORDER BY p.provider::TEXT
```







### Actual Result

```sql
Empty result
```

### Expected Result

```sql
+-----------+------------+
| provider  | min(to_ts) |
+-----------+------------+
| AWS       |       0    |
+-----------+------------+
```

commit_message:
Fix add col with with custom analyzer

Previously, the proper settings for the analyzer where not stored,
so the `IndexService` serving the index (indices for parted tables)
where not correctly storing the custom analyzers to the `indexAnalyzers`
map for the index in question, resulting in `No analyzer found` errors,
when attempting to use the full text index on the column.

Fixes: #17473

issue_title: INSERT ... SELECT with RETURNING clause throws ClassCastException
issue_body: ### CrateDB version 5.9.6 ### CrateDB setup information _No response_ ### Problem description When using an INSERT ... SELECT statement with a RETURNING clause, CrateDB throws a ClassCastException: ```sql INSERT INTO table_a(id, value) SELECT id, value FROM table_b WHERE condition = true RETURNING *; ``` Throws: `ClassCastException[null]` and sometimes `ClassCastException[class java.lang.String cannot be cast to class java.lang.Long (java.lang.String and java.lang.Long are in module java.base of loader 'bootstrap')] ` Unable to track successfully inserted records in a single query. In our case, ``` insert into doc.projects_posts( project_id, post_id ) select 'a35c6f21-864c-4f9a-b478-df9f6ef012b6', id from doc.posts where id = '019517d4-3be6-7de3-aef8-b61cfe0130b3' returning post_id; ``` It exhibits a flaky behavior: ### Steps to Reproduce 1 - Create two tables with matching schemas 2 - Run INSERT ... SELECT with RETURNING clause ### Actual Result ClassCastException is thrown Unable to use RETURNING with INSERT ... SELECT ### Expected Result RETURNING clause should work with INSERT ... SELECT statements Should return the inserted records

issue_title: Empty partitions are left behind after `DELETE FROM` even when using partition key in condition
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.6.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9, 5.10

> [!important]
> **Works as expected in 5.5.4, 5.6.4 !**
> This seems to be a regression from 5.6.4 -> 5.6.5

### CrateDB setup information

_No response_

### Problem description

_No response_

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
DROP TABLE if exists temp.t001;

CREATE TABLE temp.t001 (
  x TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
  x_day TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE GENERATED ALWAYS AS date_trunc('day', x)
) PARTITIONED BY (x_day);

INSERT INTO temp.t001 (x)
SELECT x FROM generate_series(now() - INTERVAL '5 days', now(), INTERVAL '1 day') g (x);

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.table_partitions
where table_name = 't001';

DELETE FROM temp.t001 WHERE x_day < now() - INTERVAL '3 days';

REFRESH TABLE temp.t001;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.table_partitions
where table_name = 't001';

DELETE FROM temp.t001 WHERE x_day IN (
SELECT values['x_day'] FROM information_schema.table_partitions where values['x_day'] < now() - INTERVAL '3 days'
);

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.table_partitions
where table_name = 't001';
```

```

CREATE OK, 1 row affected (0.071 sec)

|        6 |

| count(*) |

+----------+

DELETE OK, -1 rows affected (0.042 sec)

| count(*) |
+----------+
|        3 |
+----------+
SELECT 1 row in set (0.001 sec)
```

commit_message:
Fix for unremoved empty partitions when DELETE condition contained nondeterministic functions

such as `now()`. This is a regression introduced by #15924 which
incorrectly prevented normalizing nondeterministic functions during
WhereClauseAnalyzer.resolvePartitions().

The scope of #15924 was 'Do not normalize nondeterministic functions
during analysis' but WhereClauseAnalyzer.resolvePartitions() is not
part of the analysis phase.

issue_title: Filter pushdown on VIEW with UNNEST not working when filter column is aliased
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.9

### CrateDB setup information

Single node

### Problem description

On a denormalized dataset we have tables where each record has a lot of information.
We want to use VIEWs to abstract complex business logic involving unnesting data.
These VIEWs will be accessed for specific record IDs each time. 
As data is joined with other tables where column names repeat, column aliases are used.
It is critical for performance that only the relevant records are accessed avoiding full table scans, but we are seeing situations where filters are not pushed down when aliases are involved. See repro steps below.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE test_unnest1 (
	field1 INT,
	arr ARRAY(OBJECT)
) CLUSTERED INTO 1 SHARDS
WITH (number_of_replicas=0);

CREATE VIEW vw_unnest AS (	
  SELECT 
	*,
	unnest(arr)
  FROM test_unnest1	  
);

EXPLAIN
SELECT *
FROM vw_unnest
WHERE field1=1;

--> Collect[doc.test_unnest1 | [arr, field1] | (field1 = 1)]

EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT *
FROM vw_unnest
WHERE field1=1;

--> PointRangeQuery

CREATE VIEW vw_unnest_with_field_aliased AS (
  SELECT 
	field1 as tableid,
	unnest(arr)
  FROM test_unnest1
);

EXPLAIN
SELECT *
FROM vw_unnest_with_field_aliased
WHERE tableid=1;
--> Collect[doc.test_unnest1 | [arr, field1 AS tableid] | true]

EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT *
FROM vw_unnest_with_field_aliased
WHERE tableid=1;

--> MatchAllDocsQuery
```

### Actual Result

Full table scan

### Expected Result

Filter pushdown as in the scenario without a column alias.
commit_message: Fix filter pushdown for views when filtered column is aliased.

issue_title: Unexpected results when using `LEFT JOIN` with a subquery
commit_message:
Fix wrong join results for CASE in join condition

Previously, a query like the following:
```
SELECT * FROM t0
LEFT JOIN (SELECT 2 AS col2 FROM t0) AS sub0
ON CAST((CASE t0.c0 WHEN sub0.col2 THEN t0.c1 ELSE t0.c1 END )
```
would be wrongly executed with HashJoin instead of NL.
As a result, multiple rows could end up with the same hash value, but
some of them could evaluate to `true` and others to `false`, thus
right side NULLed rows wouldn't be emmitted.

Fix the `EquiJoinDetector` to only drill down to CASE and IFscalars (other than
some special cases like AND/OR/NOT operators and CAST) only if those
scalars are under a top level Equality operator (`=`).

Fixes: #17380

issue_title: Unexpected results when using `ARRAY_POSITION`
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

CrateDB 6.0.0-SNAPSHOT built c58f384

### CrateDB setup information

Manual build following the instructions here: https://github.com/crate/crate/blob/master/devs/docs/basics.rst

### Problem description

Consider the following test case. The second query returns `NULL` showing the expression should be evaluated to `NULL`. However, the third query returns one row in the table, which is unexpected.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t0;

CREATE  TABLE  t0(c0 INT , c1 ARRAY(STRING));
INSERT INTO t0(c0, c1) VALUES (1, ['alpha', 'beta', 'gamma']);
REFRESH TABLE t0;

SELECT * FROM t0; -- 1 | ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]
SELECT ((t0.c0)!=(ARRAY_POSITION(t0.c1, 'a', 1))) FROM t0; -- NULL
SELECT * FROM t0 WHERE ((t0.c0)!=(ARRAY_POSITION(t0.c1, 'a', 1)));
-- Expected: empty set
-- Actual: 1 | ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]
```

### Actual Result

one row in the table

### Expected Result

empty result set

wrong results when used on the `WHERE` clause on a table cols wrapped
with the `NOT` predicate.

issue_title: Inconsistent naming of PK contraints between key_column_usage , pg_class and SHOW CREATE TABLE
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.8 and 5.10.0

### CrateDB setup information

Single node and multi node

### Problem description

`CREATE TABLE` accepts both named and non-named PK constraints.
In the case of named PK constraints `SHOW CREATE TABLE` shows the custom names are stored.
But `pg_catalog.pg_class` (as JOINed with `pg_index`) and `information_schema.key_column_usage` always show automatically generated names and these are not consistent between these 2 system views.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE hernan.testpk (
	a int,
	b text,
	c float,
	CONSTRAINT pk_test PRIMARY KEY (a,b) 
);

SHOW CREATE TABLE hernan.testpk;
--> PK correctly named pk_test

SELECT constraint_name 
FROM information_schema.key_column_usage 
WHERE table_schema='hernan' AND table_name='testpk';
--> testpk_pk - should be pk_test

SELECT c2.relname
FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c2
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_index i ON c2.oid = i.indexrelid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class c1 ON c1.oid = i.indrelid
WHERE c1.relname = 'testpk';
--> testpk_pkey - should be pk_test

DROP TABLE hernan.testpk;

-- Repeat steps above without "CONSTRAINT pk_test" --> same results
```

### Actual Result

See above

### Expected Result

See above
commit_message:
Consolidate default pk name in info schema & pg catalog

Use `<table_name>_pkey` in both cases, whereas previously, for
`information_schema.key_column_usage` `<table_name>_pk` was used.

Fixes: #17377

Fix: show custom pk name in pg_class & key_column_usage

Previously, even if a custom name was provided for the PK during table
creation, the `pg_class.relname` and
`information_schema.key_column_usage.constraint_name` columns where
showing an artificial pkName, based on the table name and a suffix.

issue_title: Inconsistent naming of PK contraints between key_column_usage , pg_class and SHOW CREATE TABLE
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.8 and 5.10.0

### CrateDB setup information

Single node and multi node

### Problem description

`CREATE TABLE` accepts both named and non-named PK constraints.
In the case of named PK constraints `SHOW CREATE TABLE` shows the custom names are stored.
But `pg_catalog.pg_class` (as JOINed with `pg_index`) and `information_schema.key_column_usage` always show automatically generated names and these are not consistent between these 2 system views.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE hernan.testpk (
	a int,
	b text,
	c float,
	CONSTRAINT pk_test PRIMARY KEY (a,b) 
);

SHOW CREATE TABLE hernan.testpk;
--> PK correctly named pk_test

SELECT constraint_name 
FROM information_schema.key_column_usage 
WHERE table_schema='hernan' AND table_name='testpk';
--> testpk_pk - should be pk_test

SELECT c2.relname
FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c2
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_index i ON c2.oid = i.indexrelid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class c1 ON c1.oid = i.indrelid
WHERE c1.relname = 'testpk';
--> testpk_pkey - should be pk_test

DROP TABLE hernan.testpk;

-- Repeat steps above without "CONSTRAINT pk_test" --> same results
```

### Actual Result

See above

### Expected Result

See above
commit_message:
Consolidate default pk name in info schema & pg catalog

Use `<table_name>_pkey` in both cases, whereas previously, for
`information_schema.key_column_usage` `<table_name>_pk` was used.

Fixes: #17377
(cherry picked from commit e8e905a5e07bdce0ba858512351fbdb35ee3f1e4)

issue_title: Inconsistent naming of PK contraints between key_column_usage , pg_class and SHOW CREATE TABLE
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.8 and 5.10.0

### CrateDB setup information

Single node and multi node

### Problem description

`CREATE TABLE` accepts both named and non-named PK constraints.
In the case of named PK constraints `SHOW CREATE TABLE` shows the custom names are stored.
But `pg_catalog.pg_class` (as JOINed with `pg_index`) and `information_schema.key_column_usage` always show automatically generated names and these are not consistent between these 2 system views.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE hernan.testpk (
	a int,
	b text,
	c float,
	CONSTRAINT pk_test PRIMARY KEY (a,b) 
);

SHOW CREATE TABLE hernan.testpk;
--> PK correctly named pk_test

SELECT constraint_name 
FROM information_schema.key_column_usage 
WHERE table_schema='hernan' AND table_name='testpk';
--> testpk_pk - should be pk_test

SELECT c2.relname
FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c2
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_index i ON c2.oid = i.indexrelid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class c1 ON c1.oid = i.indrelid
WHERE c1.relname = 'testpk';
--> testpk_pkey - should be pk_test

DROP TABLE hernan.testpk;

-- Repeat steps above without "CONSTRAINT pk_test" --> same results
```

### Actual Result

See above

### Expected Result

See above
commit_message:
Consolidate default pk name in info schema & pg catalog

Use `<table_name>_pkey` in both cases, whereas previously, for
`information_schema.key_column_usage` `<table_name>_pk` was used.

Fixes: #17377
(cherry picked from commit e8e905a5e07bdce0ba858512351fbdb35ee3f1e4)

issue_title: MIN() and MAX() Functions on NUMERIC Data Type Order Values alphabetically Instead of Numerically
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9

### CrateDB setup information

_No response_

### Problem description

When using the MIN() and MAX() aggregate functions on columns defined with a NUMERIC data type, the values are being compared as strings (i.e., alphabetical order) rather than by their numeric value. This results in incorrect results for these functions.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
create table num_3 ("value" NUMERIC(18, 3));

insert into num_3 values (10),(9);

select max(value), min(value) from num_3 limit 100;

```

### Actual Result

```
max(value)	min(value)
9.000 	        10.000 
```

### Expected Result

```
max(value)	min(value)
10.000          9.000 	
```
commit_message:
Fix MIN/MAX for NUMERIC values

Previously, there was no `NUMERIC` signature registered, and as a
result, the `NUMERIC` values where implicitly casted to `STRING`
leading to wrong results, as an alphanumeric ordering was used instead
of the numeric one.

Fixes: #17360

issue_title: ArithmeticException on AVG() Calculation with NUMERIC Column Due to Non-Terminating Decimal Expansion
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.x and 5.10

### CrateDB setup information

I've tested with single node and 3 node cluster

### Problem description

When performing an average calculation on a column defined as NUMERIC(18,3), the query fails with an ArithmeticException indicating a non-terminating decimal expansion. The issue appears when the division results in a repeating decimal that cannot be represented exactly with the defined scale.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
create table num_2 ("value" NUMERIC(18, 3));

insert into num_2 values (6),(2),(2);

select avg(value) from num_2;

```
Note: The sum of the values is 10 and there are 3 rows, so the expected average is 10/3 ≈ 3.3333… (a repeating decimal).

I also tried to use the `round()` function to limit the result size, but got the same error.

```sql
select round(avg(value),3) from num_2;
```

### Actual Result

An ArithmeticException is thrown due to a non-terminating decimal expansion when attempting to compute the average, indicating that the division operation does not properly apply rounding or truncation for the defined scale. I got the same result when trying to explicitly round the result with the `ROUND` function.

Error message:
`ArithmeticException[Non-terminating decimal expansion; no exact representable decimal result.]`



### Expected Result

The average should be calculated as 10/3 and returned as a value rounded (or truncated) to three decimal places (i.e., 3.333). It should handle non-terminating decimals in accordance with the column’s scale definition without throwing an exception.
commit_message:
Use math context with maximal (finite) precision when computing average state

Helps to void ArithmeticException on infinite fractions

commit_message:
Fix eval projection to support fewer outputs than its source

The Eval projection has a logic to add casts to its source outputs
to a given list of target types (its own outputs). This is e.g.
needed for Union's to ensure that all source outputs are cast to
the same type.
In some situtions the source can contain more symbols than the
given target types to cast to.

Closes #17341.

commit_message:
Fix eval projection to support fewer outputs than its source

The Eval projection has a logic to add casts to its source outputs
to a given list of target types (its own outputs). This is e.g.
needed for Union's to ensure that all source outputs are cast to
the same type.
In some situtions the source can contain more symbols than the
given target types to cast to.

Closes #17341.

issue_title: COPY gets stuck with RETURN SUMMARY
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.10 (testing) / master (Jan 29th)

### CrateDB setup information

Local Mac 

### Problem description

File with 1 Million records can be imported with 

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "doc"."bluesky" (
      "did" VARCHAR,
      "time_us" BIGINT,
      "kind" VARCHAR,
      "commit" OBJECT (IGNORED) AS (
        "collection" TEXT,
        "operation" TEXT
      ),
      "identity" OBJECT (IGNORED)
) CLUSTERED INTO 10 SHARDS WITH (codec = 'best_compression');

COPY bluesky
FROM 'https://clickhouse-public-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/bluesky/file_0006.json.gz'
WITH (compression='gzip') ;
-- COPY OK, 999998 rows affected (8.099 sec)
```

However with `RETURN SUMMARY` this imports 999998 records and then the job gets stuck (also not possible to kill the job)

```sql
COPY bluesky
FROM 'https://clickhouse-public-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/bluesky/file_0006.json.gz'
WITH (compression='gzip') RETURN SUMMARY;
```


### Steps to Reproduce

see above

### Actual Result

job gets stuck, doesn't return summary.

### Expected Result

jobs executes - with potential errors - and returns summary

issue_title: Couldn't resolve value for subQuery in query with multiple references to same table
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.6 , 5.9.8 , and 5.10.0

### CrateDB setup information

Single node and 3 nodes

### Problem description

The query below fails with a `SQLParseException`

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE hernan.places  (
	place_id INTEGER,
	place_name TEXT,
	parent_place_id INTEGER	
);

INSERT INTO hernan.places VALUES (1,'Vienna',2),(2,'Austria',null);

REFRESH TABLE hernan.places;

CREATE VIEW hernan.vw_places AS SELECT * FROM hernan.places;

CREATE TABLE hernan.tbl2 (field1 TEXT,place_id	 INTEGER);

INSERT INTO hernan.tbl2 VALUES ('abc',1);

REFRESH TABLE hernan.tbl2;

CREATE VIEW hernan.vw2 as select * from hernan.tbl2;

WITH cities AS (
	SELECT g.place_id as city_id,g.parent_place_id,g.place_name as city_name
	FROM hernan.vw_places g
	WHERE g.parent_place_id=2
),
countries AS (
	SELECT s.place_name,s.place_id
	FROM hernan.vw_places s
	WHERE place_id IN (SELECT parent_place_id FROM cities)
),
cities_with_countries AS (
	SELECT *,
		(SELECT countries.place_name
		FROM countries
		WHERE cities.parent_place_id=countries.place_id) as country_name
	FROM cities
),b as (
        SELECT field1,
            place_id
        FROM hernan.vw2
        WHERE  place_id IN (SELECT city_id FROM cities)
            
    )
SELECT *
FROM b
INNER JOIN cities_with_countries c ON c.city_id = b.place_id;
```

commit_message:
Fix SubQueryResults.merge(), result values of both sides must be used

When merging 2 SubQueryResults, the result values of both sides
must be taken into account and merged.

Fixes #17307.

Single node and 3 nodes

### Problem description

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE hernan.places  (
	place_id INTEGER,
	place_name TEXT,
	parent_place_id INTEGER	
);

INSERT INTO hernan.places VALUES (1,'Vienna',2),(2,'Austria',null);

REFRESH TABLE hernan.places;

CREATE VIEW hernan.vw_places AS SELECT * FROM hernan.places;

CREATE TABLE hernan.tbl2 (field1 TEXT,place_id	 INTEGER);

INSERT INTO hernan.tbl2 VALUES ('abc',1);

WITH cities AS (
	SELECT g.place_id as city_id,g.parent_place_id,g.place_name as city_name
	FROM hernan.vw_places g
	WHERE g.parent_place_id=2
),
countries AS (
	SELECT s.place_name,s.place_id
	FROM hernan.vw_places s
	WHERE place_id IN (SELECT parent_place_id FROM cities)
),
cities_with_countries AS (
	SELECT *,
		(SELECT countries.place_name
		FROM countries
		WHERE cities.parent_place_id=countries.place_id) as country_name
	FROM cities
),b as (
        SELECT field1,
            place_id
        FROM hernan.vw2
```

issue_title: Partition is lost when attempting to `ALTER TABLE` with `number_of_shards` greater `routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node`
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.6

### CrateDB setup information

Standard single node

### Problem description

On a partitioned table, when issuing an `ALTER TABLE` that attempts to increase `number_of_shards` on an existing partition greater than `routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node`, data of that partition is lost.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE t1 (
   a INTEGER,
   b INTEGER
) CLUSTERED INTO 1 SHARDS
PARTITIONED BY (a)
WITH ("routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node" = 2);

INSERT INTO t1 VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 2);
REFRESH TABLE t1;

ALTER TABLE t1 PARTITION (a = 1) SET ("blocks.write" = true)
ALTER TABLE t1 PARTITION (a = 1) SET (number_of_shards = 64);
-- Returns "ALTER OK, 0 records affected (30.082 seconds)"
-- When running it on a large partition, a steep drop in disk usage is seen, indicating data is dropped

-- data from the a = 1 partition no longer shows
SELECT * FROM t1;
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 2 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 |
+---+---+
SELECT 2 rows in set (0.002 sec)

-- checking the reasons for missing shard allocation
SELECT DISTINCT UNNEST(decisions)['explanations'] FROM sys.allocations WHERE table_name = 't1' AND partition_ident = '04132';
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| unnest(decisions)['explanations']                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ["resize source index [[.partitioned.t1.04132/5y5gpRqlTd6n7Fc5bDs_TQ]] doesn't exists", "too many shards [2] allocated to this node for index [.partitioned.t1.04132], index setting [index.routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node=2]"] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
SELECT 1 row in set (0.009 sec)

-- trying to address the "too many shards allocated for this node" issue
ALTER TABLE t1 SET ("routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node" = 100);

-- the a = 1 partition is still unavailable
SELECT DISTINCT UNNEST(decisions)['explanations'] FROM sys.allocations WHERE table_name = 't1' AND partition_ident = '04132';
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| unnest(decisions)['explanations']                                                       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ["resize source index [[.partitioned.t1.04132/5y5gpRqlTd6n7Fc5bDs_TQ]] doesn't exists"] |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Actual Result

Changing the number of shards succeeds and original shards are dropped.

### Expected Result

An error message, preventing the deletion of original shards. Or, the ability to recover once `routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node` is increased after changing the number of shards.
commit_message:
Fix handling of unallocated shards during number_of_shards resize

The resize operation didn't check if the shards are acknowledged before
triggering the "swap and drop" operation. This led to data loss if the
shards of the resized index weren't allocated.

Solution:

- Add a check if the resize was acknowledged (plus shards acknowledged)
- Add a sanity check in the drop+swap operation that the source has all
  primaries allocated
- Remove the ChainableAction mechanism, because none of the operations
  had a undo action
- Filter away `.resized` indices when retrieving the index names for a
  table. These shouldn't be included on a `select * from tbl` and would
  lead to `IndexName.decode` errors

Closes https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/17278

issue_title: Partition is lost when attempting to `ALTER TABLE` with `number_of_shards` greater `routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node`
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.6

### CrateDB setup information

Standard single node

### Problem description

On a partitioned table, when issuing an `ALTER TABLE` that attempts to increase `number_of_shards` on an existing partition greater than `routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node`, data of that partition is lost.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE t1 (
   a INTEGER,
   b INTEGER
) CLUSTERED INTO 1 SHARDS
PARTITIONED BY (a)
WITH ("routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node" = 2);

INSERT INTO t1 VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 2);
REFRESH TABLE t1;

ALTER TABLE t1 PARTITION (a = 1) SET ("blocks.write" = true)
ALTER TABLE t1 PARTITION (a = 1) SET (number_of_shards = 64);
-- Returns "ALTER OK, 0 records affected (30.082 seconds)"
-- When running it on a large partition, a steep drop in disk usage is seen, indicating data is dropped

-- data from the a = 1 partition no longer shows
SELECT * FROM t1;
+---+---+
| a | b |
+---+---+
| 2 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 |
+---+---+
SELECT 2 rows in set (0.002 sec)

-- checking the reasons for missing shard allocation
SELECT DISTINCT UNNEST(decisions)['explanations'] FROM sys.allocations WHERE table_name = 't1' AND partition_ident = '04132';
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| unnest(decisions)['explanations']                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ["resize source index [[.partitioned.t1.04132/5y5gpRqlTd6n7Fc5bDs_TQ]] doesn't exists", "too many shards [2] allocated to this node for index [.partitioned.t1.04132], index setting [index.routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node=2]"] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
SELECT 1 row in set (0.009 sec)

-- trying to address the "too many shards allocated for this node" issue
ALTER TABLE t1 SET ("routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node" = 100);

-- the a = 1 partition is still unavailable
SELECT DISTINCT UNNEST(decisions)['explanations'] FROM sys.allocations WHERE table_name = 't1' AND partition_ident = '04132';
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| unnest(decisions)['explanations']                                                       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| ["resize source index [[.partitioned.t1.04132/5y5gpRqlTd6n7Fc5bDs_TQ]] doesn't exists"] |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Actual Result

Changing the number of shards succeeds and original shards are dropped.

### Expected Result

An error message, preventing the deletion of original shards. Or, the ability to recover once `routing.allocation.total_shards_per_node` is increased after changing the number of shards.
commit_message:
Fix handling of unallocated shards during number_of_shards resize

The resize operation didn't check if the shards are acknowledged before
triggering the "swap and drop" operation. This led to data loss if the
shards of the resized index weren't allocated.

Solution:

- Add a check if the resize was acknowledged (plus shards acknowledged)
- Add a sanity check in the drop+swap operation that the source has all
  primaries allocated
- Remove the ChainableAction mechanism, because none of the operations
  had a undo action
- Filter away `.resized` indices when retrieving the index names for a
  table. These shouldn't be included on a `select * from tbl` and would
  lead to `IndexName.decode` errors

Closes https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/17278

issue_title: Can't handle Symbol error when running query as prepared statement
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.5 and 5.10.0

### CrateDB setup information

Multi-node

### Problem description

The query below executes without issues if the parameter value is put directly into the statement but fails as a prepared statement.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE test.tbl1 (
"field1" BIGINT,
"field2" TEXT,
"field3" TEXT,
"field4" BIGINT,
"field5" BIGINT
);
```

**NB substitue hostname username and password as required**
```python
import pg8000

import ssl
ssl_context = ssl.create_default_context()

conn = pg8000.connect(
    user="admin",
    password="************************************",
    host="*******************",
    port=5432,
    database="doc",
    ssl_context=ssl_context
)

query = """

  WITH cte1 AS (
    SELECT
      p.field1,
      p.field2,
      p.field3,      
      CASE
        WHEN :param1 = 7 THEN p."field5"
      END AS field6
    FROM test.tbl1 p
    WHERE p.field2 ilike 'abc'    
    AND p.field1 IN (123)
    ORDER BY field6 DESC
    LIMIT 10
  ), cte2 AS (
    SELECT
      p.field1,
      p.field2,
      p.field3,      
      CASE
        WHEN :param1 = 7 THEN p."field4"
      END AS field7
    FROM test.tbl1 p
    WHERE p.field2 ilike 'abc'    
    AND p.field1 IN (123)
    ORDER BY field7 DESC
    LIMIT 10
  ), cte3 AS (
    SELECT field1, field2, field3,array_unique(array_agg({field7 = field7}::OBJECT)) as field8
    FROM cte2
    GROUP BY 1,2,3
  ), cte4 AS (
    SELECT field1, field2, field3,array_unique(array_agg({field6 = field6}::OBJECT)) as field9
    FROM cte1
    GROUP BY 1,2,3
  )
  SELECT DP.*, SP.field9 FROM cte3 DP INNER JOIN cte4 SP ON DP.field1 = SP.field1 AND DP.field2 = SP.field2  AND DP.field3 = SP.field3
"""

ps = conn.prepare(query)
ps.run(    param1=90)


```

### Actual Result

```

NodeOperations: [1=>NodeOp{ phase{id=1/mergeOnHandler, nodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], dist=SAME_NODE}, downstreamNodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], downstreamPhase=6, downstreamInputId=0}, 2=>NodeOp{ phase{id=2/fetchPhase, nodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A, msx5erdrReW2S6nK1ytP9g]}, downstreamNodes=[], downstreamPhase=2147483647, downstreamInputId=0}, 3=>NodeOp{ phase{id=3/collect, nodes=[msx5erdrReW2S6nK1ytP9g, zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], dist=BROADCAST}, downstreamNodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], downstreamPhase=4, downstreamInputId=0}, 5=>NodeOp{ phase{id=5/fetchPhase, nodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A, msx5erdrReW2S6nK1ytP9g]}, downstreamNodes=[], downstreamPhase=2147483647, downstreamInputId=0}, 4=>NodeOp{ phase{id=4/mergeOnHandler, nodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], dist=SAME_NODE}, downstreamNodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], downstreamPhase=6, downstreamInputId=1}, 0=>NodeOp{ phase{id=0/collect, nodes=[msx5erdrReW2S6nK1ytP9g, zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], dist=BROADCAST}, downstreamNodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], downstreamPhase=1, downstreamInputId=0}]
Leafs: [JoinPhase{executionNodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A], executionPhaseId=6, name=hash-join, joinType=INNER, joinCondition=(((INPUT(0) = INPUT(5)) AND (INPUT(1) = INPUT(6))) AND (INPUT(2) = INPUT(7))), outputTypes=[bigint, text, text, object_array, object_array], jobId=8eee562d-f936-8a8e-f4fb-157a0a5c8f20, executionNodes=[zu9oj4HoRHW1rRH11XZ43A]}]
```

commit_message:
Allow precision=scale in NumericType; Fix avg aggregation errors

During an `avg` operation it can happen that we get a `BigDecimal` value
with scale==precision.

This caused streaming to fail because it creates a `NumericType` derived
from the `BigDecimal` value and `NumericType` so far enforced that
`scale > precision`.

This relaxes the restriction.
Closes https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/17271

Allow precision=scale in NumericType; Fix avg aggregation errors

During an `avg` operation it can happen that we get a `BigDecimal` value
with scale==precision.

from the `BigDecimal` value and `NumericType` so far enforced that
`scale > precision`.

issue_title: SQLParseException in query with ROUND and aggregations
issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.5 and 5.10.0

### CrateDB setup information

Multi-node

### Problem description

In the query below `field4` is 0.25 and its `pg_typeof` is `numeric` but then when the AVG of this one row is computed something goes wrong with the tracking of the data type.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE test.tbl1 (
	"field1" BIGINT,
	"field2" BIGINT
) CLUSTERED INTO 8 SHARDS;

INSERT INTO test.tbl1 (field1,field2)
select 123 as field1,4::BIGINT as field2;

REFRESH TABLE test.tbl1;

CREATE VIEW test.vw1 AS SELECT * FROM test.tbl1;

WITH cte1
AS (
	SELECT 123 AS field1
		,'abc' as grouping1
		,1 as d	
	)
	,cte2
AS (
	SELECT cs.grouping1
		,ROUND((SUM(cs.d) / AVG(cf.field2 )) , 2) AS field4
	FROM test.vw1 cf	
	INNER JOIN cte1 cs ON cs.field1 = cf.field1
	GROUP BY cs.field1
		,grouping1
	)
SELECT AVG(field4)
FROM cte2;
```

commit_message:
Suppress missing key errors when accessing child of an object literal from aliased table

Regression from `5.10` caused by https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17052.
The root cause is the object literals returned from functions are missing
inner types. Adding a workaround so that such object literals' types would be
ObjectType.UNTYPED and catching them during subscript expression analysis
in order to fall back to subscript functions instead of searching inner types
for keys.

in order to fall back to subscript functions instead of searching inner types
for keys.

issue_body:
### CrateDB version

5.9.5 , 5.9.6 , and 5.10.0

### CrateDB setup information

12 nodes, single node, and 3 nodes

### Problem description

The query at the bottom of the repro steps below fails in the presence of statistics when the `LIMIT` is applied, removing the `LIMIT` or without statistics it works.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE test.tbl1 (
	"field1" BIGINT,
	"field2" OBJECT(DYNAMIC) AS ("arr" ARRAY(INTEGER))
)
CLUSTERED INTO 2 SHARDS;

INSERT INTO test.tbl1
SELECT a.b,{"arr"=[1,2]}
FROM generate_series(1,150) a(b);

REFRESH TABLE test.tbl1;

CREATE TABLE test.tbl2 ("field1" BIGINT)
CLUSTERED INTO 4 SHARDS;

INSERT INTO test.tbl2
SELECT a.b
FROM generate_series(1,150) a(b),generate_series(1,1400) c(d);

REFRESH TABLE test.tbl2;

create view test.vw1  as
  SELECT *
FROM test.tbl1;

ANALYZE;

SELECT vw1.field2['arr']
FROM test.vw1
INNER JOIN test.tbl2  on vw1.field1 = tbl2.field1
LIMIT 10;
```

commit_message:
Fix issue with ScopedSymbol subscript and FetchRewrite

In `Eval.rewriteToFetch` when we have an output which is a
`ScopedSymbol` and is a child (subscript) of an output of the `source()`
plan of `Eval`, previously we failed to properly rewrite the
`ScopedSymbol` as a reference (subscript function) to the `FetchStub`
generated. e.g.:

```
-- tbl2#noRows > tbl1#noRows tables are switched in the join and Eval
-- is added on top of the HashJoin.

cr> EXPLAIN SELECT vw1.field2['arr']
    FROM (SELECT * FROM tbl1) as vw1
    INNER JOIN tbl2 on vw1.field1 = tbl2.field1
    LIMIT 10;
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| QUERY PLAN                                                            |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Fetch[field2['arr']] (rows=10)                                        |
|   └ Limit[10::bigint;0] (rows=10)                                     |
|     └ Eval[vw1._fetchid] (rows=1400)                                  |
|       └ HashJoin[INNER | (field1 = field1)] (rows=1400)               |
|         ├ Collect[doc.tbl2 | [field1] | true] (rows=210000)          |
|         └ Rename[vw1._fetchid, field1] AS vw1 (rows=150)              |
|           └ Collect[doc.tbl1 | [_fetchid, field1] | true] (rows=150) |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

To fix it, properly resolve the subscript `ScopedSymbol` as a reference
to the generated `FetchStub` in `MapBackedSymbolReplacer`.

Fixes: #17267

commit_message:
Fix issue with ScopedSymbol subscript and FetchRewrite

In `Eval.rewriteToFetch` when we have an output which is a
`ScopedSymbol` and is a child (subscript) of an output of the `source()`
plan of `Eval`, previously we failed to properly rewrite the
`ScopedSymbol` as a reference (subscript function) to the `FetchStub`
generated. e.g.:

```
-- tbl2#noRows > tbl1#noRows tables are switched in the join and Eval
-- is added on top of the HashJoin.

cr> EXPLAIN SELECT vw1.field2['arr']
    FROM (SELECT * FROM tbl1) as vw1
    INNER JOIN tbl2 on vw1.field1 = tbl2.field1
    LIMIT 10;
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| QUERY PLAN                                                            |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Fetch[field2['arr']] (rows=10)                                        |
|   └ Limit[10::bigint;0] (rows=10)                                     |
|     └ Eval[vw1._fetchid] (rows=1400)                                  |
|       └ HashJoin[INNER | (field1 = field1)] (rows=1400)               |
|         ├ Collect[doc.tbl2 | [field1] | true] (rows=210000)          |
|         └ Rename[vw1._fetchid, field1] AS vw1 (rows=150)              |
|           └ Collect[doc.tbl1 | [_fetchid, field1] | true] (rows=150) |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

To fix it, properly resolve the subscript `ScopedSymbol` as a reference
to the generated `FetchStub` in `MapBackedSymbolReplacer`.

Fixes: #17267
(cherry picked from commit 15aac231208dc300e232ed6859452d228ea205d8)

issue_title: Prepared Statement Query Returns Duplicate Records. CrateDB Console Query works fine.
commit_message:
Fix issue when binding the same values to PK lookup

When querying by PK (also when additionally using _seq_no and
_primary_term), and bound parameters are used, then since the
WHERE clause optimization takes place before binding values to the
params, a query like: `SELECT * FROM tbl WHERE pkCol = ? OR pkCol = ?`
will result in 2 DocKey entries, since at that point we don't know the
actual values which will be bound, and therefore normalize and eliminate
duplicates. As a consequence, and since PkAndVersion objects were
returned in a `List`, if duplicate values are bound, the `PKLookupPhase`
will fetch duplicate records.

Use `LinkedHashSet` (to keep also the order of the values) instead of
`List` to eliminate `PkAndVersion` resuling duplicates after query
parameters are bound (in `Get#build()`).

Fixes: #17266

issue_title: openpdf-html Configuration logs a warning about missing defaults file
issue_body:
### Describe the bug

When forking flying saucer, the Configurator class was changed somewhat, including the default filename for properties from xhtmlrenderer.conf to openpdf.conf. 

However, the actual configuration file was not renamed.

### To Reproduce

Start the project with no overriding configuration files available

The first PDF generated with openpdf-html will print the warning `"No configuration files found in classpath using UR...`

### Expected behavior

No error, default values loaded

### System


- OS: Windows
- Used font: Irrellevant
- OpenPDF version: 2.2.1

### Additional context

The file in question just needs to be renamed, or if the defaults in the file is already the hardcoded defaults, the file should be deleted and we should just load the hardcoded defaults directly.

From a quick glance there's only a few differences between the hardcoded and the file

`xr.renderer.missing-character-replacement`  has value `#` in the file and  `false` in hardcoded.  The default value being false in hardcoded looks like a bug, and the defaultVal on access is also `#`

```
xr.image.background.workers=5
xr.image.background.greedy=true
```
These are not set in code, but workers are defaulted to 5 on acces, while greedy is not currently in use with a "FIXME" tag above it, meaning this has no effect.

issue_title: LZW stream decoding bug with text-based content like PostScript calculator functions
issue_body:
### Describe the bug

For PDF streams using LZW compression, i.e. a "/Filter" value of "/LZWDecode", there are certain scenarios where decoding produces incorrect decoded values, causing the decoded output to be corrupt or causing null pointer exceptions.

This code gets hit when getting decoded bytes from PdfStream or PRStream. 
 For example: 

`PdfStream.getBytes(true)`
`PdfReader.getStreamBytes(PrStream)`

These eventually use the `LZWDecoder` class (originally from 20 year old Sun Microsystems implementation for TIFF processing).

Digging deeper, this class works flawlessly when LZW stream starts with the Clear Table code (256), which appears to be there for all image data we have come across in PDFs.  For text-based data, like the Type 4 Postscript calculator function, the LZW stream does not necessarily start with the Clear Table code.  This is where things go south.  The table indexing and codes get off, causing corrupt data or null exceptions.

I have a fix I will raise a PR for that I believe is safe and correct.

### To Reproduce

Code to reproduce the issue

Attaching the raw data bytes of two LZW compressed Type 4 Postscript calculator functions.  One causes corrupt output and the other a null exception.  Here is a code snippet to reproduce with either sample:

        try {
            Path path = Path.of("/path/to/attached/encoded-file");
            byte[] encodedData = Files.readAllBytes(path);
            LZWDecoder decoder = new LZWDecoder();

            ByteArrayOutputStream outputStream = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
            decoder.decode(encodedData, outputStream);
            byte[] decodedData = outputStream.toByteArray();
            String type4Function = new String(decodedData);
            System.out.println(type4Function);

        } catch (IOException e) {
            throw new RuntimeException(e);
        }
    }

### Expected behavior

Output should match actual encoded data.  For the "202" sample attached, expedcted output looks like this:

{
1.0 3 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 2 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 1 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 1.0 exch sub 4 1 roll
1.0 3 index 1.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 2 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 1 index 1.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 1.0 exch sub 4 1 roll
1.0 3 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 2 index 1.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 1 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 1.0 exch sub 4 1 roll
1.0 3 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 2 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 1 index 0.000000 mul 1.0 exch sub mul 1.0 exch sub 4 1 roll
pop
pop
pop
}

and actual output from `LZWDecoder` looks like this:

{
1.0 2 index
10
100
 mulx 1. dech sub0
 mux 2 inde 0.60

10b0ul
1. xdech su
10blx.0 dch sub3muxroll{
x 1 2 index 0709845su
ul .0 dechub mb0ux 2 inde 1.60.0ub
10bl
1xdch 5sx 1ul .xdcub31 muxroll{.0x 1 2 inde.1207645.0usu
u1. x dch s45.b0uxind
1.6ch 5lx.su
u1.0 d1.6c
10bl 1. x  su3mrollul .0xx 2  0573646.0 d1x 1u dch0
 mub31 2 ind 01.660. dch05sxlx.sxdc45. dch05
1xh sxdcu1 3mr
pop3mr
po
}

### System

(please complete the following information)

- OS: All
- OpenPDF version: 2.0.3 and previous (affected code is several years old)

### Your real name
Scott More

### Example data 

[202-decoded-actual.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19980331/202-decoded-actual.txt)
[202-encoded.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19980332/202-encoded.txt)

* Issue 1298 - Fix in LZWDecoder when valid PDF stream data does not start with LZW Clear Table code (256), occurs in PostScript calculator functions in several PDFs we have encountered, changes include unit tests to cover both common LZW and this more uncommon scenario

* Issue 1298 - Fixed up style violations in import statements in new LZWDecodedTest file

* Issue 1298 - Removed unneeded throws IOException from new LZW decoder unit test

* Issue 1298 - Simplified unexpected case in main LZW decode loop to not throw RuntimeException and silently proceed, not as big a fan of this change but cannot get past static code analyzers without it

         nextBits = 0;
 
-        int code, oldCode = 0;
+        int code;
+        Integer oldCode = null;
         byte[] string;
 
         while ((code = getNextCode()) != 257) {
-
             if (code == 256) {
-
+                // Clear Table code, reset string table and previous code tracking state
                 initializeStringTable();
-                code = getNextCode();
-
-                if (code == 257) {
-                    break;
-                }
-
-                writeString(stringTable[code]);
-                oldCode = code;
-
-            } else {
-
-                if (code < tableIndex) {
+                oldCode = null;
+                continue;
+            }
 
-                    string = stringTable[code];
+            if (code < tableIndex) {
+                string = stringTable[code];
+                writeString(string);
 
-                    writeString(string);
+                if (oldCode != null) {
                     addStringToTable(stringTable[oldCode], string[0]);
-                    oldCode = code;
-
-                } else {
-
-                    string = stringTable[oldCode];
-                    string = composeString(string, string[0]);
-                    writeString(string);
-                    addStringToTable(string);
-                    oldCode = code;
                 }
+            } else if (oldCode != null) {

+                addStringToTable(string);

+

+        // This sample is the much more common case where LZW data starts with the Clear Table (256) code.  LZWDecoder
+        // was already decoding this sample perfectly.  Included here to verify the fix and any future changes to
+        // LZWDecoder do not break this more common case.
+        assertDoesNotThrow(() -> testLzwDecoder(
+                "/issue1298/lzw-cmap-table-encoded.bin",
+                "/issue1298/lzw-cmap-table-decoded.txt"));
+    }
+
+    private void testLzwDecoder(String encodedDataFile, String expectedDecodingFile)
+            throws IOException {
+
+        // Get LZW encoded data from test resource.  Actual data pulled from PDF streams in real-life PDF files.
+        try (InputStream encodedStream = getClass().getResourceAsStream(encodedDataFile)) {
+            // Read LZW encoded data taken from a PDF stream
+            assertNotNull(encodedStream);
+            byte[] encodedData = encodedStream.readAllBytes();
+
+            // Use LZWDecoder directly to decode this data.  This decoder gets used in these calls:
+            //    PdfStream.getBytes(true)
+            //    PdfReader.getStreamBytes(PrStream)
+            LZWDecoder decoder = new LZWDecoder();
+            ByteArrayOutputStream outputStream = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
+            decoder.decode(encodedData, outputStream);
+            byte[] decodedData = outputStream.toByteArray();
+
+            // Read expected result and compare
+            try (InputStream expectedStream = getClass().getResourceAsStream(expectedDecodingFile)) {
+                assertNotNull(expectedStream);
+                byte[] expectedData = expectedStream.readAllBytes();
+                assertArrayEquals(expectedData, decodedData);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}

issue_title: PKCS7 doesn't verify
issue_body:
### Describe the bug

If you create a PKCS7 with PdfPKCS7 and then verify it, the verification fails. 

### To Reproduce

Code to reproduce the issue

[Sample Code](https://bin.koehn.com/?31080d27d0eacdaf#3NWq3829DJywhmbhQJCyqfVG1y8RftssCPjEureYfzR9)

### Expected behavior

The PKCS7, while structurally correct (huzzah!) should also verify. If you put the PKCS7 into a PDF matching the SHA-256 digest, that will not verify. 

### System

(please complete the following information)

- OS: n/a; I'm using OpenJRE 23. 
- OpenPDF version: 2.0.3
- Problem occurs with BouncyCastle or AWS CloudHSM

## Your real name
Brad Koehn

### Additional context

The only call I can see to sign anything is happening before the signedAttributes are created. From what I can tell, the RSA signature at the end should be [SHA256withRSA(DER(SignedAttributes))](http://www.pkiglobe.org/pkcs7.html). It appears to be SHA256withRSA(pdfData). I'll try to make a version that digests the DER of the signedAttributes.

issue_title: implicit cast from "vec4" to "vec3" in PBRLighting.frag
commit_message:
Fix logic errors and exception in SpecGloss pipeline

This PR addresses this issue: 
#2386 
And then I also found another critical logic error in the spec gloss pipeline that was likely there even before riccardo adapted the shader to use structs:

It looks like the specular value taken from specularMaps was being totally ignored and not used in the roughness calculation. The code further down in the shader was calculating the roughness solely based on m_Glossiness with no regard for the glossiness texture maps, which is incorrect.

The logic error and exception should all be fixed in this PR now, but it will need testing from a spec gloss model with packed specularGlossinesMap as well as a model with seperate specular and glossiness maps in order to ensure everything works properly now.

commit_message:
Account for annotations in extends / implements when computing view as supertype (#1266)

Fixes #1252 

In JDK 21 and earlier, the `Types.asSuper` method did not account for
annotations present in extends / implements clauses. So, here we wrap
calls to `asSuper` in extra logic to re-introduce these annotations. We
already introduced the logic to fix the same issue with
`Types.memberType`.

This fix also (unexpectedly) addresses an issue in another test which
was misdiagnosed as https://github.com/uber/NullAway/issues/1022. #1022
indicated annotations were missing in cast types in earlier JDKs, but
this was incorrect (that issue should be closed). In fact, the bug
observed there (in test `intersectionTypeInvalidAssign`) was in fact the
`asSuper` bug fixed here. We misdiagnosed the problem partly because in
some JDK version after JDK 21, `Types.asSuper` started behaving
differently and preserving annotations in extends / implements clauses.

As a related cleanup, delete the unused
`InferGenericMethodSubstitutionViaAssignmentContextVisitor` class.

commit_message:
Use refined types from dataflow analysis in generic method inference (#1309)

Fixes #1287 

In generic method inference, we now try to obtain a refined type from
dataflow-based type inference for arguments when generating constraints.
This introduces a recursive dependence between dataflow analysis and
generic method inference, which we handle as follows. We track whether
generic method inference has been invoked from dataflow by passing a
`calledFromDataflow` parameter. When the parameter is true, generic
method inference calls a new API to get the _current_ dataflow fact for
the argument from the running dataflow analysis, avoiding a recursive
run. Since this may not be the fact in the final fixed point of
dataflow, we skip caching of generic method inference results when it is
invoked from the dataflow analysis. This may skip caching unnecessarily
in some cases, but we prefer to make correctness more obvious for now;
we can optimize further in the future if needed.

commit_message:
issue-1250 pattern matching for instanceof in switch case (#1259)

Fixes #1250 

The goal is to make visitCase aware of pattern variables. When it
encounters a case with a pattern (like case
BusinessExceptionUnauthenticated e), it should:
1. Positively identify that this is a pattern matching case, not a
simple constant case.
2. In the "then" branch (the code path for the body of the case), it
must record two facts:
* The variable being switched on (bException) is non-null and has the
type of the pattern.
       * The new pattern variable (e) is also non-null.
3. Crucially, in the "else" branch (the code path for all subsequent
case labels), it must not alter the existing nullness information for
the variable being switched on. This is what is
causing the bug right now - the information is being corrupted for the
following default case.

commit_message:
Invoke generic method inference in more places (#1286)

Fixes #1262, fixes #1263 

We now invoke inference for generic method calls in more places,
including when it gets queried from dataflow analysis of a full method.
Where possible, we provide a `TreePath` to the relevant call. With this
`TreePath`, we can reconstruct the assignment context of the call and
use that information when performing inference (see the new
`getInvocationAndContextForInference` method). In some cases, we pass
`null` as the `TreePath` since one is not readily available. I _believe_
that in most / all of these cases, inference should have already been
performed for the call, so we should be able to use the cached result.
If / when we find cases where that didn't happen, and it is impacting
the inference result negatively, we can fix in follow ups.

issue_title: Invalid `@Contract` declaration reported for code that doesn't exist
commit_message:
Accept any annotation with simple name `Contract`, and change reporting of invalid contract annotations (#1295)

Fixes #1222 
Fixes #1215 

We make the following changes to NullAway's handling of `@Contract`
annotations. First, NullAway now treats any annotation with simple name
`Contract` as a contract annotation, not just the JetBrains `@Contract`.
This improves the user experience when using third-party libraries
containing non-Jetbrains `@Contract` annotations on public APIs, as
those annotation types no longer need to be specified as a custom
contract annotation to be picked up by NullAway. (The custom contract
annotation option is still supported, in case someone wants to use an
annotation as a contract that doesn't have simple name `Contract`.)

Second, NullAway now only reports errors for malformed `@Contract`
annotations on the corresponding method declaration, _not_ on calls to
the method. Reporting malformed `@Contract` errors on calls to methods
was a bad behavior, since the method declaration could be in a library
that cannot be easily modified.

It's possible this change will lead to unexpected behavior, if users
were writing non-Jetbrains annotations named `@Contract` and with
similar arguments to `@Contract` but did not want them used by NullAway.
But this seems unlikely, so we go ahead and make this change without an
option to disable it. We can add such an option later if we hear about
any issues.

-->

commit_message:
fix(pipeline): Update isZip method to validate against filename extensions, and keep comic archives zipped (#4741)

# Description of Changes

This pull request updates the logic for detecting and handling zip files
in the `PipelineProcessor` to distinguish between standard zip files and
comic book archive formats (CBZ/CBR). The changes ensure that files with
`.cbz` extensions are not treated as zip files for unzipping purposes.

**Update to zip file detection and extraction:**

* Modified the `isZip` method to take an optional `filename` parameter
and treat files ending with `.cbz` or as non-zip, preventing them from
being unzipped automatically.
* Updated all usages of `isZip` to pass the filename where available,
ensuring the new logic is applied during output file processing and
nested unzipping.

commit_message: feat(compress): add advanced compression parameters and better optimization levels (#4703) # Description of Changes This PR reworks the compression endpoints, to be more consistent and apply better compression on higher levels. Some improvement on lower is also expected. ### Overview: - Added new global flags: --recompress-flate --compress-streams=y --object-streams=generate - Added --decode-level=generalized, so that if the original PDF was poorly compressed then, it can re-compress it better - Added --stream-data=compress for better compression of vector/text parts - Now conditional: --preserve-unreferenced kept only for safe levels ≤3 - Added --optimize-images --jpeg-quality 35–75 depending on level (this brings significant drop in file size, compared to earlier.) - Added QPDF_ZOPFLI for level ≥8 which is better algorithm for compressing JPEG. Comes with approx 5% gain per JPEG on PDFs. See here for details: https://qpdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/cli.html#zopfli-compression-algorithm - level 9, Ghostscript uses strongest downsampling (72/72/150) and CMYK -> RGB ### Images: - Scale factor now ramps 1 -> 9: 0.98, 0.95, 0.88, 0.78, 0.68, 0.58, 0.48, 0.38, 0.28. - JPEG quality ramps 1 -> 9: 0.92, 0.88, 0.85, 0.80, 0.72, 0.65, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35. ### Results: Sample files used: [image-doc.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22984417/image-doc.pdf) [lorem-ipsum.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22984418/lorem-ipsum.pdf) [Create Microsoft Word Document Templates.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22984419/Create.Microsoft.Word.Document.Templates.pdf) [sample-1.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22984420/sample-1.pdf) ### But is it better than the old? (On level 9) #### Old vs new: - image-doc: 1.0 MB vs 454 KB - create-word: 426 KB vs 247 KB - lorem-ipsum: 44.7 KB vs 44.4 Most of changes are focused on images, so more images = better gains. Even on lorem-ipsum text PDF (with no images) there still some gains but not significant. commit_message:
ci: fix Swagger docs generation by targeting stirling-pdf module (#3935)

# Description of Changes

**What was changed**

- Updated the GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/swagger.yml`)
to invoke the `:stirling-pdf:generateOpenApiDocs` task instead of the
root `generateOpenApiDocs`. Refactored `build.gradle` to apply the
`org.springdoc.openapi-gradle-plugin` exclusively to the `stirling-pdf`
subproject, configured its `openApi` extension, and introduced new
Gradle tasks—`copySwaggerDoc` and `cleanSwaggerInBuild`—to manage the
generated `SwaggerDoc.json` file correctly.

**Why the change was made**

- The previous configuration failed to generate OpenAPI documentation
for the `stirling-pdf` module. These changes ensure that Swagger
documentation is produced from the correct module, uploaded to
SwaggerHub as intended, and that temporary artifacts are cleaned up to
maintain a tidy build directory.

Multi tool select buttons bug (#3404)

# Description of Changes

Changes:
- In the multitool page, the behavior of the "Select/Deselect All"
buttons was changed so that if no pages are selected, then the "Deselect
All" button is disabled, and if all pages are selected, then the "Select
All" button is disabled.
- These buttons will also appear if the "Page Select" is turned on,
either by pressing the "Page Select" button or manually selecting one
page.
- Furthermore, a bug that caused the pages to remain selected when "Page
Select" is off was also fixed

Why the changes were made:
- The multitool did not allow the "Select All" or "Deselect All" button
to appear simultaneously. The multitool was relying on a toggle mechanic
for the Page Selection and this could prevent the user from selecting or
deselecting all pages as intended, if they manually select/deselect one
or more pages.

commit_message:
Fix: Context Path Handling and Static Asset Loading Improvements (#3198)

# Description of Changes

### Summary
This PR improves how Stirling-PDF handles the `context-path`
configuration in both backend and frontend components. It ensures proper
URL generation when a custom `context-path` is set in the application
properties. Additionally, it fixes static asset loading issues related
to relative paths.

### Changes Implemented:
- **Backend Enhancements:**
- Introduced `contextPathStatic` as a static variable in
`SPDFApplication.java` to store the configured
`server.servlet.context-path`.
- Modified log outputs and UI initialization URLs to include
`contextPathStatic`.
- Registered `contextPath` as a Spring Bean in `AppConfig.java` to make
it accessible in templates.

- **Frontend Fixes:**
- Updated JavaScript files (`downloader.js`, `home.js`) to dynamically
retrieve and use `contextPath`.
- Adjusted Thymeleaf template files (`navbar.html`, `home.html`,
`merge-pdfs.html`) to reference `contextPath` correctly.
- Fixed incorrect static file paths (`pdf.worker.mjs`, `pdf.mjs`) by
replacing absolute paths (`/`) with relative ones (`./`).

### Why These Changes?
- Fixes issues where deployments under subpaths (e.g.,
`example.com/stirling-pdf/`) resulted in incorrect asset and navigation
links.
- Ensures compatibility with different deployment configurations where
`context-path` is not `/`.

### Challenges Encountered
- Ensuring all JavaScript and template references were correctly updated
to use `contextPath` dynamically.
- Maintaining backward compatibility for deployments that use `/` as the
context path.

Closes #3193 #3181

Normalize File Path for Font Resource Loading (#3179)

# Description of Changes

Please provide a summary of the changes, including:

- Added logic to normalize file paths when retrieving font resources.
- Ensured that file paths starting with `file:` are properly sanitized
and formatted to prevent inconsistencies.
- Replaced `\*` and `/*` in the path to ensure proper pattern matching.
- Used `Paths.get(rawPath).normalize()` to avoid potential path
traversal issues.
- Updated `locationPattern` to ensure it uses a consistent format across
different operating systems.

This change improves reliability in loading fonts from local file paths
and prevents potential errors related to improperly formatted paths.

Closes #3178

commit_message:
PDF-A conversion removes highlight opacity fix (#3106)  (#3695)

# Description of Changes

Previously, highlight annotations in PDF documents converted to PDF/A
format lost their opacity, resulting in highlights appearing completely
opaque.
This issue stemmed from LibreOffice’s PDF to PDF/A conversion process
and affected both supported PDF/A variants (PDF/A-1B and PDF/A-2B). To
resolve this, a new conversion method was implemented.
Because PDF/A-1B does not support transparency, unlike PDF/A-2B, the
input PDF must be preprocessed to flatten existing transparent objects
when targeting PDF/A-1B.

Changes:
- Preprocess the PDF to handle highlight transparency when converting to
PDF/A-1B;
- LibreOffice's PDF to PDF/A conversion is now only used if fonts are
not embedded or images require flattening;
- If needed, missing fonts and flattened images are imported from the
LibreOffice-converted file;
- The document is traversed to remove elements non-compliant with PDF/A
standards;
- Updated metadata, including all metadata schemes, to ensure full
compliance;
- Added an ICC Profile if one was not already present.

Any challenges encountered:
- Since PDF/A-1B does not support transparency, the best workaround I
found in other conversion tools was to draw close diagonal lines with
the highlight color to simulate transparency, as seem in the example
below.

Closes #3106

issue_title: [BUG] ConvexHull Hashset loss of order
issue_body:
### Description

Problem Statement:
The original ConvexHull code uses a HashSet to collect hull points in the recursive method. While this correctly computes which points belong to the convex hull, it does not preserve any order of the points. Many downstream geometric algorithms, such as Rotating Calipers, require the points of the convex hull to be in counter-clockwise (CCW) order around the polygon. Feeding an unordered hull into such algorithms leads to incorrect results, e.g., incorrect minimum bounding rectangle areas or diameters.

Impact:

Algorithms like Rotating Calipers fail or return wrong values.
Tests that check for specific point ordering fail (ConvexHullTest, RotatingCalipersTest).
Geometric computations relying on consistent traversal around the hull cannot be trusted.

Solution:
Preserve the hull points in a list in CCW order.
Start from a well-defined point, e.g., the bottom-most, left-most point, to make results deterministic.
Remove duplicate points caused by set usage.

I’ve identified the issue with ConvexHull returning unordered points, which breaks downstream algorithms like Rotating Calipers. I’ve prepared a fix that preserves counter-clockwise order. Could I be assigned to submit a PR for this?

### Steps to reproduce


Use the original ConvexHull.convexHullRecursive(List<Point>) method on a set of points that form a convex polygon, for example:

List<Point> points = Arrays.asList(
    new Point(0, 3),
    new Point(2, 2),
    new Point(1, 1),
    new Point(2, 1),
    new Point(3, 0),
    new Point(0, 0),
    new Point(3, 3),
    new Point(2, -1),
    new Point(2, -4),
    new Point(1, -3)
);
List<Point> hull = ConvexHull.convexHullRecursive(points);


Print or inspect hull. You will notice the points are unordered (not CCW).

Pass this hull to an algorithm that relies on ordered vertices, e.g., RotatingCalipers.minBoundingRectangle(hull):

double area = RotatingCalipers.minBoundingRectangle(hull);

Observe that the returned area is incorrect (e.g., for a diamond shape it returns 1.9999… instead of 4.0).


### Excepted behavior

convexHullRecursive should return points in CCW order.

Downstream algorithms like Rotating Calipers should produce correct geometric results.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

issue_title: [BUG] MiniMaxAlgorithm.java file
issue_body: ### Description Found multiple bugs in `MiniMaxAlgorithm.java` that need to be fixed: ### Bugs Identified: 1. **Critical Logic Error in `setScores` method**: - Line 114: `scores.length % 1 == 0` always returns true - Should check if length is a power of 2: `(scores.length & (scores.length - 1)) == 0` 2. **Edge Case Handling in `log2` method**: - Doesn't handle edge cases like n=0, negative numbers - Can cause infinite recursion or incorrect results 3. **Missing Test Coverage**: - No test file exists for this algorithm - Need comprehensive unit tests to prevent regressions ### Proposed Solution: - Fix the power-of-2 validation logic - Add proper edge case handling in log2 method - Create comprehensive test suite covering all methods and edge cases - Add input validation for boundary conditions I'd like to work on this issue for Hacktoberfest 2025. ### Excepted behavior 1. **`setScores` method should correctly validate power-of-2 arrays**: - Should accept arrays with lengths that are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, etc.) - Should reject arrays with lengths that are NOT powers of 2 (3, 5, 6, 7, 9, etc.) - Should properly update the internal scores and height when valid input is provided 2. **`log2` method should handle all inputs safely**: - Should correctly calculate log base 2 for valid power-of-2 inputs - Should throw meaningful exceptions for invalid inputs (zero, negative numbers, non-power-of-2) - Should not cause infinite recursion or stack overflow 3. **Algorithm should have comprehensive test coverage**: - All public methods should be tested - Edge cases and error conditions should be covered - Tests should verify the minimax algorithm logic works correctly - Tests should prevent future regressions ### Screenshots

issue_body: ### Description Found multiple bugs in `MiniMaxAlgorithm.java` that need to be fixed: ### Bugs Identified: 1. **Critical Logic Error in `setScores` method**: - Line 114: `scores.length % 1 == 0` always returns true - Should check if length is a power of 2: `(scores.length & (scores.length - 1)) == 0` 2. **Edge Case Handling in `log2` method**: - Doesn't handle edge cases like n=0, negative numbers - Can cause infinite recursion or incorrect results 3. **Missing Test Coverage**: - No test file exists for this algorithm - Need comprehensive unit tests to prevent regressions ### Proposed Solution: - Fix the power-of-2 validation logic - Add proper edge case handling in log2 method - Create comprehensive test suite covering all methods and edge cases - Add input validation for boundary conditions I'd like to work on this issue for Hacktoberfest 2025. ### Excepted behavior 1. **`setScores` method should correctly validate power-of-2 arrays**: - Should accept arrays with lengths that are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, etc.) - Should reject arrays with lengths that are NOT powers of 2 (3, 5, 6, 7, 9, etc.) - Should properly update the internal scores and height when valid input is provided 2. **`log2` method should handle all inputs safely**: - Should correctly calculate log base 2 for valid power-of-2 inputs - Should throw meaningful exceptions for invalid inputs (zero, negative numbers, non-power-of-2) - Should not cause infinite recursion or stack overflow 3. **Algorithm should have comprehensive test coverage**: - All public methods should be tested - Edge cases and error conditions should be covered - Tests should verify the minimax algorithm logic works correctly - Tests should prevent future regressions ### Screenshots
