issue_title: Potential issue with generic BucketSort implementation
issue_body: ### Description Hello, I have some questions about the `hash` method in the `BucketSort` class and would like to discuss it with you. It seems that the logic of the `hash` method is designed for numeric types (such as `Integer`), but it is currently a generic method. The return value of `compareTo` is an ordinal, not a magnitude that can be used for calculating proportions. For example, for the numbers 10 and 30, the range we need is 20, but `30.compareTo(10)` returns 1 (for numeric types, the `compareTo` method only returns -1, 0, or 1). This means that for any non-numeric `Comparable` type (such as `String`), or even for numeric types themselves, the current bucketing strategy does not work properly (although the sorting result appears to be correct). Moreover, when all elements are equal, the `range` variable is 0, which will cause a division-by-zero exception. Although Java converts NaN to 0 instead of throwing an exception, this seems to be a logical error as well. ```java private > int hash(final T element, final T min, final T max, final int numberOfBuckets) { double range = max.compareTo(min); double normalizedValue = element.compareTo(min) / range; return (int) (normalizedValue * (numberOfBuckets - 1)); } ``` ### Steps to reproduce For example, when all the elements in the array are 1, the above logic will incorrectly place all the elements into the bucket with index 0. When the array elements are not identical, the above logic will incorrectly place the elements into only two buckets, which is determined solely by the -1, 0, or 1 returned by the `compareTo` method, rather than the correct mapping index. ### Excepted behavior After reviewing some related issues, it seems that the author does not intend to change the generic signature. Therefore, I hope to document the relevant issues in the comments so that future learners can understand the logic. If my wording is inappropriate, please forgive me. I am just a learner. ### Screenshots _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

issue_title: [BUG] Incorrect column pointer initialization in RowColumnWiseSorted2dArrayBinarySearch
issue_body:
### Description

-  I've identified a bug in the `RowColumnWiseSorted2dArrayBinarySearch.java` implementation.
- The column pointer (colPointer) is initialized using `matrix.length - 1`. But, **matrix.length returns the number of rows, not the number of columns**.
- This causes the algorithm's starting point to be incorrect for any matrix that is not square.
- The problematic line is:
```java
// in src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/searches/RowColumnWiseSorted2dArrayBinarySearch.java

int colPointer = matrix.length - 1; // The pointer at end column
```

### Steps to reproduce

- The bug can be reproduced with any non-square matrix where the number of rows and columns are different.
- For example, with a 2x4 matrix:
```java
   1 int[][] matrix = {
   2     {10, 20, 30, 40},
   3     {15, 25, 35, 45}
   4 };
```
- With the current code, matrix.length is 2, so colPointer is initialized to 1.
- The search incorrectly starts at matrix[0][1] (value 20) instead of the top-right corner matrix[0][3] (value 40).

### Excepted behavior

- The colPointer should be initialized to the index of the last column, allowing the search to correctly start at the top-right corner of the matrix. The correct initialization should be:
`int colPointer = matrix[0].length - 1;`

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional context

I would like to submit a Pull Request to fix this initialization issue.

issue_title: [BUG] Incorrect column pointer initialization in RowColumnWiseSorted2dArrayBinarySearch
issue_body:
### Description

-  I've identified a bug in the `RowColumnWiseSorted2dArrayBinarySearch.java` implementation.
- The column pointer (colPointer) is initialized using `matrix.length - 1`. But, **matrix.length returns the number of rows, not the number of columns**.
- This causes the algorithm's starting point to be incorrect for any matrix that is not square.
- The problematic line is:
```java
// in src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/searches/RowColumnWiseSorted2dArrayBinarySearch.java

int colPointer = matrix.length - 1; // The pointer at end column
```

### Steps to reproduce

- The bug can be reproduced with any non-square matrix where the number of rows and columns are different.
- For example, with a 2x4 matrix:
```java
   1 int[][] matrix = {
   2     {10, 20, 30, 40},
   3     {15, 25, 35, 45}
   4 };
```
- With the current code, matrix.length is 2, so colPointer is initialized to 1.
- The search incorrectly starts at matrix[0][1] (value 20) instead of the top-right corner matrix[0][3] (value 40).

### Excepted behavior

- The colPointer should be initialized to the index of the last column, allowing the search to correctly start at the top-right corner of the matrix. The correct initialization should be:
`int colPointer = matrix[0].length - 1;`

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional context

I would like to submit a Pull Request to fix this initialization issue.

### Issue details

When generating the CFG using the `--cfg` flag the line endings for the instructions are missing the backslash in front of them and therefore result in a broken graph.

```
...
Node_5 [shape=record,label="{5\:\ 0x0023|lr3.f.addTag(42)landroid.content.Intent r0 = (android.content.Intent) r0.getParcelableExtra(\"nextIntent\")lr3.nextIntent = r0l}"];

Node_5 [shape=record,label="{5\:\ 0x0023|r3.f.addTag(42)\landroid.content.Intent r0 = (android.content.Intent) r0.getParcelableExtra(\"nextIntent\")\lr3.nextIntent = r0\l}"];
```
This is caused by an incorrect usage of `String.replaceAll()` in `DotGraphVisitor.java`. The replacement string containing a backslash will cause problems.

issue_title: [core] JADX minimum JRE version requirement vs. `--enable-native-access` JVM option in "bin/jadx" script
issue_body:
### Issue details

Hi!

Both 1.5.2 and the current master branch have the following in the README for minimum JRE version for JADX:
> Note: ensure you have installed Java 11 or later 64-bit version.

Also the contribution guide (CONTRIBUTING.md) says this:
> Pull Request Process
> (...)
> 2. Use only features and API from Java 11 or below.

However the [downloadable 1.5.2 bundle](https://github.com/skylot/jadx/releases/download/v1.5.2/jadx-1.5.2.zip) contains the following in `bin/jadx`:
```
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='"-Xms256M" "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=70.0" "-Djdk.util.zip.disableZip64ExtraFieldValidation=true" "--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED"'
```

The `--enable-native-access` option was introduced in Java 17 and is supported by the various JVMs starting with this version.

Using e.g. OpenJDK v11 (on Ubuntu 22.04.5) causes the following error while running JADX 1.5.2:
```
$ java -version
openjdk version "11.0.27" 2025-04-15
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 11.0.27+6-post-Ubuntu-0ubuntu122.04)

Unrecognized option: --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED
Error: Could not create the Java Virtual Machine.
Error: A fatal exception has occurred. Program will exit.
```

Removing the `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` option from the script's DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS variable allows me to run JADX 1.5.2 with OpenJDK 11.

On the master branch this JVM option seems to be referenced in these files:
- [jadx-cli/build.gradle.kts](https://github.com/skylot/jadx/blob/master/jadx-cli/build.gradle.kts)
- [jadx-gui/build.gradle.kts](https://github.com/skylot/jadx/blob/master/jadx-gui/build.gradle.kts)
- [.run/jadx-gui.run.xml](https://github.com/skylot/jadx/blob/master/.run/jadx-gui.run.xml)

The two build.gradle.kts files have this comment before the JVM option:
> // Foreign API access for 'directories' library (Windows only)

It seems that this JVM option is applied regardless of the platform (as I'm using Ubuntu). I don't have a Mac, but looking at the downloaded bundle I'd say it'll work the same way on that platform too.

1.5.2

issue_title: [core] Incorrect Hexadecimal Representation for Negative Byte values
issue_body:
### Issue details

When the integer display format is set to hexadecimal (via Preferences > Decompilation > Integer Format), jadx displays negative integers in following format (e.g., 0xffff..d8). This is probably due to byte values are stored in long variable.

Please see the attached screenshot for an example:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/887d27cc-07ea-4649-b887-816d85b0deac)

Ideally, negative integers should be represented in their standard two's complement hexadecimal form.


In my experience, when working with byte arrays, I often encounter situations where negative numbers within the array, as well as Byte.MIN_VALUE and Byte.MAX_VALUE, need to be specifically handled or "replaced" to correctly interpret or utilize the data (like using the byte array in to python script). Are there any specific reason Byte.MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE used in jadx? I'd rather see raw values instead of them.

### Affected version

0.28.0

### Steps to reproduce the bug

1. install app
2. deny notifiacation permission request
3. Go to settings > notification
4. wait for the snackbar to appear
5. use it to open the android system app's notification settings
6. enable notifications
7. use hardware back button to go back

### Expected behavior

detect the changed permission state and make the settings on the page accessible.

### Actual behavior

the in-app notification settings page does not recognize the changed permission

### Screenshots/Screen recordings

_No response_

### Logs

_No response_

### Affected Android/Custom ROM version

_No response_

### Affected device model

_No response_

### Additional information

Currently, a new intent is launched to open the ANdorid app settings. The current implementation just starts an intent and tries to detect changes in `onResume()` which works if something different than the back button is used. 

Using `registerForActivityResult` might be a solution to this.

issue_title: [YouTube] SRT numbering should start at 1 (currently starts at 0)
issue_body:
### Checklist

- [x] I am able to reproduce the bug with the latest version given here: [CLICK THIS LINK](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/releases/latest).
- [x] I made sure that there are *no existing issues* - [open](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/issues) or [closed](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) - which I could contribute my information to.
- [x] I have read the [FAQ](https://newpipe.net/FAQ/) and my problem isn't listed.
- [x] I have taken the time to fill in all the required details. I understand that the bug report will be dismissed otherwise.
- [x] This issue contains only one bug.
- [x] I have read and understood the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/dev/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

### Affected version

0.28.0 and all earlier versions

### Description

Currently, into YouTube, the downloaded `.srt` subtitle files start numbering at 0. For example:

> 0
> 00:00:00,640 --> 00:00:07,160
> This mother has three young cubs just 8

Although most players (`mpv`, `VLC`, `MPlayer`, `Totem`) can still display them correctly, this is NOT compliant with the `SubRip (.srt) specification`, which requires numbering to start at 1.

Here is the specification: SubRip (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SubRip), and it says:

> Subtitles are numbered sequentially, starting at 1. 

Tested players:
- mpv 0.37.0 ✅ works with 0
- VLC 3.0.20 ✅ works with 0, even -1
- MPlayer 1.5 ✅ works with 0
- Totem 43.0 ✅ works with 0

Even though playback works fine, some stricter software or tools **may reject** these `*.srt` files. So I think it's best to fix it.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Actual behavior

This issue can be reproduced by any downloaded `*.srt` file.
Here is an example of YouTube video link ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q8aPwoe_iMc ), let's look at  the beginning of a `*.SRT` file generated by NewPipe:

> a51x:/storage/emulated/0/Newpipe $ cat Bear\ Family\ Searches\ for\ Water\ _\ Wild\ Mexico\ _\ BBC\ Earth-en.srt               
> 0
> 00:00:00,640 --> 00:00:07,160
> This mother has three young cubs just 8
> 
> 1
> 00:00:03,840 --> 00:00:07,160
> months old.
> 
> 2
> 00:00:08,520 --> 00:00:22,899
> [Music]
> 
> 3
> 00:00:24,560 --> 00:00:29,039
> It's autumn and the family needs to
> 
> 4
> 00:00:27,119 --> 00:00:32,039
> flatten up before the winter
>

commit_message:
[YouTube] *.srt numbering start at 1 instead of 0. (issue: https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/issues/12670)

- The SubRip (.srt) specification requires subtitle numbering to begin from 1.
- Please refer to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SubRip
- Previously numbering started from 0, which is accepted by most
  players (tested on mpv, VLC, MPlayer, Totem) but not strictly compliant.

issue_body:
### Checklist

- [x] I am able to reproduce the bug with the latest version given here: [CLICK THIS LINK](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/releases/latest).
- [x] I made sure that there are *no existing issues* - [open](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/issues) or [closed](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) - which I could contribute my information to.
- [x] I have read the [FAQ](https://newpipe.net/FAQ/) and my problem isn't listed.
- [x] I have taken the time to fill in all the required details. I understand that the bug report will be dismissed otherwise.
- [x] This issue contains only one bug.
- [x] I have read and understood the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/dev/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

### Affected version

0.28.0 and all earlier versions

### Description

Currently, into YouTube, the downloaded `.srt` subtitle files start numbering at 0. For example:

> 0
> 00:00:00,640 --> 00:00:07,160
> This mother has three young cubs just 8

Although most players (`mpv`, `VLC`, `MPlayer`, `Totem`) can still display them correctly, this is NOT compliant with the `SubRip (.srt) specification`, which requires numbering to start at 1.

Here is the specification: SubRip (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SubRip), and it says:

> Subtitles are numbered sequentially, starting at 1. 

Tested players:
- mpv 0.37.0 ✅ works with 0
- VLC 3.0.20 ✅ works with 0, even -1
- MPlayer 1.5 ✅ works with 0
- Totem 43.0 ✅ works with 0

Even though playback works fine, some stricter software or tools **may reject** these `*.srt` files. So I think it's best to fix it.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Actual behavior

This issue can be reproduced by any downloaded `*.srt` file.
Here is an example of YouTube video link ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q8aPwoe_iMc ), let's look at  the beginning of a `*.SRT` file generated by NewPipe:

> a51x:/storage/emulated/0/Newpipe $ cat Bear\ Family\ Searches\ for\ Water\ _\ Wild\ Mexico\ _\ BBC\ Earth-en.srt               
> 0
> 00:00:00,640 --> 00:00:07,160
> This mother has three young cubs just 8
> 
> 1
> 00:00:03,840 --> 00:00:07,160
> months old.
> 
> 2
> 00:00:08,520 --> 00:00:22,899
> [Music]
> 
> 3
> 00:00:24,560 --> 00:00:29,039
> It's autumn and the family needs to
> 
> 4
> 00:00:27,119 --> 00:00:32,039
> flatten up before the winter
>

For example: + * + * "&" → "&" + * "<" → "<" + * ">" → ">" + * " " → "\t" (TAB) + * " " ( ) → "\n" (LINE FEED) + * + * XML files cannot contain characters like "<", ">", "&" directly, + * so they must be represented using their entity-encoded forms. + * + * Jsoup sometimes leaves nested or encoded entities unresolved + * (e.g. inside

text nodes in TTML files), so this function + * acts as a final “safety net” to ensure all entities are decoded + * before further normalization. + * + * Character representation layers for reference: + * - Literal characters: <, >, & + * → appear in runtime/output text (e.g. final SRT output) + * - Escaped entities: <, >, & + * → appear in XML/HTML/TTML source files + * - Numeric entities:  , , + * → appear mainly in XML/TTML files (also valid in HTML) + * for non-printable or special characters + * - Unicode escapes: \u00A0 (Java/Unicode internal form) + * → appear only in Java source code (NOT valid in XML) + * + * XML entities include both named (&, <) and numeric + * ( ,  ) forms. + * + * @param encodedEntities The raw text fragment possibly containing + * encoded XML entities. + * @return A decoded string where all entities are replaced by their + * actual (literal) characters. + */ + private String decodeXmlEntities(final String encodedEntities) { + return Parser.unescapeEntities(encodedEntities, true); + } + + /** + * Handle rare XML entity characters like LF: (`\n`), + * CR: (`\r`) and CRLF: (`\r\n`). + * + * These are technically valid in TTML (XML allows them) + * but unusual in practice, since most TTML line breaks + * are represented as
tags instead. + * As a defensive approach, we normalize them: + * + * - Windows (\r\n), macOS (\r), and Unix (\n) → unified SRT NEW_LINE (\r\n) + * + * Although well-formed TTML normally encodes line breaks + * as
tags, some auto-generated or malformed TTML files + * may embed literal newline entities ( , ). This + * normalization ensures these cases render properly in SRT + * players instead of breaking the subtitle structure. + * + * @param text To be normalized text with actual characters. + * @return Unified SRT NEW_LINE converted from all kinds of line breaks. + */ + private String normalizeLineBreakForSrt(final String text) { + String cleaned = text; + + // NOTE: + // The order of newline replacements must NOT change, + // or duplicated line breaks (e.g. \r\n → \n\n) will occur. + cleaned = cleaned.replace("\r\n", "\n") + .replace("\r", "\n"); + + cleaned = cleaned.replace("\n", NEW_LINE); + + return cleaned; + } + + private String normalizeForSrt(final String actualText) { + String cleaned = actualText; + + // Replace NBSP "non-breaking space" (\u00A0) with regular space ' '(\u0020). + // + // Why: + // - Some viewers render NBSP(\u00A0) incorrectly: + // * MPlayer 1.5: shown as “??” + // * Linux command `cat -A`: displayed as control-like markers + // (M-BM-) + // * Acode (Android editor): displayed as visible replacement + // glyphs (red dots) + // - Other viewers show it as a normal space (e.g., VS Code 1.104.0, + // vlc 3.0.20, mpv 0.37.0, Totem 43.0) + // → Mixed rendering creates inconsistency and may confuse users. + // + // Details: + // - YouTube TTML subtitles use both regular spaces (\u0020) + // and non-breaking spaces (\u00A0). + // - SRT subtitles only support regular spaces (\u0020), + // so \u00A0 may cause display issues. + // - \u00A0 and \u0020 are visually identical (i.e., they both + // appear as spaces ' '), but they differ in Unicode encoding, + // and NBSP (\u00A0) renders differently in different viewers. + // - SRT is a plain-text format and does not interpret + // "non-breaking" behavior. + // + // Conclusion: + // - Ensure uniform behavior, so replace it to a regular space + // without "non-breaking" behavior. + // + // References: + // - Unicode U+00A0 NBSP (Latin-1 Supplement): + // https://unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0080.pdf + cleaned = cleaned.replace('\u00A0', ' ') // Non-breaking space + .replace('\u202F', ' ') // Narrow no-break space + .replace('\u205F', ' ') // Medium mathematical space + .replace('\u3000', ' ') // Ideographic space + // \u2000 ~ \u200A are whitespace characters (e.g., + // en space, em space), replaced with regular space (\u0020). + .replaceAll("[\\u2000-\\u200A]", " "); // Whitespace characters + + // \u200B ~ \u200F are a range of non-spacing characters + // (e.g., zero-width space, zero-width non-joiner, etc.), + // which have no effect in *.SRT files and may cause + // display issues. + // These characters are invisible to the human eye, and + // they still exist in the encoding, so they need to be + // removed. + // After removal, the actual content becomes completely + // empty "", meaning there are no characters left, just + // an empty space, which helps avoid formatting issues + // in subtitles. + cleaned = cleaned.replaceAll("[\\u200B-\\u200F]", ""); + + // Reasoning: + // - subtitle files generally don't require tabs for alignment. + // - Tabs can be displayed with varying widths across different + // editors or platforms, which may cause display issues. + // - Replace it with a single space for consistent display + // across different editors or platforms. + cleaned = cleaned.replace('\t', ' '); --- a/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
+++ b/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
@@ -96,11 +96,23 @@
             android:exported="false"

-        <service android:name=".local.subscription.services.SubscriptionsImportService" />

             android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />

         <activity
             android:name=".PanicResponderActivity"
             android:exported="true"

         </activity>

issue_body: 按照文档中的一键改包修改之后打开新项目配置好正常启动，访问swagger文档报错。 ### 基本信息 - ruoyi-vue-pro 版本：[v2025.09] - 操作系统：windows - 数据库：postgresql ### 你猜测可能的原因 （必填）我花费了 2-4 小时自查，发现可能的原因是：自定义的Knife4jOpenApiCustomizer的@Primary没有生效 ### 复现步骤 第一步，一键改包 第二步，打开swagger地址 第三步，idea控制台打印报错信息 ### 报错信息 2025-09-05 15:15:19.690 [http-nio-48080-exec-6] ERROR c.z.a.f.web.core.handler.GlobalExceptionHandler:335 - [defaultExceptionHandler] jakarta.servlet.ServletException: Handler dispatch failed: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.util.List org.springdoc.core.properties.SpringDocConfigProperties.getGroupConfigs()' 访问swagger发现进入的方法是原本的Knife4jOpenApiCustomizer类中的public void customise(OpenAPI openApi)而不是自己重写的，但是项目启动时在自定义的Knife4jOpenApiCustomizer类中构造器打了断点是有进入的。 带上必要的截图

issue_body: 碰到问题，请在 搜索是否存在相似的 issue。 不按照模板提交的 issue，会被系统自动删除。 ### 基本信息 - ruoyi-vue-pro 版本：2.4.1-jdk8-SNAPSHOT - 操作系统：win11 - 数据库：MySQL8 ### 你猜测可能的原因 （必填）我花费了 2-4 小时自查，发现可能的原因是： 这里‘2.1 查询我的首个任务’是获取任务列表中第一个匹配的任务，但当有多个匹配的任务时，返回的任务可能并不是用户想要的任务，用户想要审批的任务可能在任务列表tasks中排序较后。导致不管用户选择审批哪个任务，都返回的是任务列表tasks中排序较前的任务。 ### 复现步骤 第一步， 创建两个任务： 第二步， 都分配给同一用户审批： 第三步， 保存并发布该流程后，发起该流程。 在所属用户的‘待办任务’下可以看到两个任务： 选择办理‘任务2’，跳转的页面确是办理‘任务1’。其实不管选择办理哪个任务，都是跳转办理‘任务1’。 ### 报错信息 无报错。 带上必要的截图

issue_title: 未开启租户时，getTenantByWebsite，/system/tenant/get-by-website验证报错
issue_body:
### 基本信息

- ruoyi-vue-pro 版本：v2.5.0
- 操作系统：windows
- 数据库：sql server

### 你猜测可能的原因

2.5.0版本后端修改了方法
【功能新增】system：增加租户的下拉选择，用于登录界面
```java
public CommonResult<TenantRespVO> getTenantByWebsite(@RequestParam("website") String website)
```

前端没有验证 LoginForm.vue   RegisterForm.vue
```ts
onMounted(() => {

  getTenantByWebsite()
})
```
1. 虽然该接口标记了 `@TenantIgnore` 注解，但过滤器仍然会调用租户验证
2. MyBatis 多租户拦截器在处理 `system_tenant` 表查询时，又触发了租户验证
3. 形成无限递归调用
导致后端递归报错
### 复现步骤

关闭租户选项，登录，然后登出，即有报错提示（大刷login页面也可以）

commit_message:
fix(微信小程序确认收货提醒接口): 修复 #839 - received_time 时间戳单位错误（应为秒）

根据微信小程序接口要求，订单签收时间 received_time 应为秒级时间戳，但现有实现传入了毫秒，导致微信接口返回错误代码 10060029（签收时间不合理）。

新增 LocalDateUtils.toEpochSecond 方法，统一将 LocalDateTime 转换为秒级时间戳，用于接口参数转换。

BREAKING CHANGE: 无

Closes #839

issue_title: Db.use().count("select * from user")出错
issue_body:
现象：
测试用例 cn.hutool.db.DbTest#countTest 失败，生成的SQL如下语法错误
[SQL] -> SELECT
        count(*) 
    from
        () hutool_alias_count_
        
原因：
cn.hutool.db.sql.SqlUtil#removeOuterOrderBy中调用ReUtil.getGroup1，当sql中没有group by语句时，会返回null导致了异常（有group by时不会报错）

解决办法：
public static String removeOuterOrderBy(final String selectSql) {
		// 去除order by 子句
		String sql = ReUtil.getGroup1(PATTERN_ORDER_BY, selectSql);
		return sql == null ? selectSql : sql;
	}
	
修改后SQL结果：
[SQL] -> SELECT
        count(*) 
    from
        (select
            * 
        from
            user) hutool_alias_count_

issue_title: ReflectUtil中缓存无法释放的问题
issue_body:
在 cn.hutool.core.util.ReflectUtil 类中，其内部维护的三个缓存 Map（以 METHODS_CACHE 为例，类型为 WeakConcurrentMap<Class, Method[]>）存在设计层面的引用闭环问题：由于缓存值（Method[]数组）中的Method对象会通过declaringClass属性强引用其声明类（即缓存的key——Class对象），导致 WeakConcurrentMap 对 key 的弱引用机制完全失效。
这种设计缺陷在涉及自定义类加载器动态加载 Class 的场景下（如热部署功能实现）会造成严重影响：当通过 ReflectUtil.getMethod () 方法操作不同版本的动态类时，产生的缓存会长期驻留。即使触发 GC，由于缓存值对 key 的强引用始终存在，这些动态加载的 Class 对象及其对应的元空间内存也无法被回收。若此类操作频繁执行，会导致元空间内存快速膨胀，最终可能引发 OutOfMemoryError，严重影响应用的稳定性和资源利用率。

issue_title: HTTP status code mismatch between server and clients since PR #69 (broken tests)
issue_body:
# Issue: Test Failures from PR #69 Changes to Exception Handling and Status Codes

## Description
PR #69 (commit dc1f57c09) introduced changes to return proper HTTP status codes (404/204) and throw `NotFoundException` for missing resources. However, several tests were not updated to match the new behavior, causing build failures in CI.

## Background
PR #69 made these changes:
- Changed methods to throw `NotFoundException` instead of returning null for missing resources
- Return `204 No Content` for empty poll results instead of `404 Not Found`
- Updated error messages (e.g., "No such task found by" → "Task not found for")

## Failing Tests

### 1. HttpEndToEndTest.testAll() - NPE from batchPoll
**Location:** `test-harness/src/test/java/.../http/AbstractHttpEndToEndTest.java:169`

The `/tasks/poll/batch/{tasktype}` endpoint returns `204 No Content` when no tasks are available, but the HTTP client SDK deserializes this as `null` instead of an empty list.

```java
List<Task> polled = taskClient.batchPollTasksByTaskType("non existing task", "test", 1, 100);
assertNotNull(polled); // FAILS - polled is null
assertEquals(0, polled.size()); // NPE
```

### 2. HttpEndToEndTest.testTaskByTaskId() - Wrong error message
**Location:** `test-harness/src/test/java/.../http/AbstractHttpEndToEndTest.java:451`

Test expects old error message format.

```java
assertEquals("No such task found by taskId: test999", e.getMessage()); // FAILS
// Should be: "Task not found for taskId: test999"
```

### 3. QueueResiliencySpec - Missing NotFoundException expectations
**Location:** `test-harness/src/test/groovy/.../resiliency/QueueResiliencySpec.groovy:515,523`

Tests call `getTaskLogs()` and `getTask()` with non-existent IDs but don't expect the `NotFoundException` that's now thrown.

```groovy
def "Verify getTaskLogs doesn't involve QueueDAO"() {
    when:
    taskResource.getTaskLogs("testTaskId")

    then:
    // FAILS - throws NotFoundException but test doesn't expect it
    0 * queueDAO._
}

def "Verify getTask doesn't involve QueueDAO"() {
    when:
    taskResource.getTask("testTaskId")

    then:
    // FAILS - throws NotFoundException but test doesn't expect it
    0 * queueDAO._
}
```

### 4. TaskResourceTest.testGetTaskLogs() - Wrong return type
**Location:** `rest/src/test/java/.../rest/controllers/TaskResourceTest.java:110`

Method now returns `ResponseEntity<List<TaskExecLog>>` but test expects `List<TaskExecLog>`.

```java
assertEquals(listOfLogs, taskResource.getTaskLogs("123")); // FAILS
// Should be: assertEquals(ResponseEntity.ok(listOfLogs), taskResource.getTaskLogs("123"));
```

## Proposed Fixes

### Quick Fix: Update Tests
Update the 4 failing tests to match the new behavior from PR #69:

1. **TaskResourceTest.testGetTaskLogs()** - Expect `ResponseEntity.ok(listOfLogs)`
2. **AbstractHttpEndToEndTest.testTaskByTaskId()** - Update error message to "Task not found for taskId: test999"
3. **QueueResiliencySpec** (2 tests) - Add `thrown(NotFoundException)` expectations

### Deeper Issue: batchPoll 204 Response
The NPE in test #1 reveals a design issue: returning `204 No Content` for empty poll results breaks HTTP client SDK compatibility.

**Options for batchPoll:**

**Option A: Fix the HTTP Client SDK**
- Update HTTP client to handle 204 by returning empty list instead of null
- **Pros:** Maintains REST semantics
- **Cons:** Requires external SDK changes, affects all SDK users

**Option B: Return 200 + Empty List**
- Change endpoint to return `200 OK` with empty array for no tasks
- **Pros:** Compatible with existing clients, common pattern for list endpoints
- **Cons:** Slightly less semantically pure (though still valid REST)

**Recommendation:** Option B - Return `200 OK` with empty list for polling/collection endpoints. Reserve `204 No Content` for operations with truly no response (DELETE, UPDATE).

## Related
- PR #69: Return 204 instead of 404 for /poll endpoints
- Commit b47d6271a: Fix issue #38
- Issue #38: Return 204 instead of 404 for /poll endpoints handling non-existent tasks

**Location:** `test-harness/src/test/java/.../http/AbstractHttpEndToEndTest.java:169`

The `/tasks/poll/batch/{tasktype}` endpoint returns `204 No Content` when no tasks are available, but the HTTP client SDK deserializes this as `null` instead of an empty list.

```java
List<Task> polled = taskClient.batchPollTasksByTaskType("non existing task", "test", 1, 100);
assertNotNull(polled); // FAILS - polled is null
assertEquals(0, polled.size()); // NPE
```

### 2. HttpEndToEndTest.testTaskByTaskId() - Wrong error message
**Location:** `test-harness/src/test/java/.../http/AbstractHttpEndToEndTest.java:451`

Test expects old error message format.

```java
assertEquals("No such task found by taskId: test999", e.getMessage()); // FAILS
// Should be: "Task not found for taskId: test999"
```

### 3. QueueResiliencySpec - Missing NotFoundException expectations
**Location:** `test-harness/src/test/groovy/.../resiliency/QueueResiliencySpec.groovy:515,523`

Tests call `getTaskLogs()` and `getTask()` with non-existent IDs but don't expect the `NotFoundException` that's now thrown.

```groovy
def "Verify getTaskLogs doesn't involve QueueDAO"() {
    when:
    taskResource.getTaskLogs("testTaskId")

    then:
    // FAILS - throws NotFoundException but test doesn't expect it
    0 * queueDAO._
}

def "Verify getTask doesn't involve QueueDAO"() {
    when:
    taskResource.getTask("testTaskId")

    then:
    // FAILS - throws NotFoundException but test doesn't expect it
    0 * queueDAO._
}
```

### 4. TaskResourceTest.testGetTaskLogs() - Wrong return type
**Location:** `rest/src/test/java/.../rest/controllers/TaskResourceTest.java:110`

Method now returns `ResponseEntity<List<TaskExecLog>>` but test expects `List<TaskExecLog>`.

```java
assertEquals(listOfLogs, taskResource.getTaskLogs("123")); // FAILS
// Should be: assertEquals(ResponseEntity.ok(listOfLogs), taskResource.getTaskLogs("123"));
```

## Proposed Fixes

### Quick Fix: Update Tests
Update the 4 failing tests to match the new behavior from PR #69:

1. **TaskResourceTest.testGetTaskLogs()** - Expect `ResponseEntity.ok(listOfLogs)`
2. **AbstractHttpEndToEndTest.testTaskByTaskId()** - Update error message to "Task not found for taskId: test999"
3. **QueueResiliencySpec** (2 tests) - Add `thrown(NotFoundException)` expectations

### Deeper Issue: batchPoll 204 Response
The NPE in test #1 reveals a design issue: returning `204 No Content` for empty poll results breaks HTTP client SDK compatibility.

**Options for batchPoll:**

**Option A: Fix the HTTP Client SDK**
- Update HTTP client to handle 204 by returning empty list instead of null
- **Pros:** Maintains REST semantics
- **Cons:** Requires external SDK changes, affects all SDK users

**Option B: Return 200 + Empty List**
- Change endpoint to return `200 OK` with empty array for no tasks
- **Pros:** Compatible with existing clients, common pattern for list endpoints
- **Cons:** Slightly less semantically pure (though still valid REST)

**Recommendation:** Option B - Return `200 OK` with empty list for polling/collection endpoints. Reserve `204 No Content` for operations with truly no response (DELETE, UPDATE).

- PR #69: Return 204 instead of 404 for /poll endpoints
- Commit b47d6271a: Fix issue #38
- Issue #38: Return 204 instead of 404 for /poll endpoints handling non-existent tasks

issue_title: After upgrade to conductor oss v3.21.19, the connection to AWS SQS broken
issue_body:
### Describe the bug

Conductor is deployed to k8s with below settings
```
 conductor.default-event-queue.type=sqs
 conductor.event-queues.sqs.enabled=true
 conductor.event-queues.sqs.authorized-accounts={{ .Values.conductorserver.eventqueue.awsaccount }}
```
In k8s pod, below variables are injected to pod as environment variables 
```
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
AWS_REGION
```

Above works fine until I upgrade from v3.21.13 to v3.21.19,  when start up it failed to connect to AWS SQS.

commit_message:
fix: correct permission target format to appId+env+namespace/cluster (#5407)

* fix: correct permission target format to appId+env+namespace/cluster

Fixed the permission target ID format issue where cluster and namespace permissions were created with incorrect parameter order:

- buildClusterTargetId: now generates appId+env+clusterName (was appId+clusterName+env)
- buildNamespaceTargetId: now generates appId+env+namespaceName (was appId+namespaceName+env)
- Fixed initClusterNamespaceRoles parameter order in AppService

This resolves the extra bug mentioned in issue #5392 where default permissions had incorrect format.

* test: add unit tests for permission target ID format fix

- Add tests for buildNamespaceTargetId with and without env parameter
- Add tests for buildClusterTargetId method
- Verify correct parameter order: appId+env+namespaceName/clusterName
- Ensure the bug fix for permission format is properly tested

* docs: update CHANGES.md for permission target format fix

Add entry for PR #5407 to Apollo 2.5.0 changelog documenting the fix
for permission target format issue (appId+env+namespace/cluster order).

* fix: revert buildNamespaceTargetId parameter order to maintain backward compatibility

The previous change to buildNamespaceTargetId parameter order from
appId+namespaceName+env to appId+env+namespaceName would break existing
permission data stored in the database, causing permission checks to fail.

Reverted to original appId+namespaceName+env format to ensure backward
compatibility with existing deployments.

issue_title: [Bug] BanyanDB data node OOMKilled by write trace data with secondary index
issue_body: ### Search before asking - [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues. ### Apache SkyWalking Component BanyanDB (apache/skywalking-banyandb) ### What happened I have created a new BanyanDB cluster with a trace-related index, and I continue to write trace data with small traffic (50 spans per streaming, sleeping for 300 milliseconds per streaming). Seems the BanyanDB data node will OOM-kill. The screenshots below show that the data-node-0 has been OOMKilled at 12:04. Then I have stopped the traffic, and the memory of data-node-1 has been reduced to normal at 12:06. Here is the heap dump result of data-node-0 before OOMKilled: [heap-data-node-0.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22588930/heap-data-node-0.zip) ### What you expected to happen No OOMKill in the data node. ### How to reproduce Keep writing trace data into the BanyanDB cluster. ### Anything else _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a pull request to fix on your own? - [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a pull request on my own! ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://www.apache.org/foundation/policies/conduct)

issue_title: [Bug] Got `STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` when sending metrics to banyanDB liaison node
issue_body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues.


### Apache SkyWalking Component

BanyanDB (apache/skywalking-banyandb)

### What happened

When I stress test to write metrics into the liaison node, I often see this error log in the client. 
```
{"level":"error","module":"MEASURE-CLIENT-0","error":"measure service got an unexpected response: message_id:77693335381003 status:\"STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR\" metadata:{group:\"metricsMinute\" name:\"service_status_code2_minute\"}","time":"2025-09-21T11:30:00Z","message":"failed to receive response from measureService"}
```

There is also have this kind of log in the liaison node: 
```
{"level":"error","module":"SERVER-QUEUE-PUB-LIAISON","err_msg":"code: STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR, msg: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded","code":"STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR","time":"2025-09-21T11:22:00Z","message":"node banyandb-liaison-1.banyandb-liaison-headless.banyandb:18912 returns error"}
```

But there no any error logs in the data node. 

### What you expected to happen

On the client side, there is no error received when sending metrics. 

### How to reproduce

1. Start a banyanDB cluster.
2. Write metrics with an interval(1m). 

### Anything else

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a pull request to fix on your own?

- [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a pull request on my own!

issue_body: ### Search before asking - [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues. ### Apache SkyWalking Component BanyanDB (apache/skywalking-banyandb) ### What happened When writing metric data to Banyandb during stree testing, I observed that the memory usage of one liaison node would continuously spike until it reached 100% utilization, at which point it was terminated by Kubernetes OOMKill. When the memory usage of the liaison node approached 80%, I profiled memory using pprof. Here is the memory flamegraph: Here is the heap pprof file: [pprof.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22401498/pprof.zip) ### What you expected to happen No OOMKill in the liaison node. ### How to reproduce 1. Deploy 2 liaison and 2 data nodes in Kubernetes. 2. commit_message:
8.0.0 release notice (#4855)

* 8.0.0 changes

* Add a missing dot.
patch:
--- a/CHANGES.md
+++ b/CHANGES.md
@@ -2,72 +2,66 @@ Changes by Version
 ==================
 Release Notes.
 
-7.0.0
+8.0.0
 ------------------
 
 #### Project
-* SkyWalking discards the supports of JDK 1.6 and 1.7 on the java agent side. The minimal requirement of JDK is JDK8.
-* Support method performance profile.
-* Provide new E2E test framework.
-* Remove AppVeyor from the CI, use GitHub action only.
-* Provide new plugin test tool.
-* Don't support SkyWalking v5 agent in-wire and out-wire protocol. v6 is required.
+* v3 protocol is added and implemented. All previous releases are incompatible with 8.x releases.
+* Service, Instance, Endpoint register mechanism and inventory storage entities are removed.
+* New GraphQL query protocol is provided, the legacy procotol is still supported(plan to remove at the end of this year).
+* Support Prometheus network protocol. Metrics in Prometheus format could be transferred into SkyWalking.
+* Python agent provided.
+* All inventory caches have been removed.
 
 #### Java Agent
-* Add lazy injection API in the agent core.
-* Support Servlet 2.5 in the Struts plugin.
-* Fix RestTemplate plugin ClassCastException in the Async call.
-* Add Finagle plugin.
-* Add test cases of H2 and struts.
-* Add Armeria 0.98 plugin.
-* Fix ElasticSearch plugin bug.
-* Fix EHCache plugin bug.
-* Fix a potential I/O leak.
-* Support Oracle SID mode.
-* Update Byte-buddy core.
-* Performance tuning: replace AtomicInteger with AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater.
-* Add AVRO plugin.
-* Update to JDK 1.8
-* Optimize the ignore plugin.
-* Enhance the gRPC plugin.
-* Add Kotlin Coroutine plugin.
-* Support HTTP parameter collection in Tomcat and SpringMVC plugin.
-* Add @Tag annotation in the application toolkit.
-* Move Lettuce into the default plugin list.
-* Move Webflux into the default plugin list.
-* Add HttpClient 3.x plugin.
+* Add MariaDB plugin.
+* Vert.x plugin enhancement. More cases are covered.
+* Support v3 extension header.
+* Fix ElasticSearch 5.x plugin TransportClient error.
+* Support Correlation protocol v1.
+* Fix Finagle plugin bug, in processing Noop Span.
+* Make `CommandService` daemon to avoid blocking target application shutting down gracefully.
 
 #### OAP-Backend
-* Support InfluxDB as a new storage option.
-* Add `selector` in the `application.yml`. Make the provider activation more flexible through System ENV.
-* Support sub-topology map query.
-* Support gRPC SSL.
-* Support HTTP protocol for agent.
-* Support Nginx LUA agent.
-* Support skip the instance relationship analysis if some agents doesn't have upstream address, currently for LUA agent.
-* Support metrics entity name in the storage. Optional, default OFF.
-* Merge the HOUR and DAY metrics into MINUTE in the ElasticSearch storage implementation. Reduce the payload for ElasticSearch server.
-* Support change detection mechanism in DCS.
-* Support Daily step in the ElasticSearch storage implementation for low traffic system.
-* Provide profile export tool.
-* Support alarm gRPC hook.
-* Fix PHP language doesn't show up on the instance page.
-* Add more comments in the source codes.
-* Add a new metrics type, multiple linears.
-* Fix thread concurrency issue in the alarm core.
+* Support meter system for Prometheus adoption. In future releases, we will add native meter APIs and MicroMeter(Sleuth) system.
+* Support endpoint grouping.
+* Add **SuperDataSet** annotation for storage entity. 
+* Add **superDatasetIndexShardsFactor** in the ElasticSearch storage, to provide more shards for @SuperDataSet annotated entites. Typically TraceSegment.
+* Support alarm settings for relationship of service, instance, and endpoint level metrics.
+* Support alarm settings for database(conjecture node in tracing scenario).
+* Data Model could be added in the runtime, don't depend on the bootstrap sequence anymore.
+* Reduce the memory cost, due to no inventory caches.
+* No buffer files in tracing and service mesh cases.
+* New ReadWriteSafe cache implementation. Simplify codes.
+* Provide default way for metrics query, even the metrics doesn't exist.
+* New GraphQL query protocol is provided. Support the metrics type query.
+* Set up length rule of service, instance, and endpoint.
+* Adjust the default jks for ElasticSearch to empty.
+* Fix Apdex function integer overflow issue. 
+* Fix profile storage issue.
+* Fix TTL issue.
+* Fix H2 column type bug.
+* Add JRE 8-14 test for the backend. 
 
 #### UI
-* Support custom topology definition.
-
+* UI dashboard is 100% configurable to adopt new metrics definited in the backend.
 
 #### Document
-* Add FAQ about `python2` command required in the compiling.
-* Add doc about new e2e framework.
-* Add doc about the new profile feature.
-* Powered-by page updated.
+* Add v8 upgrade document.
+* Make the coverage accurate including UT and e2e tests.
+* Add miss doc about collecting parameters in the profiled traces.
+
+#### CVE
+* Fix SQL Injection vulnerability in H2/MySQL implementation.
+* Upgrade Nacos to avoid the FastJson CVE in high frequency.
+* Upgrade jasckson-databind to 2.9.10. 
 
-All issues and pull requests are [here](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/milestone/37?closed=1)
 
+All issues and pull requests are [here](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/milestone/45?closed=1)
+
+7.0.0 release
+------------------
+You could find all CHANGES of 7.0.0 at [here](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/blob/v7.0.0/CHANGES.md)
 
 6.x releases
 ------------------

issue_title: [Bug] oom due to skywalking java agent too many span log
issue_body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I had searched in the [issues](https://github.com/apache/skywalking/issues?q=is%3Aissue) and found no similar issues.


### Apache SkyWalking Component

Java Agent (apache/skywalking-java)

### What happened

In my program, there is a xxlJob task that takes a long time to execute. In this task, there is a loop that queries the database and asynchronously sends MQ messages. Due to an MQ exception, the thread pool that asynchronously sends MQ messages experiences message backlog, triggering the rejection strategy of the thread pool. As a result, a large number of tasks that send messages are rejected. At this time, OOM is sent. Upon checking the dump log, I found a large number of Skywalking Log DataEntity and KeyValuePair in it

### What you expected to happen

In the above situation, the problem will not occur

### How to reproduce

1. create an xxlJob task and an asynchronous thread pool (requiring a CountingRejectHandler rejection policy), and start the skywalk thread pool plugin
2. start a long loop in the task
3. submit sleep tasks (sleep (1000)) in an internal loop to trigger rejection policies in the thread pool

commit_message: Remove User Guide links to non-existent Gson website (#2861)
patch:
--- a/UserGuide.md
+++ b/UserGuide.md
@@ -385,8 +385,6 @@ Gson has built-in serializers and deserializers for commonly used classes whose
 
 For many more, see the internal class [`TypeAdapters`](gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/internal/bind/TypeAdapters.java).
 
-You can also find source code for some commonly used classes such as JodaTime at [this page](https://sites.google.com/site/gson/gson-type-adapters-for-common-classes-1).
-
 ### Custom Serialization and Deserialization
 
 Sometimes the default representation is not what you want. This is often the case when dealing with library classes (DateTime, etc.).
@@ -739,7 +737,9 @@ Sometimes you need to share state across custom serializers/deserializers ([see
 
 ### Streaming
 
-In addition Gson's object model and data binding, you can use Gson to read from and write to a [stream](https://sites.google.com/site/gson/streaming). You can also combine streaming and object model access to get the best of both approaches.
+In addition Gson's object model and data binding, you can use Gson to read from and write to a stream with the classes [`JsonReader`](https://javadoc.io/doc/com.google.code.gson/gson/latest/com.google.gson/com/google/gson/stream/JsonReader.html) and [`JsonWriter`](https://javadoc.io/doc/com.google.code.gson/gson/latest/com.google.gson/com/google/gson/stream/JsonWriter.html). These classes operate on a JSON document as a sequence of tokens that are traversed in depth-first order. Because the streams operate on one token at a time, they impose minimal memory overhead.
+
+You can also combine streaming and object model access to get the best of both approaches. For example by starting to manually read a JSON document using a `JsonReader` and then using [`Gson#fromJson(JsonReader, ...)`](https://javadoc.io/doc/com.google.code.gson/gson/latest/com.google.gson/com/google/gson/Gson.html#fromJson(com.google.gson.stream.JsonReader,java.lang.reflect.Type)) to read a nested value, or starting to manually write a JSON document using a `JsonWriter` and then using [`Gson#toJson(..., JsonWriter)`](https://javadoc.io/doc/com.google.code.gson/gson/latest/com.google.gson/com/google/gson/Gson.html#toJson(java.lang.Object,java.lang.reflect.Type,com.google.gson.stream.JsonWriter)) to write a nested value.

issue_title: gson 2.13.0 causes StackOverflowError with Gradle license report plugins
issue_body:
# Gson version
2.13.0

# Java / Android version
Android 14 (API 34)
Android 15 (API 35)

# Used tools
- [ ] Maven; version: 
- [x] Gradle; version: 8
- [ ] ProGuard (attach the configuration file please); version: 
- [x] com.jaredsburrows:gradle-license-plugin:0.9.7
- [x] React Native: 0.75.5

# Description
The latest version of gson (2.13.0), released around April 11, 2025, causes StackOverflowErrors when used with Gradle license report generation tools, specifically with `com.jaredsburrows:gradle-license-plugin:0.9.7`.

## Expected behavior
The license report generation task should complete successfully, as it does with gson 2.12.1 and earlier versions.

## Actual behavior
When the project resolves to gson 2.13.0, the license report generation task fails with a StackOverflowError with no additional error message.

# Reproduction steps
1. Create or use a project that includes the gradle-license-plugin:
```gradle
plugins {
  id "com.jaredsburrows.license" version "0.9.7"
}
```
2. Include a dependency that uses gson 2.13.0 (or a library with wildcard dependency like `com.google.code.gson:gson:+`). In my case this happens with `rollbar-react-native`
3. Configure license report generation:
```gradle
licenseReport {
  generateHtmlReport = false
  generateJsonReport = true
  copyHtmlReportToAssets = false
  copyJsonReportToAssets = true
}
```
4. Run the license report generation task:
```
./gradlew licenseReleaseReport
```

# Exception stack trace
```
FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.

* What went wrong:
Execution failed for task ':app:licenseReleaseReport'.
> java.lang.StackOverflowError (no error message)
```

Additional information:
- The error does not occur when forcing gson 2.12.1 with this workaround:
```gradle
configurations.all {
  resolutionStrategy {
    force 'com.google.code.gson:gson:2.12.1'
  }
}
```
- I discovered this issue in a React Native project using rollbar-react-native, which includes a wildcard dependency on gson, but the issue appears to be with gson 2.13.0 itself.

issue_title: Class name `$Gson$Preconditions` breaks module system when shading
issue_body:
# Gson version
2.12.1

# Java / Android version
JDK 21

# Used tools
<!-- List relevant build tools and plugins with version number here which might affect Gson -->
- [x] Maven 3.9.9
- [x] maven-shade-plugin 3.6.0

# Description
In a downstream project we're trying to shade gson.

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
    <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>3.6.0</version>
    <configuration>
        <shadedArtifactAttached>false</shadedArtifactAttached>
        <artifactSet>
            <includes>
                <include>com.google.code.gson:gson</include>
            </includes>
        </artifactSet>
        <relocations>
            <relocation>
                <pattern>com.google.gson</pattern>
                <shadedPattern>com.nimbusds.jose.shaded.gson</shadedPattern>
            </relocation>
        </relocations>
        <filters>
            <filter>
                <artifact>com.google.code.gson:gson</artifact>
                <excludes>
                    <exclude>**/module-info.class</exclude>
                </excludes>
            </filter>
        </filters>
    </configuration>
    <executions>
        <execution>
            <phase>package</phase>
            <goals>
                <goal>shade</goal>
            </goals>
        </execution>
    </executions>
</plugin>
```

The class in question is correctly moved to `com.nimbusds.jose.shaded.gson.internal.$Gson$Preconditions`. However classes importing this are now broken and incorrectly do this:

```java
import com.nimbusds.jose.shaded.gson.internal..Gson.Preconditions;
```

This leads to all kinds of follow-up bugs when trying to load these classes from the module path. Loading from class path is fine for some reason (I suspect the `com.nimbusds.jose.shaded.gson.internal..` can't be matched by a corresponding `exports` statement in the module-info)

## Expected behavior
relocated classes have a proper name


## Actual behavior
the naming scheme breaks the shade plugin.


# Reproduction steps
1. Build https://bitbucket.org/connect2id/nimbus-jose-jwt/src/10.1/ (`mvn package -DskipTests`)
2. Unpack resulting jar
3. Inspect `com.nimbusds.jose.shaded.gson.GsonBuilder`

# Exception stack trace
N/A

# Clarification / Justification
I'm posting this in support of #1744. I am aware that you could argue this is an issue with the shade plugin. However, since other users reported this as a JLS violation I believe it is up to GSON to fix it.

According to 4efb133 the whole point of this naming scheme is to affect behaviour of some "IDE's auto import functionality". All modern IDEs have been respecting the `module-info.java` for several years now, so this rationale is obsolete, since `com.nimbusds.jose.shaded.gson.internal` is [not exported](https://github.com/google/gson/blob/c6d44259b53a9b2756b5767b843d15e8acacaa31/gson/src/main/java/module-info.java#L22-L27).

Currently the gson release requires in its manifest:

The annotations should only be imported with optional

issue_title: [Regression] Batch execution hangs when Redis master node fails in cluster mode
issue_body:
### Redis version

5.0.5

### Redisson version

3.44.0

### Redisson configuration

**Redisson configuration**

```
Config config = new Config();
config.useClusterServers()
      .addNodeAddress(
          "redis://node1:6379",
          "redis://node2:6379",
          "redis://node3:6379"
      );
// + optional authentication if needed
RedissonClient redisson = Redisson.create(config);
```


**Batch configuration (simplified):**

```
public RBatch createBatch() {
    int retryAttempts = getConfigValue("batch.retry.attempts");
    int retryInterval = getConfigValue("batch.retry.intervals");
    int responseTimeout = getConfigValue("batch.response.timeout");

    return redisson.createBatch(
        BatchOptions.defaults()
            .retryAttempts(retryAttempts)
            .retryInterval(retryInterval, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
            .responseTimeout(responseTimeout, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
    );
}
```


**Batch usage (simplified):**

```
RBatch batch = createBatch();

batch.getBucket(recordKey, codec)
     .setAsync(recordValue);

batch.execute(); // <-- hangs if a master fails


```
**Description:**
We are running Redis in cluster mode with 3 master nodes and 3 slaves.
When one of the master nodes fails (e.g., promoted to slave or replaced by a slave node), batch execution in Redisson hangs indefinitely.

This issue started occurring after upgrading from 3.17.0 → 3.44.0.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

Set up a Redis cluster with 3 masters and 3 slaves.

Run a batch execution using Redisson.

Cause one of the master nodes to fail (kill process or trigger a role change).

Observe that the batch execution hangs.

**Environment:**

- Redisson version: 3.44.0 (previously worked on 3.17.0)
- Redis version: 5.0.5
- Java version: 1.8

**Deployment:** 
Redis cluster (3 masters, 3 slaves)

### What is the Expected behavior?

Batch execution should either retry with the new master or fail fast with an error.

### What is the Actual behavior?

Batch execution hangs indefinitely after master node failure.

Thread Dump (excerpt):

```
sun.misc.Unsafe.park(Native Method)
java.util.concurrent.locks.LockSupport.park(LockSupport.java:175)
java.util.concurrent.CompletableFutures$Signaller.block(CompletableFuture.java:1707)
java.util.concurrent.ForkJoinPool.managedBlock(ForkJoinPool.java:3334)
java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture$Signaller.awaitDone(CompletableFuture.java:1742)
java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture.get(CompletableFuture.java:1908)
org.redisson.command.CommandAsyncService.get(CommandAsyncService.java:176)
org.redisson.command.CommandBatchService.execute(CommandBatchService.java:260)
org.redisson.RedissonBatch.execute(RedissonBatch.java:253)
```

### Additional information

- The issue only appears during cluster failover events.
- The thread remains in WAITING state, holding ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker lock.
- Did not occur in 3.17.0, started happening in 3.44.0.

  # 从节点相关配置（故障转移时使用）
  failedSlaveReconnectionInterval: 3000
  failedSlaveCheckInterval: 60000

# 序列化方式：推荐 Jackson（支持 JSON 和复杂类型）
codec: !org.redisson.codec.JsonJacksonCodec {}

# 线程池大小（Netty 线程和 worker 线程）
nettyThreads: 32
threads: 16

```

### What is the Expected behavior?

Keys such as redisson_lock_queue and redisson_lock_timeout used internally by RedissonFairLock should be processed through the configured NameMapper (e.g., via getLockName() or similar methods) to ensure consistent key naming and proper key prefixing. This ensures that all related keys hash to the same slot in Redis Cluster, avoiding CROSSSLOT errors during multi-key operations.

### What is the Actual behavior?

The internal keys redisson_lock_queue and redisson_lock_timeout are not being passed through the NameMapper. As a result, they do not receive the expected prefix or naming transformation, causing them to be stored with raw, unmapped names. This leads to these keys potentially hashing to different slots in Redis Cluster, which triggers the CROSSSLOT Keys in request do not hash to the same slot error when atomic multi-key operations are executed.

### Additional information

- This issue occurs specifically in Redis Cluster mode when RedissonFairLock performs operations involving multiple internal keys.
- The root cause appears to be that while the main lock key is correctly mapped, auxiliary keys used by the fair lock algorithm (e.g., for queuing and timeout tracking) bypass the NameMapper entirely.
- Other lock types or data structures in Redisson may have similar issues if they rely on multiple related keys without consistently applying NameMapper.
- Users who rely on key prefixes (via Config.setNameMapper()) are most likely to encounter this issue, as the mismatch between prefixed and non-prefixed keys directly leads to cross-slot routing.

issue_title: Redisson Spring Data reactive: XPENDING missing group (syntax error) and NPE on empty pending summary
issue_body:
Hi there! I ran into an XPENDING syntax error and an NPE in reactive streams (details below).

### Environment

- Redisson Version: 3.51.0 (using redisson-spring-boot-starter)
- Spring Boot Version: 3.4.3
- Redis Server Version: 5.0.14
- Previous Setup: Was working fine with `spring-boot-starter-data-redis`

```kotlin
    // build.gradle.kts
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-data-redis")
    implementation ("org.redisson:redisson-spring-boot-starter:3.51.0") {
        exclude("org.redisson", "redisson-spring-data-35")
    }
    implementation("org.redisson:redisson-spring-data-34:3.51.0")
```

After migrating from `spring-boot-starter-data-redis` to `redisson-spring-boot-starter`, 
I'm encountering two critical issues with Redis Stream pending message processing: 
(The same code worked perfectly with the previous Redis client.)


### Issue 1: XPENDING Syntax Error

Getting a syntax error when trying to retrieve pending messages using Range.unbounded<String>():
```
org.springframework.data.redis.RedisSystemException: ERR syntax error. channel: [...]
command: (XPENDING), params: [[98,97,116,99,104,95,116,114,97,110,...], -, +, 1], promise: java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture@b945e3d[Not completed, 1 dependents]
	at org.redisson.spring.data.connection.RedissonBaseReactive.lambda$write$3(RedissonBaseReactive.java:88)
	at reactor.core.publisher.Mono.lambda$onErrorMap$29(Mono.java:3862)
	at reactor.core.publisher.FluxOnErrorResume$ResumeSubscriber.onError(FluxOnErrorResume.java:94)
	at reactor.core.publisher.MonoNext$NextSubscriber.onError(MonoNext.java:93)
	at reactor.core.publisher.FluxCreate$BaseSink.error(FluxCreate.java:479)
```

### Issue 2: NPE When Pending Queue is Empty

When there are no pending messages in the stream, getting NPE exceptions instead of graceful handling.
```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "org.redisson.api.StreamMessageId.toString()" because the return value of "org.redisson.api.PendingResult.getLowestId()" is null
    at org.redisson.spring.data.connection.RedissonReactiveStreamCommands.lambda$xPendingSummary$8(RedissonReactiveStreamCommands.java:125)
    ...
```

### Current Code

```kotlin
@Repository
class BatchJobStreamRepository(
    private val reactiveRedisTemplate: ReactiveRedisTemplate<String, String>,
    private val streamProperties: StreamProperties
) {
    // Issue #1 (XPENDING Syntax Error)
    // pass "Range.unbounded<String>()" as range
    suspend fun getPendingMessages(range: Range<*>, count: Long): List<PendingMessage> {
        return reactiveRedisTemplate
            .opsForStream<String, String>()
            .pending(
                streamProperties.key,
                streamProperties.consumerGroup,
                range,
                count
            )
            .awaitSingleOrNull()
            ?.toList() ?: emptyList()
    }
    
    // Issue #2 (NPE When Pending Queue is Empty)
    suspend fun getPendingMessagesSummary(): PendingMessagesSummary? {
        return reactiveRedisTemplate
            .opsForStream<String, String>()
            .pending(streamProperties.key, streamProperties.consumerGroup)
            ?.awaitSingleOrNull()
    }
    // ... other methods
}
```

### Questions

Is there a different usage required for `pending(...)` with Redisson’s Spring Data reactive adapter?
If not, could this be a bug in `RedissonReactiveStreamCommands` argument building (range path) and null-handling (summary path)?
Any known workarounds (e.g., a specific Range variant, synchronous template path, or direct Redisson RStream API) until a fix?

Any guidance on the correct usage patterns with Redisson would be greatly appreciated!

issue_title: Avoid null warning logs on connection timeout
issue_body:
<!--
Upgrade to Redisson PRO https://redisson.pro with advanced features.
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

While establishing a connection through ClusterConnectionManager (redisson/src/main/java/org/redisson/connection/ClusterConnectionManager.java), a null message is being logged at the warn level.

After investigation, I found that this happens when a connection attempt fails inside the doConnect method. It uses connectionFuture, but the configured timeout was too short, causing an exception to be logged as log.warn(e.getMessage()), which results in a null message.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Although increasing the timeout value mitigates the issue, **I believe the logging could be improved to be more helpful** and informative.

Since connection timeouts can frequently occur, especially during connection initialization, I suggest adding a more descriptive log message when e.getCause() is an instance of ConnectTimeoutException. This would make the log clearer and help users understand the actual cause of the issue.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

The problem was resolved by increasing the timeout value, but that doesn’t improve the developer experience when diagnosing such issues. Clearer logging in timeout scenarios would provide immediate insight and improve usability without requiring deep investigation into the source code.

issue_title: Connections being closed and reopened unexpectedly
issue_body:
### Redis version

valkey 8.0 (elasticache serverless)

### Redisson version

3.45.1

### Redisson configuration

```
      val redisConfig = new Config()
      redisConfig
        .setLazyInitialization(false)
        .useSingleServer()
        .setUsername(...)
        .setPassword(...)
        .setAddress(...)        
        .setConnectionPoolSize(64)
        .setConnectionMinimumIdleSize(64)
        .setRetryAttempts(1)
        .setRetryInterval(50)
        .setTimeout(100)
        .setConnectTimeout(100)
        .setIdleConnectionTimeout(40000)
        .setPingConnectionInterval(30000)
```

### What is the Expected behavior?

Due to min-idle conns and max conns being set to the same value, I expected connections to remain open pretty much indefinitely.

Due to the idle timeout to 40s which is higher than the ping interval, 30s, I expected to remain non-idle.

### What is the Actual behavior?

I see that Redisson periodically closes the connections and opens new ones. (I've discounted the possibility that the server closes the connections - it's the client sending the FIN packets and the server sends back RST/ACK after that - not a clean FIN/ACK but it still shows the client is the one closing.)

Incidentally, and a separate issue actually, Redisson sends QUIT commands when it closes connections. I see that's deprecated since version 7, and that a client should just close, so I wonder if Redisson should try and do that. For us, most of these QUIT commands (98%) timeout. Our timeout settings are quite low but this is still surprising.

issue_title: Direct byte buffer leak when using RLocalCachedMap with StoreMode.LOCALCACHE
issue_body:
### Redis version

7.2.3

### Redisson version

3.50.0

### Redisson configuration

```
singleServerConfig:
  idleConnectionTimeout: 10000
  connectTimeout: 10000
  timeout: 3000
  retryAttempts: 3
  retryInterval: 1500
  password: null
  subscriptionsPerConnection: 5
  clientName: null
  address: "redis://localhost:6379"
  subscriptionConnectionMinimumIdleSize: 1
  subscriptionConnectionPoolSize: 50
  connectionMinimumIdleSize: 24
  connectionPoolSize: 64
  database: 0
  dnsMonitoringInterval: 5000
codec: !<org.redisson.codec.SerializationCodec> { }
useThreadClassLoader: false
transportMode: "NIO"
protocol: RESP3
```

### What is the Expected behavior?

_No response_

### What is the Actual behavior?

I use `RLocalCachedMap` with option `StoreMode.LOCALCACHE`, and every time I call methods `.readAllKeySet()`, `.readAllValues()` or `.readAllEntrySet()` , some amount of netty's direct byte buffers (instances of `PooledUnsafeDirectByteBuf`) leaked (maybe some other methods are also subject to this issue, I didn't check all of them). 

Netty's leak detector also reports this problem, especially if enabled with option `-Dio.netty.leakDetection.level=PARANIOD`.

After some investigations I found a place in code of `RedissonLocalCachedMap.readAllEntrySetAsync()`. There is an accumulation of map keys (their byte buffers) in local collection `List<Object> mapKeys`, and then condition `if (storeMode == LocalCachedMapOptions.StoreMode.LOCALCACHE)` forces fast return, but buffers remain in `mapKeys` non-released, which, when garbage collected, leads to memory leak.

```java
@Override
    public RFuture<Set<Entry<K, V>>> readAllEntrySetAsync() {
        ...
        List<Object> mapKeys = new ArrayList<Object>();
                     ^^^^^^^
        for (CacheValue value : cache.values()) {
            ...
            mapKeys.add(encodeMapKey(value.getKey(), mapKeys));
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^
            ...
        }

        if (storeMode == LocalCachedMapOptions.StoreMode.LOCALCACHE) {
            return new CompletableFutureWrapper<>(result);
            ^^^^^^
        }

        RFuture<Set<Entry<K, V>>> future = readAll(ALL_ENTRIES, mapKeys, result);
        ...
```

On the other side, if cache mode was specified as `StoreMode.LOCALCACHE_REDIS`, that `if`-condition will not kick us out, and then execution will dive inside network interaction with redis, where all passed `ButeBuf`-arguments are properly released.

### Additional information

Minimal code that demonstrates continuously increasing total allocated direct buffers size (example in kotlin, but it's pretty simple to rewrite it in java):

```kotlin
suspend fun main() {
    val redisson = Redisson.create(Config.fromYAML("...")) // mentioned above
    val cache = redisson.getLocalCachedMap(defaultLocalCachedMapOptions<String, String>("TEST"))
    
    println("FILLING CACHE...")

    (1..1000).forEach { cache["key-$it"] = "$it".repeat(10000) }
    println("Buffers = ${getMemoryUsedMegabytes()}")

    println("READING...")

    while (true) {
        cache.readAllValues()
        println("Buffers = ${getMemoryUsedMegabytes()}")
        delay(100)
    }
}

private fun <K, V> defaultLocalCachedMapOptions(name: String): LocalCachedMapOptions<K, V> =
    LocalCachedMapOptions.name<K, V>(name)
        .cacheSize(0).timeToLive(Duration.ZERO).maxIdle(Duration.ZERO)
        .reconnectionStrategy(LocalCachedMapOptions.ReconnectionStrategy.LOAD)
        .syncStrategy(LocalCachedMapOptions.SyncStrategy.UPDATE)
        .cacheProvider(LocalCachedMapOptions.CacheProvider.CAFFEINE)
        .storeMode(LocalCachedMapOptions.StoreMode.LOCALCACHE)
        .expirationEventPolicy(LocalCachedMapOptions.ExpirationEventPolicy.DONT_SUBSCRIBE)

private val bufferPoolMonitor = ManagementFactory.getPlatformMXBeans(BufferPoolMXBean::class.java).first { it.name == "direct" }

private fun getMemoryUsedMegabytes(): String {
    return String.format("%.2f Mb", 1.0 * bufferPoolMonitor.memoryUsed / 1024 / 1024)
}
```

Output:
```
Buffers = 20.00 Mb
Buffers = 20.00 Mb
... (here goes some amount of lines with the same reported size; maybe JVM and/or MBeanServer has some lag, I don't know why it doesn't increase everytime I call readAllValues(), but it increases anyway after some test iterations)
Buffers = 20.00 Mb
Buffers = 24.00 Mb
Buffers = 24.00 Mb
...
Buffers = 24.00 Mb
Buffers = 28.00 Mb
Buffers = 28.00 Mb
Buffers = 28.00 Mb
...
```

issue_title: Update to 3.46 is causing "java.lang.IllegalStateException: This method doesn't work in batch mode."  while using renameAsync
issue_body:
### Redis version

7.1

### Redisson version

3.46

### Redisson configuration

Hello team,

Recently, we updated redisson library from 3.23 to 3.46. And now the code is running into the following exceptions:

```java  
java.lang.IllegalStateException: This method doesn't work in batch mode.
	at org.redisson.RedissonObject.checkNotBatch(RedissonObject.java:313) ~[redisson-3.46.0.jar:3.46.0]
	at org.redisson.RedissonObject.renameAsync(RedissonObject.java:320) ~[redisson-3.46.0.jar:3.46.0]
```

The code which was working earlier is as following:
```java  
RBatch batch = redissonClient.createBatch();
for (String mapName : REDIS_MAP_NAMES) {
	batch.getMap(mapName, compositeCodec).renameAsync(newMapName);
}
```

Here, REDIS_MAP_NAMES contains map names.
Those maps are implementations of `LocalCachedMap<K, V>` .

Based on the code analysis, looks like https://github.com/redisson/redisson/commit/3f63e4b322178013611ef123eba412e44de5fcc0 commit introduced `checkNotBatch()` check for ClusterConfig but Not for other case. So can't see the issue in local environment with single redis node. But, it runs into issues where we have ClusterConfig.

### What is the Expected behavior?

It should be successful. It shouldn't throw exception.

### What is the Actual behavior?

The rename operation fails with the exception.

### Additional information

_No response_

issue_title: Flow triggering multiple times if multiple flow triggers defined
issue_body:
## Describe the issue

For flows that have multiple flow triggers defined, if one of those triggers causes the flow to execute, the flow will be executed the same number of times as the number of triggers defined in the flow. Each triggered execution has the same trigger details.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Define `flow_a` which is executed manually

```yaml
id: flow_a
namespace: dev.general

tasks:
  - id: hello
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.log.Log
    message: Hello World! 🚀
```

2. Define `flow_b` which is executed when `flow_a` completes either successfully or unsuccessfully.

```yaml
id: flow_b
namespace: dev.general

tasks:
  - id: hello
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.log.Log
    message: Hello World! 🚀

triggers:
  - id: on_completion
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.trigger.Flow
    states: [SUCCESS]
    conditions:
      - type: io.kestra.plugin.core.condition.ExecutionFlow
        namespace: dev.general
        flowId: flow_a

  - id: on_failure
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.trigger.Flow
    states: [FAILED]
    conditions:
      - type: io.kestra.plugin.core.condition.ExecutionFlow
        namespace: dev.general
        flowId: flow_a
```

3. Execute `flow_a`, and observe that `flow_b` will be triggered twice, whereby both executions show a trigger id value of `on_completion`.

Please note, I understand the above two triggers can be combined into one for that example, however, it has been split out to illustrate the issue. This same behaviour is exhibited where the trigger conditions are not so easily combined or need to be controlled independently.

## Environment

Kestra Version: `0.24.10`

issue_title: Bug: Blueprints filtering breaks when selecting multiple tags
issue_body: ### Describe the issue **Description** There appears to be an issue with the tag-based filtering logic on the Blueprints page of the Kestra website. When a single tag is selected, the expected set of blueprints is displayed correctly. However, when two or more tags are selected, the results section becomes empty, even though there are blueprints that should match the selected filters. **Steps to Reproduce** Navigate to https://kestra.io/blueprints . Select any single tag (for example, Database). → The page correctly displays matching blueprints. Select an additional tag (for example, Python or SQL). → The displayed results disappear completely. Deselect the additional tag. → The results reappear as expected. **Expected Behavior** When multiple tags are selected, the page should display blueprints that match the selected tags based on the intended filter logic (either intersection or union, depending on design). Currently, the filter seems to eliminate all results, suggesting a possible logical or state-handling issue in the filtering implementation. **Actual Behavior** The results section becomes empty whenever more than one tag is selected, even though each tag individually yields valid results. **Possible Cause** The filtering logic might be using a strict AND condition (requiring blueprints to include all selected tags) or an incorrect combination of predicates that results in an empty array. Alternatively, the UI state may not be updating the filter query correctly when multiple tags are active.**** ### Environment - Kestra Version: develop

issue_title: Paused workflow resumes on Killing
issue_body:
### Describe the issue

Suppose a workflow execution is `paused` Now if we kill that execution using `/api/v1/main/executions/{executionId}/kill` api then workflow is resumed and starts execution from next task.
Example flow:
```
id: pause_five_minutes_flow
namespace: company.team

tasks:
  - id: hello
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.log.Log
    message: Hello World! 🚀

  
  # Wait for only five minutes
  - id: wait_five_minutes
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.Pause
    behavior: CANCEL
    onResume:
      - id: metadata
        type: JSON
      
      - id: review
        type: BOOL
        required: true
        defaults: true

  # Wait for a day
  # If user fails to provide review in specific time 
  # continue do not wait infinitely
  - id: wait_a_day
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.Pause
    pauseDuration: PT5M
    behavior: RESUME
    onResume:
      - id: metadata
        type: JSON
      
      - id: review
        type: BOOL
        required: true
        defaults: true

  # Wait till user gives its input but due date is 5 days
  - id: wait_till_review_with_duedate
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.flow.Pause
    behavior: RESUME
    onResume:
      - id: metadata
        type: JSON
      
      - id: review
        type: BOOL
        required: true
        defaults: true
```


### Environment

- Kestra Version: v1.0.2

issue_title: Kubernetes task runner causes webserver and executor crashes
issue_body:
### Describe the issue

Flows using the Kubernetes task runner crash the webserver and executor with serialization/deserialization errors.

- **Webserver**: Returns HTTP 500 errors when loading flow lists or opening the flow editor
- **Executor**: Enters CrashLoopBackOff and continuously restarts when processing executions

Here is a flow example:
```
id: quelea_920469
namespace: dev.yvrng

tasks:
  - id: exec
    type: io.kestra.plugin.scripts.python.Commands
    taskRunner: 
      type: io.kestra.plugin.ee.kubernetes.runner.Kubernetes
    commands:
      - python --version
```

issue_body:

When viewing execution's output, if you scroll down on the 1st scrollbar to the bottom then scroll on the sidebar to the bottom, the code snippets overlay the main UI

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d0398b8-28e5-4a83-b5f1-c264f0dc4e59

- Kestra Version: develop

issue_title: FlowId is not highlighted as a link
issue_body: ### Describe the issue In the Flow tab, flowId isn't highlighted as a link, but it's still a link. I think it would be helpful to have a more prominent ID so the user understands it's a link. This is similar to what was done in issue #11682. #### In light mode: #### In dark mode: #### Conclusion: I'm participating in HacktoberFest and I'm willing to work on this issue, if it really adds something to the project. ### Environment - Kestra Version: 1.0.7

issue_title: [Native Image] Localized data/time data not working in native image
issue_body:
### Describe the Issue

Given this sample:

```java
final var ARABIC_GREGORIAN_DATE_FORMATTER = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("EEEE dd\\MM\\yyyy G").localizedBy(Locale.forLanguageTag("ar"));
final var ENGLISH_GREGORIAN_DATE_FORMATTER = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("EEEE dd/MM/yyyy G").localizedBy(Locale.ENGLISH);

var now = Instant.now();
String arabicGregorianDate = ARABIC_GREGORIAN_DATE_FORMATTER.format(now.atZone(ZoneId.systemDefault()));
String englishGregorianDate = ENGLISH_GREGORIAN_DATE_FORMATTER.format(now.atZone(ZoneId.systemDefault()));

Log.info("arabicGregorianDate = " + arabicGregorianDate);
Log.info("englishGregorianDate = " + englishGregorianDate);
```

When running in JVM mode, I get this output:

```
arabicGregorianDate = السبت 18\10\2025 م
englishGregorianDate = Saturday 18/10/2025 AD
```

However, when I compile it to GraalVM native-image and run it, I get this output:

```
arabicGregorianDate = Sat 18\10\2025 CE
englishGregorianDate = Saturday 18/10/2025 AD
```

Notice that Arabic word for Saturday `السبت` is fallbacked to `Sat` and `م` to `CE`?

I am using `-H:IncludeLocales=ar,en` as well.

issue_title: [Native Image] Generated .exe file exports way more symbols in GraalVM 25 - compared to GraalVM 24
issue_body: ### Describe the Issue [Enso](http://github.com/enso-org/enso) is using so called _"dual JVM mode"_. A _native image_ process uses `LoadLibraryA` to dynamically load HotSpot JVM. This used to work in `graalvm-community-openjdk-24.0.1+9.1` on Linux, Macs, Windows. It is broken on Windows since `graalvm-community-openjdk-25+15.1` (it still works on Linux and Macs). Analysis has revealed - the [problem is in the linking process](https://github.com/JaroslavTulach/LaunchJdkViaJni/pull/4#issuecomment-3408909860). - there is [too many /EXPORTS](https://github.com/oracle/graal/issues/12384#issuecomment-3416135334) in GraalVM 25 version! E.g. the cause is known. However it is not clear what commit has changed the behavior and how to mitigate that. ### Using the latest version of GraalVM can resolve many issues. - [x] I tried with the [latest version](https://www.graalvm.org/downloads/) of GraalVM. ### GraalVM Version The behavior is on Windows since `graalvm-community-openjdk-25+15.1`. Previous version `graalvm-community-openjdk-24.0.1+9.1` used to work fine. ### Operating System and Version Windows 11 ### Troubleshooting Confirmation - [x] I tried the suggestions in the [troubleshooting guide](https://www.graalvm.org/latest/reference-manual/native-image/guides/troubleshoot-run-time-errors/). ### Run Command I have prepared a sample project [pull request demonstrating the failure](https://github.com/JaroslavTulach/LaunchJdkViaJni/pull/4). issue_title: [Native Image] 控制台程序中文乱码
issue_body:
### Describe the Issue

操作系统为Windows 11 家庭中文版24H2
代码源文件保存为UTF-8
在cmd中使用graalvm中的java.exe直接执行源文件中文显示正常，使用graalvm中javac.exe编译源文件再通过java.exe运行编译之后的class文件中文显示正常
使用native-image.cmd编译生成exe，执行exe则中文显示乱码

### Using the latest version of GraalVM can resolve many issues.

- [ ] I tried with the [latest version](https://www.graalvm.org/downloads/) of GraalVM.

java version "25" 2025-09-16 LTS
Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment Oracle GraalVM 25+37.1 (build 25+37-LTS-jvmci-b01)

Windows 11 家庭中文版24H2

native-image.cmd -Ob

执行生成的exe应该与java.exe直接执行源代码显示结果一致

生成的exe中文显示乱码，需要额外切换控制台字符集chcp 65001,且在win7下切换字符集也是乱码

1、代码源文件包含中文字符串保存文件为UTF-8
2、在cmd中使用graalvm中的java.exe直接执行源文件中文显示正常，使用graalvm中javac.exe编译源文件再通过java.exe运行编译之后的class文件中文显示正常
